What Happens to the Second Amendment if Democrats Pack the Court? | | | Nov 2 | | | | | | | | | | | | On the October 24, 2026 edition of Fox's Ingraham Angle -- ten days before the midterms -- Laura Ingraham put the hypothetical to Mike Davis: founder and president of the Article III Project, former chief counsel for nominations to the Senate Judiciary Committee's Republicans, a clerk for Neil Gorsuch. What happens to the Second Amendment if Democrats pack the Supreme Court? Davis needed three words: "It would be gone." Then he said the rest: they would take away our God-given right to keep and bear arms, and they would claim the Second Amendment covers only the National Guard. Hyperbole? Only if you don't know the math or the history. Both cut his way. The math behind "gone." District of Columbia v. Heller (2008) recognized an individual right to keep a handgun at home, 5-4\. The Court described the right as pre-existing -- the amendment protects a right it did not create, the same Creator-endowed logic as the Declaration -- which is why Davis says God-given. But it was close. Four dissents argued the right belongs to the militias -- the "organized militia" the federal government reorganized as the National Guard by the Militia Act of 1903 and the National Defense Act of 1916. Justice John Paul Stevens wrote that dissent, and in March 2018 he published a New York Times op-ed titled, without euphemism, "Repeal the Second Amendment." McDonald (2010) applied the right to the states, 5-4\. Bruen (2022) extended it outside the home, 6-3. The anti-Heller bloc currently numbers three -- the Court's three Democratic appointees. Add four seats and it is seven to six. Heller, McDonald, and Bruen flip in a single term; D.C.-style handgun bans are constitutional again; the militia reading becomes the law of the land. Hillary Clinton herself once called D.C.'s ban "reasonable" -- a polite way of dissenting from Heller. That is what "gone" means: not a repeal passed by Congress and ratified by thirty-eight states, but seven justices declaring that the words mean what the dissidents always said they meant -- Guard service and a permission slip. Repealing the text is impossible. Repainting its meaning takes a majority of both chambers and a willing president. The thirteen-circuits excuse. Days before the segment, on a podcast, Clinton supplied the justification the packing push had been missing: "You know, it used to be that you'd have one justice for each circuit. We now have 13 circuits, we should have 13 justices." Add her headline caveat -- "we should seriously look at expanding the court while the Democrats are in power" -- and note that Elizabeth Warren backs the idea, while Jim Clyburn said on Meet the Press that "we ought to expand." Davis destroyed this in about thirty seconds, and the historical record supports every syllable. There have been nine justices since 1869. Yes, for most of the Court's first century the justices rode circuit -- and while they did, Congress did grow the bench alongside the circuits: six justices and three circuits in 1789; a seventh of each in 1807; the eighth and ninth in 1837; a tenth circuit in 1863. But in 1891 Congress created the Courts of Appeals so the justices would not have to ride, and by 1911 circuit-riding was formally abolished. The workload rationale died with it. Then comes the proof. Congress kept adding circuits and never added a justice. The Tenth Circuit was created in 1929 -- the bench stayed at nine. The Federal Circuit in 1982 -- nine. Of today's thirteen circuits, two (the D.C. Circuit and the Federal Circuit) aren't geographic circuits at all. One justice per circuit was never a constitutional rule or a statute; it was a workload arrangement from the horseback era that ended 135 years ago. Clinton was quoting an administrative convenience of 1837 as if it were a principle of 2026. The circuits are geography. The bench is not. The question that ends the debate. If the court truly needs thirteen -- if it's arithmetic about circuits -- why is no Democrat demanding thirteen right now, with a Republican president and a Republican Senate? Because the demand follows power, not principle. The last time Democrats held the House, the Senate, and the White House with a 6-3 court, Senator Ed Markey and Representative Hank Johnson introduced the Judiciary Act of 2021: exactly four seats, a thirteen-justice court. It went nowhere -- the filibuster stood, Manchin and Sinema stood with it -- and the number quietly disappeared until this month's election-eve revival. To be fair to Clinton, "look at" and "see if we could make it work" is softer than enactment. But that is the tell. A principle doesn't wait to see if it can work; a device does. The device resurfaces only when the court's composition is the prize. Four votes. Franklin Roosevelt wanted six extra seats in 1937 -- a court of fifteen -- and the Senate Judiciary Committee killed the plan in July, 10-8\. The modern ask is smaller and surgical: four seats turn every contested line -- Heller, Bruen, the rest of the 5-4s and 6-3s -- into seven-vote majorities overnight. Not reform. The minimum winning number. That is Davis's real answer, and Ingraham's monologue -- which RealClearPolitics clipped under the title "The Democrats Stampede To Pack the Supreme Court" -- framed it: a court you can pack is a court you can own. Nine justices have held the text above simple majorities since 1869. The circuits figure is the fig leaf; four is the operative number; and "It would be gone" is the price of admission. ? Of course, no one cares about my vote, because I live in New York where most contests are pre-decided by the time the general election arrives. All eyes will be on Congressional races and Senate contests in Texas, Michigan, Maine, Ohio, and even unlikely places like Kansas, Alaska, Montana, South Dakota and Idaho. I'm also intrigued by gubernatorial races in Ohio, Florida and Iowa. The question on everyone's mind is on who wins the House and the Senate and whether Democrats will be in position to stifle Trump and the Republicans before the clock turns to '28.
I got asked on TV the other day whether Democrats win both the House and the Senate. I think they do. Trump and J.D. Vance have Kansas and Montana on their travel schedules. That's a schedule of trying to stop the bleeding. Trump's approval rating is a historically low 32% and even the South Dakota Senator Mike Rounds scrubbed the Trump language from his materials. You know you're doing badly when Republicans in South Dakota are running away from you.
In my mind, the major question is whether Republicans accept the results. They've been trying to muddy the water in various ways, and AI bots hacking results is a genuine possibility. The Trump crew isn't prone to accepting defeat. Will they accept the one that is coming their way tomorrow?
You have an unhappy populace, an unpopular war, stubborn inflation, anxiety about AI, and an administration that seems almost intentionally petty and tone-deaf. So I expect a blowout night for Democrats tomorrow night, including victories in places that have been pipe dreams for decades. Americans are as ornery as I've ever seen, and it's an anti-incumbent wave.
If the results are what I expect, the Democrats will soon begin crowing about how everyone likes and believes in them again, which unfortunately for them couldn't be further from the truth. A majority of Americans - 55% - disapprove of the Democratic Party while only 40% approve. It's kind of tough to make a case for being the governing majority when most Americans don't like or trust you before you say a word. Indeed, some of the most successful candidates of this cycle, like James Talarico and Rob Sand, go out of their way to separate themselves from the two-party system.
It's also why we've seen Independent Senate candidates running competitively in Idaho, South Dakota, Montana, and Nebraska, with all of those states requiring investment on the part of the Republicans to play defense in states that most would consider deep red and non-battlegrounds. This was the case I made back in 2021: that you need a third force in American politics that energizes the growing plurality - 45% or so - that consider ourselves Independents. I've campaigned with each of these Senate candidates and dearly hope that one or more of them breaks through. What a story and victory that would be! If you feel like giving some last minute money or energy, [Brian Bengs](https://substack.com/redirect/2d76c235-082c-4232-9739-daa1e33b863f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Todd Achilles](https://substack.com/redirect/2b0bb478-55b8-45ce-a3fe-df45e63b4947?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and/or [Seth Bodnar](https://substack.com/redirect/17955d93-c4c0-4e36-834f-53074bedda85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or [Forward](https://substack.com/redirect/dc34c43a-9f1e-4c29-ba58-4d5f81898fcc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) could definitely use them, and the math says that your dollar will go a much longer way with these scrappy upstarts in remote locations.
My trip to South Dakota last week was a reminder of how big and diverse the country is. Normal people don't get caught up in the news cycle social media firestorm of the day. They just want a sense that their lives and their kids' lives might get a little better. I think their vote tomorrow is going to send a clear message.

Hi there,

If your inbox is anything like mine, it’s probably flooded with donation
requests from candidates like me (sorry!), and I’ll be honest: in a
minute, I am going to ask you to please chip in before Election Day. [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/25131?t=1003&akid=2137%2E181023%2ElRWn_f ]If you don’t need
to hear any more, click here to chip in.

I need to be transparent: I’m not sending this email to everyone on our
list.

My team identified you as a top supporter who has stayed
up-to-date with our email updates, but hasn’t had a chance to chip in yet.

With less than a day until the Election, I wanted to personally reach out
and tell you the impact your first donation can have.

This is one of the most competitive gubernatorial races in the country,
and we have just 1 day left to reach undecided voters, share our message,
and make sure every Michigander understands the stakes of this election.

By pitching in for the first time today, you help us get one more
volunteer out knocking doors, put one more digital ad on a voter’s feed,
and keep us talking to voters until the polls close.

This campaign isn’t funded by a couple of mega-donors writing
million-dollar checks. It’s built by nearly a hundred thousand grassroots
supporters like you giving what they can. $25, $5, even $1 at a time.

Look, asking for money is one of my least favorite parts of running for
office, but it’s one of the most important to making sure we win. If we
don’t raise the resources we need to finish this race strong, we leave the
door open for MAGA Republicans to flip this seat and take power in
Michigan. [ https://act.jocelynbenson.com/go/25134?t=1011&akid=2137%2E181023%2ElRWn_f ]So, today I’m lowering my

before it’s too late?

🔥 While Mr. Rennie spent decades making an oversized impact on students at Port Angeles High School, his impact in this next stage of life may be even greater.

Melonie and I stayed there a few weeks ago and the hospitality was world class, the lodging was exquisite, and the views were breathtaking. Everything about our stay was thoughtfully designed and thoroughly considered by Dan & Janet who have created a remarkable experience for all their guests.

💥 The view from the back porch and deck isn’t of the Potomac River – it’s even better!

📣 The combination of vision, faith, and passion can produce something magnificent – and it certainly did here!

🔑 I was honored to write the Foreword for this new book. Some of my thoughts include:

🎤 "In 1948, Peter Marshall, Chaplain of the United States Senate, prayed the following: "Help us, our Father, to show other nations an America to imitate... the America that loves fair play, honest dealing, straight talk, real freedom and faith in God ...

📣 Sadly, Americans today are largely ignorant of the strong spiritual core provided by our Founders through our founding principles. So many of these American attributes have eroded away. The next generation desperately needs to know about our real Bible-based history. Leaders – in the church, in the school, in the home, and throughout society – need a faith-based blueprint to teach true American history and to correct false claims.

💥 Most importantly, we need a widespread revival, one that can relight the flame of liberty and reestablish the Christ-honoring glow befitting of a Shining City on a Hill. Understanding the truths behind In God We Trust, Liberty, and E Pluribus Unum will help reignite a candle that is dimming by the day. May today’s Christians stoke the flames and hold the light of liberty high; may we strive to be an America to imitate.”

body:
Before you vote, remember these facts
| | | | [](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
---
Hi Friend,
If you haven’t voted already, here’s the truth:
_**Elections aren’t decided by polls or predictions. They’re decided by the people who show up.**_
Tomorrow night, you’ll either be glad you voted or wish you had.
Your neighbors, your kids, and your community are counting on you to speak up. Don’t leave it to chance, and don’t leave it to someone else to speak for you.
Suhas is counting on you not showing up. He wants everyone to believe this election is already decided.
But what Suhas doesn’t know is that this community is passionate about the integrity of our democracy, the quality of our neighborhoods, and leaving this country better than we found it for our kids and grandkids.
In his 2 years in Congress, Suhas has broken too many promises on the issues that matter most to us, from protecting federal workers to stopping data centers in our communities to fighting fraud, and our quality of life has suffered for it.
**We must show up to shut down Suhas Subramanyam.**
Election Day is Tuesday, November 3. Polls are open from 6 a.m. to 7 p.m. Pick your time right now, bring a neighbor, and _**make sure everyone you know has a plan to vote Suhas out.**_
Not sure where to vote? Click below to find your polling place.
[FIND MY POLLING PLACE](https://link.mail.beckwithforcongress.)
| | | I will fight hard in Congress to restore faith in the American Dream, but I need you to show up and vote.
**If you haven’t voted yet, get out and VOTE on Tuesday, November 3rd!**
See you at the polls!

God Bless, Dave Beckwith
**Beckwith for Congress** _Restoring Faith in the American Dream_

### The U-Haul economy meets the 287(g) state

The trucks tell it plainly. Between 2018 and July 1, 2025, Tennessee grew from roughly 6.77 million people to 7,315,076 -- a gain of more than 540,000 residents, most of them Americans moving in from other states (Census Bureau estimates). Read the license plates on I-40: New York, Illinois, New Jersey, and since the pandemic a long, unbroken line from California. For years the running joke on both coasts has been "California, our Tennessee" -- the idea that enough Left Coast transplants could officially tip the state blue. Could happen. Hasn't yet: the General Assembly is more Republican than ever, and Nashville is bluer while its exurbs redden. But the arithmetic keeps compounding. Half a million people is the city of Tucson, dropped whole into the Cumberland Plateau, asking about schools.
Now hold that image next to what else Tennessee has been building since 2025.
In a special legislative session, the state created the Centralized Immigration Enforcement Division inside the Department of Safety & Homeland Security, run by a governor-appointed chief with a direct line to Washington. Adopting a sanctuary policy became a felony for officials. A 2026 follow-up orders every county sheriff into a 287(g) agreement with ICE by January 2027 -- or the county loses state funding. Driver's tests are English-only now, with a one-time foreign-language option. Benefits require status verification; licenses require more than a work permit. ICE's own count: 120 287(g) partners in Tennessee as of September 9 -- near the top of the national table. Republicans cite 18,500-plus removals under the current administration. Public trackers, which count detentions rather than removals, put the figure near 15,000 since early 2025, two-thirds of the detainees showing no criminal record or only pending charges (Tennessee Lookout). Cite the first number; audit the second.
Missouri is the patient version of the same instinct. English became the state's official language in 2008 with 86.31% of the vote (Ballotpedia). Status checks on arrested people date to that same year; the ban on college aid for unlawfully present students to 2009; the sanctuary ban, with funding penalties, to the years after. In 2025, Governor Mike Kehoe put the Highway Patrol into a 287(g) partnership with ICE on Inauguration Day, January 13. Missouri's reward, according to the chain email that has resurfaced in every enforcement cycle since 2010, is that the state has "no illegals" -- and that the media won't say so. False, as it was false in 2010: about 100,000 unauthorized people live in Missouri by independent estimates. What Missouri actually proves is smaller and more honest. Fifteen-plus years of consistency lowers a pull factor -- and a state that was never a destination in the first place gets to claim the credit.
Tennessee's unfinished fronts tell you where the ambition runs. House Bill 793, Majority Leader William Lamberth's vehicle for challenging 'Plyler v. Doe', would let schools refuse enrollment or charge tuition to children here without status; stalled nearly two years over federal-funding fears, it survives only as a watered-down tracking mandate passed by the House in March. And last week a Davidson County judge blocked the state from verifying immigration status for Ryan White HIV/AIDS patients (Nashville CARES v. Tennessee Department of Health). The laws are largely on the books now. The rate limiter is the courts. The gap Tennessee still wants to close is the one Florida and Texas own: the street-level 287(g) Task Force Model -- immigration checks during routine duties, not just jail screening. Tennessee's 120 partners are mostly jail-screening arrangements. Florida deputizes the highway.
Which brings us back to the trucks. The most aggressively enforced immigration state in America is also one of its great welcome mats -- for the domestic kind. No Tennessee statute asks a Californian for papers. E-Verify screens the hired; the U-Haul pulls up unvetted. The transplant arrives with an out-of-state checkbook, a higher tolerance for property taxes, and a vote that arrives on schedule. Nobody in the legislature has proposed a 287(g) agreement for moving companies, though the moving companies change the state more, in aggregate, than any single foreign-born labor flow. That is not an argument against the newcomers. It is an observation about the architecture: one migration gets a felony statute, a mandate, a funding clawback, and a publicity campaign for every ignored detainer; the other gets a tax incentive, a chamber-of-commerce video, and billboards in Los Angeles.
The state's answer to its one blue county is the same architecture pointed inward. Nashville is both the destination of a large share of those transplants and the place the legislature treats as a special case: no exemptions to the 287(g) mandate, revenue withheld, the county jail told to comply. Preemption is how a supermajority governs a city. The transplants are the ironic margin in that fight -- the growth keeps making Nashville more Democratic and the surrounding counties more Republican, and the enforcement statutes keep assuming the opposite.
The attrition-through-enforcement thesis says: make illegal presence expensive, and people leave or never come. The growth thesis says: make moving here cheap, and people come. Tennessee is running both experiments at once, on two different populations, and only one of them got asked for documents. Who decided that? The new Tennesseans did, one driver's license and one down payment at a time; the ones on the other migration never got that option. The laws decide who belongs.
The trucks don't read them.

name: Kailee Buller for Congress
subject: Tomorrow, we decide.
body:
Four things I need you to know before polls open.

| | | | |
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Peter, I'm going to get right to the point:
Tomorrow is Election Day, and I need every one of our supporters to know four things before polls open.

1. **This race is within reach.** President Trump said it himself! The only thing that decides it now is who shows up.
2. **Your vote counts more here than almost anywhere**. NY-22 is close. A few votes per town could be the difference.
3. **Know your plan.**[ Find your polling place.](https://us.list-manage.com/1915vgbtOGy?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
4. **Bring someone with you.** Every friend, neighbor, and family member you bring matters.

---
| [I'M VOTING TOMORROW >>](https://us.list-manage.com/rZINrD4Jden?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Tomorrow is Election Day. Before we get there, I want to say thank you.
Over the past several months, I've traveled all across Northeast Ohio, listened to your stories, heard your concerns, and met so many wonderful people who care deeply about our communities.
You've reminded me why I started this journey.
To everyone who knocked on doors, made phone calls, put a sign in their yard, donated, shared a post, or simply offered a kind word along the way — thank you.
Tomorrow, we have an opportunity to make our voices heard.
Whether you've already voted or you're heading to the polls tomorrow, thank you for being part of this journey.

body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9913%2E582294%2EI2Dgii ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9913%2E582294%2EI2Dgii ]Chris Pappas for Senate

At the GOP Senate debate, John Sununu told a roomful of Republicans he’s
running to send me back to “bussing tables” at my family’s “chicken
restaurant.” He meant it as an insult.

As if the people who work in restaurants — cooking your food, clearing
your plates, keeping family businesses alive — have something to be
embarrassed about.

My great-grandfather came to New Hampshire from Greece over a century ago
and opened a candy shop in Manchester. My family built it into a
restaurant that’s been serving our community ever since.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_2.EyU5B2&refcode=em20261102-2&t=1003&akid=9913%2E582294%2EI2Dgii ]Puritan Backroom sign

John Sununu was born into a political dynasty. His father was governor and
White House Chief of Staff. His brother was governor. John went to
Washington and then spent the next 17 years cashing in with Big Oil, Big
Pharma, and Wall Street.

Oh, and his family business invested in a literal gold mine in Azerbaijan
that sells minerals to China. He’s never had to work hard a day in his
life — and his comments at that debate prove exactly what he thinks of
people who do.

The people who bus tables, flip burgers, and run small businesses in New
Hampshire don’t need a senator who looks down on them. They need one who
comes from them.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_2.EyU5B2&amount=5&refcode=em20261102-2&t=1022&akid=9913%2E582294%2EI2Dgii ]Donate $5 »

John Sununu doesn’t know the real New Hampshire. I do. That’s why I’m
running for Senate.

— Chris Pappas

name: Derek Merrin
subject: 43 Years in Washington. Tomorrow, You Decide What's Next.
body:
Time's Running Out! Ensure Your Voice is Heard in This Crucial Election.
| | | | |
---
| Friends,
Tomorrow is Election Day.
After months of campaigning, the decision is finally in the hands of Northwest Ohio voters. This is one of the most competitive congressional races in the country, and the outcome could come down to an incredibly small number of votes.
Every. Single. Vote. Matters.
Tomorrow, voters will decide who represents Northwest Ohio in Washington and helps shape the direction of our country for the next two years.
The issues facing our communities are too important to ignore. From the cost of living and economic opportunity to public safety and the future of our communities, the decisions made in Washington have real consequences here at home.
If you haven't voted, make a plan RIGHT NOW to vote tomorrow.
Polls in Ohio are open from 6:30 AM to 7:30 PM.
Make sure you know your polling location, have the identification you need, and set aside time to cast your ballot.
Don't assume someone else will make the difference.
YOU are the difference.
Thank you for being part of this campaign. Tomorrow, let's make sure Northwest Ohio's voice is heard.
Derek Merrin
---
| | | | Derek Merrin for Congress | PO Box 75 | Monclova, OH 43542 US

After nearly a year of campaigning, traveling across our state, and connecting with Texans who are ready for change, it all comes down to who shows up and makes their voice heard tomorrow.
_**There 's One Fight on the ballot -- will Texas be a state that is by and for the people, or is this the billionaires' world and we just live here?**_
I'm in this fight to make Texas a place where hardworking people can secure the American Dream.
The American Dream has always meant that if you work hard, you should not just survive -- you should thrive in this country and in Texas. But whether or not we are able to realize this vision for the future of Texas comes down to who gets the most votes tomorrow.
That's why I'm sharing helpful resources you can pass along to your friends, family and neighbors who haven't yet made it to the polls.
Here's what you need to know about casting your ballot:
* **Election Day:** Tuesday, November 3rd
* **Polls are open:** 7 a.m. - 7 p.m.
* **Find your polling location:**[ https://iwillvote.com/TX](https://substack.com/redirect/ad20f9ff-103e-40bb-acae-68f56a235bbd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Texans across the state will walk into polling places and cast their votes to decide who will be the next Governor of Texas.
**Every voter needs to hear this message: I 'm running for Governor to secure the American Dream by saving our Texas public schools and putting money back in your pocket.**
This campaign has always been about the people of Texas and the future we want to build together. And now, we're just one day away from having the opportunity to turn that vision into a reality.
**Poll after poll have shown me ahead, but a lead only matters if our voters show up.** Our organizers are on the ground right now, knocking on doors, making calls, and doing everything possible to turn out voters tomorrow.
**[With less than 24 hours until Election Day, we're counting on one final surge of grassroots support. That is why a generous supporter is matching grassroots donations up to $200,000 to power our last get-out-the-vote efforts across Texas. If you can, will you please chip in $5 (matched to $10) today to help us reach the remaining voters we need to win and take back Texas?](https://substack.com/redirect/8941bc1f-223a-4199-9544-817957872890?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[DONATE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/8941bc1f-223a-4199-9544-817957872890?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for being part of this journey. Now, let's finish what we started.
Gina

Dear Vermonters, Tomorrow is election day, and I want to thank you for your years of support.
I never expected it to take 10 years to get the majority in Montpelier to finally recognize that affordability is a priority. But we’ve finally turned the corner.

That’s why this election, you have a clear choice:

Re-electing me, so we can move toward a more affordable Vermont with a stronger economy and safer communities.

Or, electing my opponent whose agenda of higher taxes for unproven policy experiments is the exact approach that got us into this affordability crisis.
I know Vermonters are struggling from the burden of gas and grocery costs, property taxes and more.

And that’s exactly why I’m running again. Me and my team have laid the groundwork, and we have _real_ plans to [_lower health care costs_](https://us.list-manage.com/H74KG6MCw0Q?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) , [_lower energy bills_](https://us.list-manage.com/fmxarpl0X0q?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) , build more [_housing_](https://us.list-manage.com/n17vFDqt1Sj?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c) , and [_rein in property taxes_](https://us.list-manage.com/8nkxqHprxxo?e=19cebfe173&c2id=84d1094b3a168b6495ef78aca9f3540c).

Our plans rely on proven strategies used in other states - with better, more affordable results. And, they are funded _without_ raising taxes or fees.

Now, my opponent has made a lot of promises. Free this, and free that – all paid for by someone else. But as I’ve said, **her math doesn’t add up**. And you can guess who will pay the hundreds of millions of dollars to fill the gap.
That’s right: You will.

I’ve heard you loud and clear: You can’t afford more.
I also know Vermont needs strong leadership as we move into the next two years of the Trump Administration.
So when you cast your vote for governor tomorrow, I ask you to think about who you trust to fight for affordability, the economy and common sense government? And in times of crisis, who do you trust to lead?

I believe I’m the best candidate to get it done, and I’d be honored to, once again, have your support.
In appreciation,
Governor Phil Scott

Tomorrow is Election Day, and I wanted to say thank you.
For the last 15 months, you've knocked on doors, talked with your neighbors about this race and chipped in when you could. You've made phone calls on your lunch breaks and spent your weekends fighting for my campaign. I'm grateful for all of it.
With the help of folks like you claiming a stake in their own future, we've built an amazing people-powered movement.
I've spent these last 15 months on the road, hearing from people in every kind of community. Families struggling to afford child care. Recent graduates dealing with expensive rent. Farmers trying to keep up with tariffs.
I've met with volunteers who told me they'd never been to a political event before, new grassroots donors who've had enough of big money in politics and people working hard to leave a better future for the next generation.
What stays with me is how many of these conversations and relationships began with frustration, and transformed into something else. I've watched disappointment turn into hope-driven action again and again, all across the state.
I know we are ready to flip this seat. And when the polls close tomorrow night, we will show the rest of the country just how many people are committed to fighting for change.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/131a5772-b5dd-46e4-9024-6b3d7dfb3ffc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But races in North Carolina are won and lost in the margins. I've seen it every time I've had the honor of being on your ballot so I know just as well as anyone: a state like this doesn't hand you a cushion.
Tomorrow is our last chance to make sure people who haven't voted have a plan to cast their ballot. My team will be out knocking on doors across the entire state.
I am hopeful -- I know what we are capable of. And I am also determined. I don't want to wake up on November 4th feeling like we missed something, like we didn't fight hard enough to the very end. I know you don't either.
[So if you're ready for one last fight, please chip in $5 or whatever you can spare, to help us finish strong.](https://substack.com/redirect/cb023736-3cee-4621-a75a-3bf30fd821d3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Your support will help us reach the very people who could decide this race.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/131a5772-b5dd-46e4-9024-6b3d7dfb3ffc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Our moment is finally here, and I am so grateful to be in it with you.

ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace-Jones before the House Administration Committee, June 10, 2026, where she repeatedly invoked the Fifth Amendment (New York Times)
In June, ActBlue CEO Regina Wallace-Jones testified before the House Administration Committee and declined -- reportedly twenty-two times, by the count Republicans kept -- to answer a single substantive question about how her platform vets foreign donations. Her own lawyers, the *Times* reported, had warned her she might have misled Congress on precisely that point.
By late September, the silence was complete. House investigators on three committees -- Judiciary (Jordan), Administration (Steil), Oversight (Comer) -- had deposed ten ActBlue witnesses: its lawyers, its fraud-prevention team, its board members. Every single one took the Fifth. The first round, back in April, had already produced the file's famous number: 146 questions asked, zero answered...

_As Democrats, we understand that this election is about holding President Trump accountable. But it's also about change. It's about new ideas and fixing a system that has stopped working for people. - DNC Chair Ken Martin_
In 2024, Trump promised to lower costs, start no new wars, and drain the swamp.
**Two years later, he’s failed.**
Every day over the last two years, Democrats have laid the groundwork to win on November 3 and then get to work to change the system. For DNC Chair Ken Martin, he understand that this election is about accountability, but it’s also about change. It’s about new ideas and fixing a system that has stopped working for people.

clean_body: Mai is the working-class champion we need| | | | Peter, I’m proud to endorse Mai Vang for Congress in California’s 7th District. Mai grew up poor, the eldest of 16 children. She became a community organizer and has served on the Sacramento City Council since 2020. She knows what working families are up against—and she’s ready to fight for them in Congress. Like me, Mai will call out the genocide in Gaza, support taxing billionaires, and stand for Medicare for All and the working class. Mai is running to make healthcare, housing, and a people-first economy priorities in Washington. That’s the kind of leadership we need to build a new Democratic Party—one that stands up to entrenched power and delivers for working families. = = With just one day left, every contribution can help get her message out and bring this campaign across the finish line. = With your support, we know Mai can win—and help build a Democratic Party that delivers. There's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted. Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes. I will not be distracted. Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders. — This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach. — And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades. **Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.** Election Day is Tuesday. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. It's hard to believe we're finally here.
Two years ago, voters gave me the opportunity to represent this district in Congress. I've never taken this responsibility lightly and it means so much to me.
Since then I've had the privilege of serving our communities and fighting for the families who put their trust in me.
But this election is about so much more than another two years in Congress.
_**Defending this seat is critical to Democrats' fight to take back the House and hold the Trump administration accountable.**_
After all the chaos coming out of Washington, I believe Americans deserve a Congress that asks tough questions, demands answers and provides real oversight of this administration.
That's why the outcome of this election matters so much.
Republicans have fought hard to take this seat back. Trump endorsed my opponent, Speaker Mike Johnson came to Nassau County to campaign against me and we've faced relentless attacks throughout this race.
But through it all you've stood with me.
Now we're just hours away from Election Day and our team is still working to reach voters before polls close tomorrow.

It's hard to believe we're finally here. Two years ago, voters gave me the opportunity to represent this district in Congress. I've never taken this responsibility lightly and it means so much to me. Since then I've had the privilege of serving our communities and fighting for the families who put their trust in me. But this election is about so much more than another two years in Congress. Defending this seat is critical to Democrats' fight to take back the House and hold the Trump administration accountable. After all the chaos coming out of Washington, I believe Americans deserve a Congress that asks tough questions, demands answers and provides real oversight of this administration. That's why the outcome of this election matters so much. Republicans have fought hard to take this seat back. Trump endorsed my opponent, Speaker Mike Johnson came to Nassau County to campaign against me and we've faced relentless attacks throughout this race. But through it all you've stood with me. Now we're just hours away from Election Day and our team is still working to reach voters before polls close tomorrow. = | | | | | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | = | | | | = | | | | Thank you for standing with me. October 2026, and the polls are doing something polls were not supposed to do. A Republican-aligned firm, Cygnal, asks likely midterm voters whether Israel has a right to exist. Among voters under thirty -- the rising crop of the right -- 41 percent say yes. Pew, back in April, found 57 percent of Republicans under fifty holding an unfavorable view of Israel, up from 50 percent a year earlier, while the party's over-50s remained solidly favorable. Yale's youth poll found the Israel divide is now wider by age than by party. The party of Reagan is aging out of its own doctrine, and the young are aging into somebody else's.
Any "Reagan Republican" in 2026 who tells you Israel is our enemy is quoting a script written in another man's administration. He is, in the only sense that matters, an Obama voter. Not because he pulled a lever in 2008 -- because the talking point he is pulling is older than his audience, and it carbon-dates to Cairo.
Overton windows do not drift. They are moved -- by repetition, at the podium, with a budget behind them. And the window on Israel was moved, deliberately, for most of twenty years.
**The old arithmetic**
George W. Bush stood before Congress on September 20, 2001 and said: "Either you are with us, or you are with the terrorists." In that arithmetic, Israel was the 'us'. Unambiguously. The Bush team codified what it called "no daylight" -- the standing rule that America and Israel would disagree only in private, because public disagreement is a torch in a hayfield. And the alliance paid for itself: Iron Dome co-production, intelligence sharing, a steadfast partner through two decades of war our enemies did not survive...

Friend, there's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted. Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes. **I will not be distracted.** Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders. — This election is**** about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it. — This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach. — And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades. Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t. Election Day is Tuesday. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes. **I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.** [**Please split a donation of $25 or any amount right now to fund BLAIR PAC****and our last get-out-the-vote ads before polls close on Tuesday.**](https://blairpac.org/l/Ic4Zh1WsSgnm)

body:
| Peter, tomorrow is Election Day, and as I think about everything we've accomplished in this campaign, I keep coming back to how extraordinary it is that we get to do this at all.

When our Founding Fathers drafted the U.S. Constitution, they understood that power must come with accountability. They gave America a system of checks and balances to ensure that no one person or branch could act without scrutiny — and they gave Congress the lion's share of power to hold the executive branch accountable.

Our constitutional design ensures that we the people have the power to elect representatives who share our values and speak for us on the national stage.

Unfortunately, Mariannette Miller-Meeks seems more interested in answering to Washington insiders, billionaires, and the super PACs funding her campaign than to the Iowans she was elected to represent. **The beauty of our democracy is that when our leaders fail us, we have the power to demand better and vote for change.**

That is why I entered this race. I was tired of looking around at the community I love and seeing my neighbors overlooked by the people who were supposed to represent them. I knew we deserved a representative who would put our families and the issues we care about ahead of party politics.

I never could have imagined what we would build together. I am profoundly grateful to every single person who has joined us in this fight for a better future and brought strength to this movement. I know there is a powerful political machine on the other side of this race. But I believe our people power is greater than any amount of money spent trying to buy this race.

Tomorrow, I hope you will make your voice heard. If you have not yet voted, please make a plan to get to the polls. And if you have already cast your ballot, please reach out to one more person. Tell a friend, a neighbor, or a family member why this election matters to you.

Thank you,

Christina

P.S. Tomorrow, my team and I will be out talking to voters right up until the polls close. We're giving this final push everything we've got, and any donation helps. body:
I’ve seen a lot of campaigns throw in the towel the day before Election Day.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142740883/657888134/777330224?refcode=email-logo&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDcvMS8xMDU4MjciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMzljMDg0YWEtZDJkNi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=pluGJn2xn474MAU4F736CIQ9481MHrxMEEp1CZoMj2A=) I’ll be honest: I’ve seen a lot of campaigns throw in the towel the day _before_ Election Day. They think nothing can change from now until tomorrow — that the outcome is already set in stone. So why bother sprinting through the finish line? Well, I’ve got 17 reasons why I’m going to give these final 24 hours everything I’ve got: **My closest election was decided by just 17 votes.** That’s the number that sticks with me, because it reminds me that every conversation matters, every voter matters, and every last minute of work matters. _We never would’ve earned those 17 votes if we’d slept in and kicked our feet up the day before Election Day._ I’m a dad. GOP Rep. Chip Roy took **[a wrecking ball to CNN's GOP-bashing midterms narrative,](https://substack.com/redirect/2cc36b00-0934-421e-a702-f58f9e6dea65?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** firing back at Kaitlan Collins' attempt to paint President Trump's 2nd term as a failure, and arguing that Republicans are in the middle of a bold project to reduce spending and secure geopolitical strength in the middle east that needs to be finished.

# **Trump floats preemptive pardons for staff if Democrats flip Congress**
President Donald Trump told The NY Post's Miranda Devine he's **[willing to issue sweeping preemptive pardons](https://substack.com/redirect/90867263-d9d2-4f08-b435-d0195d048e14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to his entire administration if Democrats regain Congress and pursue prosecutions, comparing it to his Jan. 6 pardons and Biden's own last-minute pardons of allies and family.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/90867263-d9d2-4f08-b435-d0195d048e14?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* **The comments follow threats from Democrats including Sen. Elissa Slotkin,** who said a Democratic majority should prosecute "the people who enable" Trump to deter future conservatives from joining his administration, and Rep. Jamie Raskin, who's vowed to investigate alleged "systemic corruption."
* **Trump dismissed talk of prosecuting allies like Elon Musk as unlikely** but said he'd act to protect them if needed, while acknowledging uncertainty about his own legal exposure and calling unfavorable midterm polls "rigged."

Student arrested after assaulting conservative influencer A University of Michigan student after shoving conservative influencer Lizzy Benichou to the ground during a campus event, following a heated confrontation at a table discussing whether Islam is compatible with the West. The student continued a profanity-laced tirade while being handcuffed, telling onlookers she wished she had killed Benichou and showed no remorse; campus police confirmed an officer witnessed the assault during an unpermitted event and took her into custody. Benichou said she was "OK" after the attack, which occurred during a "Liberty Under Fire USA tour stop," and claimed her attacker supported Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed -- a claim that surfaced ahead of Tuesday's election between El-Sayed and Republican Mike Rogers. Haley Stevens endorses Mike Rogers over El-Sayed, Trump invites her to join GOP President Donald Trump publicly after she withdrew her endorsement of Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed and instead backed Republican Mike Rogers, praising her "bravery" while calling El-Sayed a "jihadist" and mocking the idea of needing special security measures for him in the Senate. Stevens announced the switch after El-Sayed 's campaign reportedly told her to stay away from his events, citing tensions over his ties to Hasan Piker and his campaign's handling of antisemitism concerns following a controversial ad criticizing U.S. aid to Israel. Trump had earlier praised Stevens on Truth Social as a "Highly Respected Democrat" with broad support, including among Black and Jewish voters in Michigan. Stevens's Jewish fiance has also said he plans to vote for Rogers. Trump floats preemptive pardons for staff if Democrats flip Congress President Donald Trump told The NY Post's Miranda Devine he's to his entire administration if Democrats regain Congress and pursue prosecutions, comparing it to his Jan. 6 pardons and Biden's own last-minute pardons of allies and family. The comments follow threats from Democrats including Sen. Elissa Slotkin, who said a Democratic majority should prosecute "the people who enable" Trump to deter future conservatives from joining his administration, and Rep. Jamie Raskin, who's vowed to investigate alleged "systemic corruption." Trump dismissed talk of prosecuting allies like Elon Musk as unlikely but said he'd act to protect them if needed, while acknowledging uncertainty about his own legal exposure and calling unfavorable midterm polls "rigged." All 9 aboard Learjet killed in Florida crash near Mar-a-Lago A Learjet 60 near Cresthaven, Florida, Sunday afternoon, killing all nine people aboard; the jet had departed Austin, Texas, en route to North Eleuthera, Bahamas, with identities not yet released. Dashcam footage showed the plane rapidly descending before crashing nose-first and exploding into flames; Gov. Ron DeSantis described the scene as "cataclysmic," comparing the impact to a missile strike that left a large crater and scattered debris. The crash displaced roughly 600 residents near a nearby mobile home park, which officials said is being treated as a crime scene; county officials and the Red Cross are relocating affected residents to shelters as the FAA and NTSB investigate. * You're currently a free subscriber to . body:
Tonight is the last full evening to reach voters before the polls open.
Patriot–I am on the road working on Get Out the Vote efforts every day until election. _Because of that, we scheduled an email intended to be sent tomorrow, but it accidentally went out earlier this morning._ But the message is still the same. Months of work by candidates, campaigns, and volunteers come down to the next 24 hours.Tonight is the last full evening to reach voters before the polls open. A voter who hears from you tonight goes to bed with a plan for tomorrow.**Here's what I need you to do today:**
1. Read [_**this simple instruction guide**_](https://emails.teapartypatriots.org/CL0/https:%2F%2Ftpp-resources.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fdocuments%2FTPPCF-TextVoters-OnePager.pdf/1/010001a19cf2057e-4422e5cd-f29e-44d0-8ba1-3bb0745ed796-000000/CUn1gQH8H-BHFzFtqM3hMYO1aWuu_ZidjyoExrcNCUo=452) to get started.

body:
#
Peter —
This is not the update we wanted to share, but you deserve full transparency. We just got out of a budget meeting, where we decided we had to make some cuts.
It’s not great, but we missed our fundraising projection yesterday. We thought maybe it was just because it was Sunday and the end of daylight saving time. But when things didn’t pick up more today, we knew we had to make a quick decision.
It wasn’t a huge cut. We think we can survive it, but we’re reaching out because we are hoping you can help us avoid deeper cuts.
**[If you can afford it, will you chip in $5 or whatever you can spare to our campaign today? We can’t afford to come up short and let Elon Musk buy his own personal United States Senator.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-2-ak&t=1&akid=1187%2E1347274%2Eg-KptX)**
We know there’s a limit to what folks can give, and we don’t expect people to give every time we ask. Not in the slightest.
But we know some folks are still looking for races where they can make an impact on tomorrow’s results — and Texas is one of those places. It’s a huge state, and Democrats have not won statewide in 30 years.
And right now, every dollar is going to turning out voters — for James and Democrats up and down the ballot so we can truly transform our state and our politics.
Every dollar is going toward making sure as many Texas Democrats cast their vote tomorrow as possible.
**[So please, if you want to take back Texas and the Senate majority, consider making a donation to help us cover the last few gaps in our budget.](https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-2-ak&t=2&akid=1187%2E1347274%2Eg-KptX)**

body:
If you’re with me, & our Movement - step forward NOW:
| | | | [](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
---
As you lie in bed tonight, the house quiet and the day finally still, think about this: **_tomorrow you might wake up in a country that no longer has the majority that protects the things you care about most._** All of it can slip away _not because_ the other side suddenly became more popular, _but because_ **enough good people like you decided, just this once, that voting wasn’t quite important enough.**
I know what you’re telling yourself. Trump’s already President. Why do I still have to show up? You’ve got a lot going on. Voting feels like one more thing. I get it. I hear it every day.
But the truth is simple and it is hard: **if we lose the House and the Senate, everything we have fought for since I walked back into that office can be stopped cold.**
The executive orders that secured the border, that cut the red tape, that put America first—those become nothing more than paper.
A single hostile committee, a single activist judge, a single speaker who hates everything we stand for, **and the progress stops.** The investigations start.
**The country you voted for in 2024 begins to unravel, not in some dramatic collapse, but in a thousand quiet votes you never cast.**
This is not just another midterm. This is the election that decides whether the America we reclaimed stays reclaimed or gets handed back, piece by piece, to the people who spent years trying to tear it down.
If we lose the majority, it will not be because patriots suddenly became Democrats. It will be because too many of us looked at the calendar, looked at the lines, looked at our own busy lives, and decided someone else would carry the load.

**There is no someone else.**
**There is only you.** ****

**_[So tonight, for maybe one more time, I’m giving Patriots the opportunity to join my MAGA Membership. As long as you promise to vote red tomorrow. Not later. Not “if I have time.” Tomorrow.](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)_**

**_[]()_**_If you’re with me, if you feel the weight of what’s at stake, then step forward right now._

[Join here >>>](https://link.win.donaldjtrump.)
