FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
November 2, 2026
# **Lenney Takes On Anthon for Pro Tem: "Two More Years of Chairmen Holding Republican Bills Hostage? No Thanks."**
NAMPA, Idaho, Nov. 2, 2026. State Sen. Brian Lenney (R-Nampa) announced today he's running for President Pro Tempore of the Idaho Senate, challenging incumbent Kelly Anthon (R-Burley) when Senate Republicans pick their leadership in December.
"Leadership should change often," Lenney said. "When the same people hold the keys to the Senate year after year, the lobbyists, bureaucrats, and big-money PACs get too comfortable, and the people get ignored. Follow the money and the endorsements. It's all right there. Two more years of chairmen holding good Republican bills hostage? No thanks."
Lenney says the 2026 session proves the point. Republicans brought several bills to fight illegal immigration. The Senate delivered nothing significant, and the cheap-labor lobby that profits off illegal workers cheered. The bill to stop taxpayer support of teachers' unions should've been easy to pass. Instead, it got buried by a Republican chairman who made a backroom deal with the teachers' unions. So Lenney pulled a last-minute floor maneuver to drag it in front of the full Senate, and it passed.
But the chairman who sat on that bill still has his gavel.
"We had a Republican chairman holding a popular bill hostage and fighting his own party's agenda," Lenney said. "Nobody in leadership lifted a finger. The Pro Tem has the power to fix that, and that power has to be used."
As Pro Tem, Lenney says he'd put the right people in the right spots so good bills get a hearing and a vote, instead of getting stuffed in a drawer.
"I'm America First, and I'm one of the most consistent conservatives in the Senate," Lenney said. "The governor, the bureaucrats, and the lobbyist class already have plenty of errand boys. The people of Idaho need someone working for them."
Lenney represents District 13 in Nampa and begins his fifth legislative session in January 2027.

name: Gina Hinojosa
subject: Last chance to double it
body:
We’re $54,000 away, and the match ends when polls close tomorrow.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
We’re almost there. We’ve raised $146,000 toward our $200,000 get-out-the-vote goal. We’re just $54,000 away from unlocking every dollar of this match.

After months of relentless organizing, tomorrow is Election Day.
#
Peter, tomorrow is Election Day.
After months of relentless organizing, **everything comes down to these next 24 hours.**
Tim Walz started Small Town PAC to show up in places often overlooked by DC politicians and support Democratic candidates who understand and will fight for working families.
Tomorrow, voters across the country will make their voices heard, and we have an incredible opportunity to help elect all nine of our endorsed candidates:
For Congress:
**● Jake Johnson** — Minnesota’s 1st district
**● Sarah Trone Garriott** — Iowa’s 3rd district
**● Rachel Wallace** — Pennsylvania’s 9th district
**● Bob Brooks** — Pennsylvania’s 7th district
**● Denise Powell** — Nebraska’s 2nd district
**● Mitch Berman** — Wisconsin’s 1st district
For Governor:
**● David Crowley** — Wisconsin
**● Amy Acton** — Ohio
**● Cindy Holscher** — Kansas
These leaders embody the heart, resilience, and vision our small towns deserve, and they’re ready to take on the modern-day robber barons seeing record profits while everyday people struggle to get by.
By supporting this slate, we can flip the House from red to blue and elect new Democratic governors to stand up to the Trump administration in their respective states.
But Donald Trump’s billionaire megadonors and far-right super PACs aren’t backing down — they’re spending more than ever, right up until the final second, to try and stop our momentum.
**That’s why our last-minute GOTV efforts are critical, Peter.** Every phone call made, door knocked, and voter we turn out to the polls in these final hours can be the difference between winning and coming up short in each of these nine races.
**[We have the power to build a brighter future for working families — but we need everyone standing with us right now to make it happen. Can you rush $5 or whatever you can spare right now to power our Election Day push?](https://act.timwalz.com/go/73?c0=stp-ms-em-20261102-2.Frjh36&amount=5&refcode=em20261102-1310&t=1&akid=1310%2E34582%2Eze0-j_)**

Peter,
For months, the Trump administration has tried to rig the upcoming election by using the U.S. Postal Service to block mail ballots from reaching voters.
The courts, including the Supreme Court, have repeatedly blocked the scheme.
But by every indication, Trump still plans to use the Postal Service to rig this election. And the latest proof is bonechilling.
The Trump admin is now deploying nearly 1,000 armed guards from Prosegur, a private security firm accused of human rights abuses, to postal facilities across the country ahead of the tomorrow's election:
---
| | [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001Y3K5viRotKolnaT8y_vENgll8yylfEkUv_iqb618LiGUURSeq-hp_TNbI3-sovYCmXdO-RuykFeKAAtWac5zp6w7Wf4gtUBtou_pvCZlSzrq3n1ALzOUl4ZfYiusgzEHLExh0M2eO2ZMRWZJylLseExM4l4WvK6-2maBc97__8z7urVq9JuNCfRG2llSiSsGrEp7HBA3-a9iL-iQVMPdZ5uiCGqiBi8x5O7ZSaQHGQY=&c=_KBbJEMxWN2cepqdmYv0br1jkDuIYemjOPiOOyBMrnLhwKZaM4xSVg==&ch=OHzUo1e6ZSV0U46ViaHtdFuZF5oXNrnxZtTkpePMDDhol4V0HqPL_w==)

Make no doubt about it, Trump is putting the chess pieces in position to attempt a fascist coup in the coming days. You don't hire one of the shadiest private security contractors in the world just to protect the mail. Trump is deploying them to commit treason on his behalf.
And none of this is happening in a vacuum. Trump just blocked international election observers from monitoring our elections for the first time in more than two decades. In their place, the administration is sending DOJ, FBI, and potentially ICE to "monitor" polling places.
Why is Trump assembling an army of armed guards and federal agents around our elections this November?
Democrats must stay focused on what we have to do to save our country. We have to get out and vote, and make this election too big to rig. When we flip the House and Senate, we must immediately move to impeach and prosecute Trump for treason.
Defend Our Courts is fighting to expand the firewall of state Supreme Courts, the courts that can prevent Trump's election rigging, on a national scale, while turning out voters in states with key House and Senate races.
We cannot overstate the threat our Democracy faces at this moment. What we do in these final hours very well may determine whether we even have one at all. Hey folks,
J.D. Vance wants to be president. There's just one problem: Donald Trump doesn't seem all that interested in helping him get there.
Vance is struggling to draw crowds, Trump is reportedly complaining about it, and Marco Rubio is suddenly looking like a serious threat to Vance's 2028 ambitions. And when a young voter asks Vance a genuine question about how anyone can afford to start a family, his response tells you everything about what's wrong with this guy.

* [**00:02:19**] New York Times reporting reveals Trump has been privately criticizing Vance's small crowds, and I explain why the vice president could become a convenient scapegoat if Republicans lose big in the midterms.
* [**00:04:24**] Vance's increasingly awkward campaign appearances reveal a politician obsessed with crowd sizes and Trump's approval, while Republicans struggle to generate enthusiasm in Texas.
* [**00:07:09**] Trump gets a direct opportunity to endorse Vance for president in 2028 and refuses. We get into why Marco Rubio, Pete Hegseth, and other Republicans could be circling.
* [**00:09:39**] New polling shows Vance leading the potential Republican field but deeply unpopular with Americans, raising serious questions about whether he can actually win a national election.

This is about more than J.D. Vance's presidential ambitions. It's about a Republican Party built around one man's ego, where loyalty matters more than competence and politicians spend more time chasing Trump's approval than answering people's real concerns. Americans are struggling to afford homes, raise families, and build decent lives. name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: Let them have the drama
disclaimer_text: Paid for by DLCC PAC
body:
Don’t get pulled into the noise. Lock in. Focus on one thing: getting every Democrat in Michigan to the polls on Tuesday. | | |
---
| | Peter, there's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted. Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes. **I will not be distracted.** Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders. — This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it. — This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach. — And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades. Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t. Election Day is Tuesday. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes. **I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.** [Please split a donation of $10 or any amount right now to fund the Democratic Legislative Campaign Committee and our last get-out-the-vote ads before polls close tomorrow. ](https://an.dlcc.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqvLlvOtFHcHSW1T-Hwi1Or__yaKH0zdPYprfjeVfO2jiRa3WacfooHyMO0MJQYcvCY4YbAWTHobBoTVMWGy2da1iUS25gqDhcjEYUjBXsx98Za6EeacuSjY8-30FVvdLabIUsUwf3xlliQtkR2Kc7gQLQ22lG_lKbACs42nxWSW55g9yUO80O2xMgsBge1NhKrNHlaQkjiFMjD-BjktQsZE8pPuiAyQHNs7gx0d51AS-aHxfB2pJptbXXTnmm35pJ4fvPqIRsZtNdf0uO8hdW_6fzousAPp9DUMt_XuPUK69UQ4zEy2ooV0Wckj_a2MZDRIRC3igdnjs4jn_3hntOclpvYNSq2pfFU6f0QHH32XKcVQ_fxgjoD1TMY6I7yT1fwFUmmQZ0G1zdlBV2qZj0xMHeE5UL0rgaHje16kTWrnLr5leuWAoM1FKatIBrpqw8o/4ve/Q4U5k6VUTG2PxbY2r4uGqg/h0/h001.nL1cxOrtaeFKt6neCZULxcU-SUzkAFmMYgIg51SM3SQ) | If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will process immediately and be split between Abdul El-Sayed and DLCC PAC.

clean_body: Don’t get pulled into the noise. Lock in. Focus on one thing: getting every Democrat in Michigan to the polls on Tuesday. | | | | | Peter, there's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted. Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes. I will not be distracted. Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders. — This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it. — This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach. — And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades. Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t. Election Day is Tuesday. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes. name: Mark Kelly
subject: Why your support still matters
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Mark Kelly for Senate
body:
Campaigns have to project how much they’re going to raise over those last few days before the election, same as any other time.
#

Team, it’s a question as good as any other right now.
“Why am I still getting asked to donate to campaigns now, this close to the election?”
And it’s a question I can answer, if you’ll let me.
I ran a campaign in 2020, and another in 2022. What we raised in 2020 was the best indication of what we might raise in 2022. From the beginning of that campaign, we built out projections based on that information.
You need to know how much you can expect to raise because that tells you how much you can expect to spend. Every dollar goes toward reaching and turning out voters. And in races that can be determined by just a few thousand, even a few hundred votes, that information is absolutely critical.
Campaigns have to project how much they’re going to raise over those last few days before the election, same as any other time. That’s budgeted. It’s how you fully fund your final advertisements, get-out-the-vote efforts, rallies, and the last rounds of payroll for staff who have worked night and day for you for months, sometimes years.
This close to the election, you don’t have time to make up the gap if you do end up falling short. That makes these final days the most stressful of the campaign, and that’s why you’re still getting fundraising requests.
I’ve been there, and I know what that’s like. So, I’m going to do what I can over these final hours to try to help out.
[**Right now, what that means is asking you to split a donation between Abdul El-Sayed’s campaign for Senate in Michigan, and mine. I was just with Abdul last month, and I know they need the support. It’d mean a lot to me if you could chip in.**](https://act.markkelly.com/go/1389?c0=mek-em-elsayed.ji7AWM&refcode=em261102-1-MS&t=1&akid=6810%2E6688874%2E_wPo8S)

If we turn out every Democratic voter in Wisconsin, we’re going to win in a landslide. | | | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquchf2e3e-bIm5hAkq2zKIje5ZlElB9ot5ZI8yW4fgOALJQAT7uIIIYwY2Mj6-d9DJq3ZgAnWd4qCwlf-wDGwFGIlal8xGmnJViUlm1LKIx844rzKJbu-FmA83kA66wvTQuM2H3qieTogVkcXU6AAkKKKF1UcyxC8Kek3h0HEK5IIfli_rGxPDJrcVcaXkyXlyK9WR42KO51WlSNSfwDb7JMwS7hOSKgYISVLWMqhQtiO_2Gf6rFlLDgXcLAb7iiAKyzUJLZEJhuq4t35aiOzn48gOKBf1G2NnXcGBtZZvbKTA__tVe9xSfiKrSwbT-H-UdgwisTPCKNE8qas-cS776RI4wNENYYSbxElolqr2Tps7kvwhDB5p0TSiR2IIe_rvruNn3LTd6HANHbIWljqe6DZPvNvgucGkFss6DOP1zjPup-vnyzyE17x4IvyW0gBc/4ve/8vG-OqaMRxOXwbt6HoolvA/h0/h001.Frtpn8ETsECAeGDXk8uvOSffq0bBxss7ml_WX1aTVMU) Hey, Derek, it’s Ben Wikler, former WisDems chair. We have ONE DAY left. And the fight we’ve all been fighting—sixteen years of organizing to win a Democratic governorship and state legislature in Wisconsin—is on a knife’s edge. The election-denying billionaires on the right know the stakes in this election. That’s why they’ve poured over $34 million into helping Tom Tiffany. But there’s one thing they didn’t count on. You. You’ve powered Democratic victories year over year in the hardest-fought state in the country. You beat Scott Walker, you flipped the state Supreme Court majority, you ended gerrymandered maps. And in these final days, the power is in your hands to ensure that David Crowley and the Dems win it all. If we turn out every Democratic voter in Wisconsin, we’re going to win in a landslide. **[Can you split $10 right now between WisDems and Battleground Wisconsin to help turn out every last Democrat in the state?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquchf2e3e-bIm5hAkq2zKIje5ZlElB9ot5ZI8yW4fgOALJQAT7uIIIYwY2Mj6-d9DJq3ZgAnWd4qCwlf-wDGwFGIlal8xGmnJViUlm1LKIx844rzKJbu-FmA83kA66wvTQuM2H3qieTogVkcXU6AAkKKKF1UcyxC8Kek3h0HEK5ICYagiLOLCVE_7MoMFzDAUNCsty7JCboR-2jSZBO1FIPSLh-fKviXcU0uwRybcPenXKOMNwM-ek5j-vfLui7j9hPGiqTXyzkg9ZTFprCceBh0-8uFUyGY6JrTHK4vRZAMFGC_ywjgulWVPjC8g3b9dCbX70ioATG7qLbipyFVctdysqPWhzeuSGsj_eQUdO6vqFcGogguVQUAsZhUkaNlG_ZgQX40EtXw6azPnZLgDSj4hHenLl4neKdlqf2zdpCuB72rpky5zXlbkJ9vZGrFSo/4ve/8vG-OqaMRxOXwbt6HoolvA/h1/h001.FM31haHMKmqNxEMscsmJlKUky9ovyGp-esip1hVMLnc)** We’ve seen this movie before: Elon Musk tried to buy the state Supreme Court race in 2025. We threw him out of the state and elected Susan Crawford by ten percentage points. Now, Elon Musk is back—and along with him, three more MAGA mega-billionaires who are flooding the airwaves with ads and flying canvassers in from Texas to knock on Wisconsinites’ doors. But you know our secret weapon: people power. Our organizers are working with teams of volunteers in every corner of the state, right now, to talk to their neighbors, make phone calls, and build a blue wave from the bottom up. I was proud to support that grassroots operation when I was chair. Devin Remiker and the whole WisDems team are doing an amazing job now to organize their way to even higher heights. The GOP has more money, but at the grassroots level, they’re not even close to what you’ve helped build. Now we have to run through the tape. Your money pays for (expensive!) gas mileage as organizers drive from canvass launch to canvass launch, for clipboards for volunteers, and for printing costs for door hangers. clean_body: If we turn out every Democratic voter in Wisconsin, we’re going to win in a landslide. | | | | Hey, Derek, it’s Ben Wikler, former WisDems chair. We have ONE DAY left. And the fight we’ve all been fighting—sixteen years of organizing to win a Democratic governorship and state legislature in Wisconsin—is on a knife’s edge. The election-denying billionaires on the right know the stakes in this election. That’s why they’ve poured over $34 million into helping Tom Tiffany. But there’s one thing they didn’t count on. You. You’ve powered Democratic victories year over year in the hardest-fought state in the country. You beat Scott Walker, you flipped the state Supreme Court majority, you ended gerrymandered maps. And in these final days, the power is in your hands to ensure that David Crowley and the Dems win it all. If we turn out every Democratic voter in Wisconsin, we’re going to win in a landslide. We’ve seen this movie before: Elon Musk tried to buy the state Supreme Court race in 2025. We threw him out of the state and elected Susan Crawford by ten percentage points. Now, Elon Musk is back—and along with him, three more MAGA mega-billionaires who are flooding the airwaves with ads and flying canvassers in from Texas to knock on Wisconsinites’ doors. But you know our secret weapon: people power. Our organizers are working with teams of volunteers in every corner of the state, right now, to talk to their neighbors, make phone calls, and build a blue wave from the bottom up. I was proud to support that grassroots operation when I was chair. Devin Remiker and the whole WisDems team are doing an amazing job now to organize their way to even higher heights. The GOP has more money, but at the grassroots level, they’re not even close to what you’ve helped build. Now we have to run through the tape. Your money pays for (expensive!) gas mileage as organizers drive from canvass launch to canvass launch, for clipboards for volunteers, and for printing costs for door hangers. Every dollar helps. | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation to the Democratic Party of Wisconsin and Battleground Wisconsin will process immediately: | | | | | | On November 4, the day after this election, we’ll all look back and think about what we did to ensure a victory. Every person who did all they could will feel the glow of knowing that they were part of making history. Let’s spread that amazing feeling. Let’s do everything in our power. And let’s turn this nailbiter into a landslide. In solidarity, Ben Wikler * | | | | ---|---|---|--- | AS GOES WISCONSIN, SO GOES THE NATION Our party is committed to advancing progressive values and ensuring Democratic victories up and down the ballot. name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: Who this election is actually about
disclaimer_text: Paid for by McBride for Delaware
body:
Don’t get pulled into the noise. Lock in. Focus on one thing: getting every Democrat in Michigan to the polls tomorrow.
There's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted.
Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes.
**I will not be distracted.** Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders.
— This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.
— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach.
— And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades.
Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.
Election Day is tomorrow. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes.
**I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.**
[**Please split a donation of $5 or any amount right now to fund Sarah McBride's and our last get-out-the-vote ads before polls close tomorrow night.**](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_aes_em_mcbride_20261102-2.j04kSU&refcode=em20261102-4111&amount=5&t=1&akid=4111%2E21716%2EU6boQz)
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=partner_ms_aes_em_mcbride_20261102-2.j04kSU&amount=5&refcode=em20261102-4111&t=20&akid=4111%2E21716%2EU6boQz)**
Let them have the drama. Let us earn the votes.
Abdul

name: James Talarico HQ
subject: In the red
body:
[1]Talarico for Texas

We wanted to make sure you saw this note below from James. A donation
today is still important because we spent into the red, and our
fundraising is pacing behind.

We’re talking about scaling back when we really need to focus on turning
out Texans. [ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-1-ak&t=1001&akid=1188%2E1347274%2EKEI_fs ]Please donate $5 or any amount you can
afford.

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-1-ak&t=1002&akid=1188%2E1347274%2EKEI_fs ]CONTRIBUTE

We’re getting a lot of questions about whether or not a donation today can
really make any difference.

And the answer is, in no uncertain terms, absolutely. Here’s why:

When we made our budget, we had to look at historical data and fundraising
trends. It gave us an idea of what we could raise and how we needed to
manage our cash flow.

And what you see in every election cycle is that there is a significant
amount of money raised in the final few days before Election Day. So you
need to take that into account as you make spending decisions.

Smart campaigns will spend a bit into the red — knowing that money will
come through. That’s what we did. Not egregiously — a responsible amount
based on what our data suggests we’re likely to raise.

But it’s not an insignificant amount either. It makes me a bit
uncomfortable how much, but to be as transparent with you as I can —
historical data and our own metrics showed we should raise more in the
final three days of this campaign than we raised in the entire month of
October 2025. Wild, right?

So right now, we’re in the red. There are bills due tomorrow and Tuesday
that we have to pay, and if we don’t see the money that we projected
rolling in, then we’ll have to quickly cancel a bunch of ads and
organizing work to get refunds. It could mean our campaign goes dark in
the final hours of the race — when the undecided voters who plan to vote
on Election Day will make up their minds.

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-1-ak&t=1003&akid=1188%2E1347274%2EKEI_fs ]So yes, your donation today can make a difference, so I am personally
asking you to consider making a contribution if you can.

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-1-ak&t=1004&akid=1188%2E1347274%2EKEI_fs ]CONTRIBUTE

I know there are still some folks who will have questions. I hear it every
day: “But James, haven’t you raised a record-breaking amount of money?
Isn’t that already enough?”

And I hear you. I too wish that elections did not cost this much. It’s
gross, and I would love to watch the Longhorns play without being
inundated with political attack ads.

But history says this kind of spending is what it takes for Democrats to
flip a Senate seat like this. In 2020, Jon Ossoff needed more than $150
million to flip Georgia — which has a population a third of the size of
Texas.

On top of that, Elon Musk swooped in and almost single-handedly made this
the most expensive non-presidential race in American history. He
personally bankrolled the operation to rescue Ken Paxton.

And the spending is entirely lopsided. The next most expensive races have
had far more parity between Democrats and Republicans — while we’re being
basically obliterated. Ken Paxton has a massive spending advantage behind
him. His allies are spending $200 million more than ours.

It is likely once all of the data shakes out that I will have more money
spent against me than any non-presidential candidate in American history.

Sorry to inundate you with data and explanations, but I thought you
deserved candor.

The truth is every dollar we have raised has been spent already. It was
the only way to avoid an unspent surplus. That would be a disservice to
everyone who invested their hopes and resources in this movement.

There’s nothing that would make me feel worse than someone giving their
hard-earned money to our cause just to have it go unspent because we
weren’t smart enough to plan ahead.

But it does mean that every dollar we raise right now is making an impact.
It’s winning votes and turning out Democrats.

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-1-ak&t=1005&akid=1188%2E1347274%2EKEI_fs ]So if you care about taking back Texas, I hope you will consider making
a contribution today to help us win. It’d mean a lot to me.

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-1-ak&t=1006&akid=1188%2E1347274%2EKEI_fs ]CONTRIBUTE

James

[ https://act.jamestalarico.com/go/512?c0=jt-em-2026q4.erR9_P&refcode=em261102-1-ak&t=1007&akid=1188%2E1347274%2EKEI_fs ]'New York Times: In Texas, Talarico Inspires a Recurring Blue-Tinted
Dream In the go-big-or-go-home collective consciousness of Texas, no
ambition is deemed too reckless, no daydream too wild. Save perhaps one.
It is the idea, fantastical to many as it is irresistible to others, that
the Democrats will win a statewide race in Texas for the first time in 32
years. According to the latest New York Times/Siena University poll of the
race for U.S. Senate, James Talarico, a 37-year-old state legislator seen
by national Democrats as one of the breakout stars of this cycle, is ahead
of his Republican rival, Ken Paxton, the state’s scandal-plagued attorney
general, by six points. The poll was conducted from Sept. 21 to Sept. 30.
A survey from mid-September, the ReconMR/Siena Research Institute poll,
also showed the Democratic gubernatorial candidate, Gina Hinojosa, four
points ahead of the three-term G.O.P. incumbent, Greg Abbott, the most
dominant political figure in Texas. Cue the fluttering heartbeats. Cue, as
well, the eye-rolls. Given how thoroughly Republicans have dominated the
state, and how the hopes of Democrats have repeatedly crashed, some Texas
pollsters remain skeptical. “At some point, you do get conditioned by all
that’s happened in the past,” said James Henson, the director of the
University of Texas at Austin’s Texas Politics Project. “I mean, you look
at the trends and you have to admit that something’s going on. But you
still don’t want to believe your lying eyes, because you’ve been burned
for so long.” Mr. Henson was referring to the perennial spectacle of
much-ballyhooed Texas Democratic aspirants face-planting against the Lone
Star State’s red wall. First came Tony Sanchez Jr., the swaggering and
self-funding Laredo oilman whom Gov. Rick Perry dispatched in 2002 by an
18-point margin. Next was the state senator Wendy Davis, who attracted
worldwide attention for her filibuster in the Texas Legislature against an
anti-abortion measure but whom Mr. Abbott demolished by 20 points in 2014.
Finally, the El Paso congressman Beto O’Rourke came up 2.6 points short of
defeating Senator Ted Cruz in 2018 but then suffered a 10-point loss to
Mr. Abbott four years later. Even with the awareness of such humiliations,
Democrats find themselves maintaining that 2026 could, at long last, be
the year. President Trump’s deep unpopularity and the prospect of a blue
wave could, they insist, extend into the state he won by nearly 14 points
in 2024. According to a September survey conducted by Texas Southern
University, Mr. Trump is seven points underwater in Texas. Mr. Talarico
has run an energetic and well-financed campaign, while Mr. Paxton has
staged far fewer public events and has had to rely on outside groups to
fund an attack-ad blitzkrieg against his Democratic opponent. Mr. Abbott,
meanwhile, has outspent Ms. Hinojosa by a 10-to-one ratio, yet has been
unable to build an insurmountable lead. “People have vastly underestimated
Gina,” said Ms. Davis, now a political consultant and a senior adviser to
Planned Parenthood Texas Votes, an advocacy organization. “Dollar for
dollar, she’s running the best statewide campaign we’ve ever seen.” Such
optimism stands in defiance of the political axiom that Texas is where
idealistic Democrats go to be mugged by reality. The party’s demise there
is not a product of ill fortune, Mr. Henson said. “Governor Abbott has
built an impressive election machine that has benefited state-level
Republicans again and again for a decade and a half,” he said. “And the
Democratic machinery here is almost nonexistent.” A ‘Hollowing-Out’ I have
written about the politics of my native state at regular intervals for
more than three decades. After watching the Democrats’ century-long rule
in Texas come to a decisive end with Gov. Ann Richards’s loss to George W.
Bush in 1994, I saw the party descend into atrophy in which failure begot
more failure. “The 30-year drought has done a lot of things,” said Luke
Warford, the chairman of the Travis County Democratic Party and the
founder of the Agave Democratic Infrastructure Fund. “It’s kept donors on
the sidelines, which makes a lot of potentially good candidates not run
because there’s no belief they can win. And it also makes a lot of really
talented staff leave to find better-paying work in true battleground
states.” The Democratic Party has no counterpart to Mr. Abbott, and hasn’t
since 1993, when Senator Lloyd Bentsen moved to Washington to join
President Bill Clinton’s cabinet. Its weaknesses are even more glaring
farther down the hierarchy. In recent elections, as many as one-third of
state races have gone uncontested by Democrats. One-fifth of the party’s
county chairs and two-thirds of its precinct chairs have been left
unfilled. Until last year, the state party had a negative operating
budget. As the veteran Democratic consultant Matt Angle observed, “There’s
been a hollowing-out of the party.” Still, those of us who recall the
satisfied sense of invincibility among Texas Democrats after roughly a
century of one-party rule have detected similar signs of overconfidence
among the state’s ruling party. The party’s rightward tilt, increasingly
forceful with each legislative session, reached its apotheosis in March,
with Mr. Paxton’s primary victory over the more moderate Republican
four-term incumbent, Senator John Cornyn. Mr. Paxton, a close ally of Mr.

Valley. “When national donors are deciding where to invest, they look at a
place like Iowa, where $5 million can fully fund a race,” said Katherine
Fischer, the director of the Texas Majority PAC, which was established by
the liberal philanthropist Soros family. “That’s why Texas is always at
the bottom of their list. It’s just so damned big.” Reaching so many

for Talarico,” he said. “But I don’t like Paxton. He’s never done anything

failed to make good on their promises. Thaddeus Cleveland, the Republican

into the votes of his neighbors as “the price of groceries and gas, which
are compounded here because we’re so far from everywhere else.” But it is

pay the price for having potentially overestimated its mandate from the
voters. Conservative leaders have cut funds for nonprofits that aid
at-risk children, subjected school library books to right-wing litmus
tests and eliminated free bus rides to polling stations in poor
neighborhoods. “The far-right leaders here have implemented Project 2025

early sign this year that area Republicans may be out of step with Tarrant

clean_body: [1]Talarico for Texas We wanted to make sure you saw this note below from James. A donation today is still important because we spent into the red, and our fundraising is pacing behind. We’re talking about scaling back when we really need to focus on turning out Texans. [ ]Please donate $5 or any amount you can afford. [ ]CONTRIBUTE We’re getting a lot of questions about whether or not a donation today can really make any difference. And the answer is, in no uncertain terms, absolutely. But history says this kind of spending is what it takes for Democrats to flip a Senate seat like this. In 2020, Jon Ossoff needed more than $150 million to flip Georgia — which has a population a third of the size of Texas. It is likely once all of the data shakes out that I will have more money spent against me than any non-presidential candidate in American history. That would be a disservice to everyone who invested their hopes and resources in this movement. There’s nothing that would make me feel worse than someone giving their hard-earned money to our cause just to have it go unspent because we weren’t smart enough to plan ahead. But it does mean that every dollar we raise right now is making an impact. It’s winning votes and turning out Democrats. [ ]So if you care about taking back Texas, I hope you will consider making a contribution today to help us win. It’d mean a lot to me. ## VOTE NO ON ALL 3
When you get your ballot, flip it over. There are three constitutional amendments on it, and I am asking you to vote NO on all three. Question 1 would write abortion into our Constitution as a "fundamental right." It has no protection for parental consent, it allows abortion through all nine months for "mental health" reasons, and it shields providers from being held accountable. As the sponsor of born-alive legislation in Richmond, I can tell you this amendment goes far beyond anything most Virginians support. Vote NO. Question 2 would strip the definition of marriage as one man and one woman from our Constitution and write "sex" and "gender" into its place, with no protection for churches, pastors, or people of faith. Hey everybody, my team needs to make the call on our final voter outreach budget in a bit and I'm told we're still coming up short. You can help make sure we don't need to scale back our efforts in the final hours of the campaign **[by making a donation right now.](https://substack.com/redirect/ebed4592-0f72-4e3f-8807-5ede8e432139?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
If this year feels different, **you 're not imagining it.**
Donald Trump won Ohio by a double-digit margin in 2024. But tomorrow, we're taking it back and giving working people a voice in Washington.
My opponent has spent the last two years in the Senate with real power to make people's lives better. When given the opportunity to address voters' concerns - gas, groceries, tariffs, health care - he votes to help The Money over The Many. Every time.
**That negligence would be bad enough, but I think it 's even worse.**
Jon Husted, Vivek Ramaswamy, JD Vance - and the crypto, pharma, oil, data center, and FirstEnergy guys bankrolling them - have real _contempt_ for working people.
Husted said, _we 've got to end this war_. Two weeks later, he voted to continue it. To date, he has voted 14 times to keep this war going.
He told a woman with a disabled daughter, _I will never cut Medicaid_. Two weeks later, he voted to cut Medicaid. He has voted 9 times to raise your health care costs.
Why would he tell people to their faces that he was going to do something to help, and then turn around and do the opposite? Why would he say Ohioans' "work ethic is broken"?
It's contempt.
It's not hard to know what Ohioans need and want. Husted can see it - and still he votes the other way. So now, Republicans have spent $320 million trying to convince Ohio voters that their real concerns aren't as important as whatever nasty new attack about me they're putting on the air that week.
**On November 3, Jon Husted will have to answer to Ohioans of all political stripes about the job he 's done.** Because it wasn't Ohio voters who voted for the war. We didn't vote for fertilizer prices nearly doubling, diesel going up dramatically, food prices higher than ever, gas prices, same thing. Voters didn't vote for the health care premium hikes that led to 160,000 people in Ohio dropping coverage. We didn't vote for the Medicaid cuts, or for what's happening to rural hospitals here.
Jon Husted did that. And voters know it.
We have just 1 day left. This election will be won by things we can't fully measure, like the conversations you're having with your neighbors, friends, colleagues, or family.
I want you to tell them: Help is on the way. We're going to end this war, end the tariffs, and ban health insurance companies from denying care that your doctors say you need. Tell them we're working to make it illegal for drug companies to charge them more than they do in other countries - the same pill should be the same price. Tell them I'm taking on Big Tech, Jon Husted is just taking their money.

Jim Himes has represented Connecticut in Congress for nearly 18 years--almost an entire generation.
[Pledge your support](https://substack..1Ask_orXgcNWOSJINmZo8XnxD7cntz6kymGugVhPO8M?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=223185184)
My argument is that Connecticut's families face greater challenges today than when he first took office: healthcare affordability, energy costs, infrastructure, and opportunities for the next generation.
**It 's time for a new generation of experienced leadership.**
I bring a different background to this race--as a physician and attorney, with experience confronting problems in healthcare and advocating for practical solutions.
Below are my opening remarks from our second debate. They explain where I believe our approaches differ and the questions I think every voter should consider before Election Day.
> **Good evening everyone I am Dr. Michael Goldstein the Republican Candidate for Congress, I would like to thank the CT mirror for hosting this debate**
> **This debate is between myself and Jim Himes Donald Trump is not here this evening and he probably does not even know who I am.**
> **This debate is about the failures of the past in Connecticut under the total control of the Democrats**
> **We have 2 Democrat Senators 5 Democrat Congressman, a Democrat Governor and Democrat control of both houses in the State legislator.**
> **What have we gotten from this team, the highest unemployment rate in the country, among the highest taxes, almost the highest utility rates , the most congested highway in America, and limited opportunities for our children to stay and find jobs in Connecticut**
> **If Connecticut was a baseball time there would be a clean sweep but instead like drug addicts who can 't break the habit voters keep electing only Democrats knowing that they are failing the people of Connecticut.**
> **Jim Himes, will be staring in his role as Hollywood Jim in the fantasy tale of how Donald Trump will be interfering with this election with Kash Patel impounding the voting machines, federal agents with assault rifles will be at the polls and ICE agents will arrest citizens who came to vote. The real truth is that the major cheating in our elections is by democrats in cities like Bridgeport**
> **This election should be about, affordability, energy, infrastructure, the boarder, healthcare, sane immigration policies, job growth, Iran**
> **This election should be about Jim Himes failed record in helping the people of Connecticut the hundred foot congress street bridge that was never rebuilt, the hundreds of hours wasted by commuters on I95 because Himes has not raised the federal money to fix it, or the 400 postal jobs exported to White Plains so our mail can be sorted in New York and not Connecticut.**
> **Don 't forget the Democrat Socialists of America, including 3 radical socialists Mamdani congressman, and others like them. Don't forget the radical jihadists antisemite Abdul El Sayed that Even Barak Obama is looking to add to the Democrat bullpen.**
> **If you no longer want to live in a failed state you have two choices, move or elect new leaders**
> **I believe in Connecticut and if you do to I 'm asking for your vote.**
* * *
**My Closing Message**
Eighteen years is a long time to serve in Congress. It is also enough time for voters to examine the results.
The question is not simply how long someone has held office. It is what has been accomplished, what remains unfinished, and which experience and proposals will best serve Connecticut going forward.
**One generation has passed. Now we must decide what kind of future we want for the next.**
_**Please read and share these remarks, discuss the issues with your family and neighbors, and make your voice heard on Tuesday, November 3.**_
**Dr. Michael Goldstein**
Republican Candidate for Congress -- Connecticut's 4th District
Ballot Position 2B

body:
This New Hampshire Senate race is HUGE.
Hey,
Andy Cohen here! 👋
Between executive producing, hosting, and running around after my kids, I have a pretty full plate. But every once in a while, something comes along that's important enough to make me jump into your inbox.
**And this New Hampshire Senate race? It's HUGE.**
We all love a little drama, but when it comes to our country's future, the stakes are way too high to just sit back and do nothing.
**[That's why I'm throwing my support behind Chris Pappas for Senate, and I hope you'll join me.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_6.hI88QH&refcode=em20261102-6&t=1&akid=9959%2E582294%2EJ7hspN)**
**[Donate »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_6.hI88QH&refcode=em20261102-6&t=2&akid=9959%2E582294%2EJ7hspN)**
Chris is the real deal. He's fighting to lower health care costs, protect working families, and defend our fundamental rights. We need more people like him in Washington: people who are focused on making life better for the people they represent, not doing favors for special interests.
And can we talk about the history Chris could make? He could make history as the first out gay man elected to the U.S. Senate. Now that's a moment worth celebrating. 🌈
But first we've got to get him there.
Republicans are spending big to flip this seat, and control of the Senate is on the line. New Hampshire could make all the difference. _And trust me, this is one plot twist we do NOT want._
**[Will you chip in $15, $25, or whatever you can today to help Chris win? Every contribution helps give his campaign the resources it needs to compete.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_6.hI88QH&refcode=em20261102-6&t=3&akid=9959%2E582294%2EJ7hspN)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_6.hI88QH&amount=5&refcode=em20261102-6&t=22&akid=9959%2E582294%2EJ7hspN)**
Unlike when watching a reality show, we can't just yell at the TV and hope for the best. We have to show up, speak out, and make sure our voices are heard.
Let's help Chris get to the Senate!
Mazel! 💖

Tomorrow, the South Sound decides.

---
| | Tomorrow, the South Sound decides. Tomorrow, the South Sound decides.

Many of you have known me since my days as mayor of Tacoma. I’ve spent my whole career working twice as hard for half as much, and I’ve never stopped showing up for Pierce and Thurston counties: helping South Sound residents navigate federal agencies, returning money to taxpayers, and securing federal grants for bridges, schools, and public health.

This is the work that drives me, and it’s the work I’ll continue to do in Congress.

So I’m asking you directly: Can I count on your vote?

Drop boxes close at 8pm tomorrow. If you haven’t registered, you can still register and vote in person at your county elections office until 8pm.

One door becomes one conversation.
One conversation becomes a whole family supporting us.
That family invites the neighbors over.
Those neighbors sign up for a volunteer shift.
Before long, a precinct that had never once heard from a Democrat had yard signs on every street and friends walking friends to the polls.
Seats like this one flip that way, block by block.
Our rockstar volunteers and staff have lived service before self through every mile of it.
Nothing we are promising is revolutionary.
A steady job.
A roof over your head without going bankrupt.
A government that stops hunting imaginary enemies and starts solving actual problems.
But in the age of Keith Self’s extremism, ordinary decency became the boldest platform in Texas.

clean_body: All thanks to you. | | Peter, About a year ago, I knocked on a random door in Fairview and met a wonderful family. We talked about the challenges facing our country and the need for a different direction. A few weekends ago, that same family threw a barn party for our campaign at their lovely home. We started the year as strangers and ended it resolved to fight for the same future, side by side. | That is the pattern we have repeated across TX-03 for over a year. One door becomes one conversation. One conversation becomes a whole family supporting us. That family invites the neighbors over. Those neighbors sign up for a volunteer shift. Before long, a precinct that had never once heard from a Democrat had yard signs on every street and friends walking friends to the polls. Seats like this one flip that way, block by block. Our rockstar volunteers and staff have lived service before self through every mile of it. Nothing we are promising is revolutionary. A steady job. A roof over your head without going bankrupt. A government that stops hunting imaginary enemies and starts solving actual problems. But in the age of Keith Self’s extremism, ordinary decency became the boldest platform in Texas. The whole state is counting on us, because the stakes go beyond flipping this seat. Dave Wasserman of the Cook Political Report spent this weekend editorializing that Collin County is a must-flip for James Talarico. Our ground game is how he gets it done, and we intend to deliver this county for him. | It all comes down to tomorrow. Every door we knocked, every forum Keith Self skipped, every line around the block led here. Let’s finish what one knock on one door in Fairview started. November 2, 2026, on the eve of Election Day
**I. The claim, stated plainly**
Between the parties' closing arguments, the ad wars, the donor calls, and the surrogate armies, hundreds of people have worked this cycle to keep the Republican House majority. On the evidence, no single person did more to help them than a 25-year-old investigative reporter from the National Pulse named Natalie Winters.
On October 28, Winters published a fourteen-page election guide marked **CONFIDENTIAL** -- prepared by Protect Democracy, a group co-founded by former Obama White House associate counsels Ian Bassin and Justin Florence, and promoted to progressive state legislators by the State Innovation Exchange (SiX). It is, by any reading, the other side's operational playbook for a post-Election Day constitutional fight: seven scenarios running from Election Day through counting to certification, complete with messaging doctrine, messenger lists, and political-cost calculations.
She handed the Republican Party the enemy's war plan five days before the war. The evidence of the past five days is that the party filed it in a drawer.
**II. Who Winters is -- and why October was hers**
Winters is not a casual observer. Born in 2001, a University of Chicago graduate, she rose as a senior investigative reporter at the National Pulse and became co-host of Steve Bannon's War Room -- reportedly listened to by millions -- and a White House correspondent since January 2025, a seat she won while the press establishment worked to exclude her (her National Press Club membership bid was famously rejected). Her beat has been the stories the mainstream press buried: political corruption, national security, foreign influence.
Her October run was a sustained body of work on how the 2026 election would be fought *after* the polls closed:
\- **October 28** : "Inside the Left's 'Confidential' Playbook for the 2026 Midterm Fight" -- the fourteen-page Protect Democracy guide, its seven scenarios, its grand-jury proposals, its communications timetable.
\- **October 30** : "Inside the Anti-MAGA Plan to Count Votes Outside Government" -- the counting-week machinery.
\- War Room and Glenn Beck appearances walking millions of listeners through the documents.
Nobody else in the movement -- not the RNC's research shop, not the super PACs, not the congressional leadership's operation -- produced anything comparable in October. That is not a rhetorical flourish. It is the record.
**III. What she actually found**
According to Winters' reporting, the "confidential" guide, laid out for progressive lawmakers a "_**Deceive, Disrupt, Deny**_ " theory of a three-part administration strategy, then mapped seven distinct threats across three phases -- voting, counting, certification:
| # | The threat | What the playbook proposes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Voter intimidation | Volunteer documentation, police coordination, litigation to extend polling hours |
| 2 | Nationalized election administration | Framing it as an overreach, "label an election emergency illegitimate" |
| 3 | Seizure of ballots, machines, records | Litigation, warrant-response training, and -- in the guide's words -- "Make the escalation politically costly" |
| 4 | Criminal investigations of officials | Challenge subpoenas; educate community members to "reject improper prosecutions when serving on grand juries" |
| 5 | Interference with counting | Legal teams, observers, ballot curing, peaceful events supporting tabulation |
| 6 | Mass ballot challenges | Registration checks, provisional ballots, litigation against late voter removals |
| 7 | Refusal to certify | Litigation plus "mass peaceful mobilizations" |
And then the doctrine. The document tells lawmakers that online disinformation peaks in the _ten days before_ Election Day -- so have your messaging ready now. It tells them to amplify clergy, veterans, and business owners rather than arguing facts themselves. It says, in its emergency scenario, the quiet part with unusual candor:
"**When we fight feelings with facts, we lose.** "
And it reassures its readers: "none of these require passing a bill."
**IV. Why this was the most valuable thing done for the House GOP all cycle**
1\. Information asymmetry. House Republicans and their allies have spent hundreds of millions of dollars on television, mail, and digital. No dollar amount can buy the adversary's operational plan. Winters obtained one -- verified, documented, with a public SiX briefing trail from October 22 -- and gave it away. In the economics of campaigns, a copy of the enemy's playbook is worth more than any ad flight, because every ad flight fights a battle the enemy has already chosen.
2\. It was checkable. This was not a rumor or a leak of vibes. The guide exists; SiX publicly linked it in an October 22 briefing by its Shared Tactics & Training director, Anthony Gad. Winters' reporting gave every Republican communications office in the country a quotable, sourceable document. Whether they used it is the subject of this brief.
3\. It predicted the real battlefield. 2020 and 2022 both taught the same lesson: American elections are decided *after* the polls close -- during counting, ballot curing, litigation, and certification. The playbook's own risk chart places threats across all three phases, with a planning horizon that runs "well past the close of the polls." Winters delivered a map of that terrain five days before the game began.
4\. The timing was maximal. She published on October 28 -- inside the very ten-day window her own reporting identified as the peak information-warfare period. Whatever influence the document could have had on closing messages, surrogate scripts, and Monday-night radio bookings, the window was open.
5\. She had standing the party ignores at its peril. Winters did not merely publish; she co-hosts the most-listened-to program in the movement. The warning did not need a road map to reach the party -- it had a microphone the party controls. That the party still did not act makes the failure inexcusable, not excusable.
**V. The evidence they did not heed her**
The party built a lawsuit machine instead of a story machine. The RNC, by its own description, has fielded "the most extensive election integrity apparatus in the party's history": more than 130 election-integrity lawsuits across 30-plus states, deputy state directors in 22 states, and a record observer corps. Necessary work -- and it answers the _legal_ half of the fight. But Winters' document reveals the left's plan is the *narrative* half: make every escalation politically costly, frame every legal demand as intimidation, mobilize the public, and never -- ever -- fight with facts. Litigation does not rebut a story. Nobody in the GOP apparatus appears to have been assigned to.
The doctrine she exposed is already running. On October 30 -- two days after her report -- a federal court barred the Justice Department and DHS from pressuring election officials, threatening prosecutions, or demanding halts to ballot processing. That is exactly the scenario the playbook anticipated, and exactly the moment the intimidation framing was built to exploit. California's attorney general went on cable television to say the administration is "planting post-election loss excuses and sowing distrust." The left's story is deployed and in the field. Where is the Republican counter-story? Not on the air.
The trajectory never bent. As of this writing, the Silver Bulletin's average has Democrats up roughly nine on the generic ballot; Kalshi traders put the odds of a Democratic House takeover at 92 percent; the Cook Political Report's late-October projection has Democrats flipping between 12 and 25 House seats against a 219-214 Republican margin. Whatever the warnings changed, it does not show in the numbers.
Her reporting reached the converted and stopped there. The playbook expose traveled through War Room, Rumble, Glenn Beck, and the conservative internet -- and no mainstream outlet, no Sunday show, no network evening news treated a "CONFIDENTIAL" plan for post-election constitutional warfare as a national story. That is precisely why a party counter-offensive mattered: without the GOP making the document famous, the information war never left the right's own trench.
**VI. The counter-argument, answered**
Protect Democracy will say the guide is civic education: seven bad scenarios, a call to prepare, and -- note it -- a call to *accept the results regardless of the winner*. Run the symmetry test. If a Trump-aligned group circulated a fourteen-page "CONFIDENTIAL" guide to state legislators on fighting certification with mass mobilization, on educating jurors to "reject improper prosecutions," and on making the seizure of election materials "politically costly," it would be above the fold on every front page in America, and rightly so. The document's own language -- pre-bunking, "mass peaceful mobilizations" if necessary, "none of these require passing a bill" -- is the language of operations, not civics. Winters' reporting made it possible to have that argument in public. The party declined to have it.
**VII. What heeding her would have looked like -- and still could**
The window is nearly closed, but not shut, and the lessons outlast Tuesday:
1\. Steal their messenger list. The playbook's own research says trusted voices are clergy, veterans, and business owners. The GOP should have had those exact people on camera all week, in every battleground media market, before the counting starts -- not after.
2\. Pre-bunk, don't rebut. Every lawful observer filing and ballot challenge on Wednesday will be labeled intimidation. That label is in their playbook, word for word. Quote the playbook. The cheapest weapon in politics is an opponent's own sentence.
3\. Stand up a counting-week narrative desk. Their risk chart runs from Election Day through certification. The Republican response -- litigation dockets and observer rosters -- ends where the actual fight begins. Someone must own the story from November 3 until the last gavel.
4\. Adopt the maxim. "When we fight feelings with facts, we lose" is not just their confession; it is the instruction manual. Stop fact-checking feelings. Out-feel them: real voters, real sheriffs, real pastors, real small-business owners, on camera, first.
5\. Institutionalize the Winters function. Every cycle, one desk in the party should do nothing but read the adversary's playbooks full time -- and be answered, not managed. One person with a document and a deadline just demonstrated it can be done.
**VIII. Conclusion**
Election Day decides votes. The week after Election Day decides who governs the story -- and the story is what decides who keeps power. Natalie Winters did the only genuinely asymmetric thing done for the House Republican majority this cycle: she read the other side's playbook and rang the bell, in public, in time.
The party's answer was 130 lawsuits and zero sermon-writers; poll watchers and no storytellers; a court docket where the enemy planned a doctrine. Whatever happens tomorrow, the record is already written, and it says this plainly:
The best help anyone gave House Republicans this year cost them nothing, arrived five days early, and came with the enemy's own words as proof.
They left it on the porch.

What she actually found According to Winters' reporting, the "confidential" guide, laid out for progressive lawmakers a "Deceive, Disrupt, Deny " theory of a three-part administration strategy, then mapped seven distinct threats across three phases -- voting, counting, certification: | # | The threat | What the playbook proposes | |---|---|---| | 1 | Voter intimidation | Volunteer documentation, police coordination, litigation to extend polling hours | | 2 | Nationalized election administration | Framing it as an overreach, "label an election emergency illegitimate" | | 3 | Seizure of ballots, machines, records | Litigation, warrant-response training, and -- in the guide's words -- "Make the escalation politically costly" | | 4 | Criminal investigations of officials | Challenge subpoenas; educate community members to "reject improper prosecutions when serving on grand juries" | | 5 | Interference with counting | Legal teams, observers, ballot curing, peaceful events supporting tabulation | | 6 | Mass ballot challenges | Registration checks, provisional ballots, litigation against late voter removals | | 7 | Refusal to certify | Litigation plus "mass peaceful mobilizations" | And then the doctrine. The document tells lawmakers that online disinformation peaks in the ten days before Election Day -- so have your messaging ready now. It tells them to amplify clergy, veterans, and business owners rather than arguing facts themselves. It says, in its emergency scenario, the quiet part with unusual candor: "When we fight feelings with facts, we lose. " And it reassures its readers: "none of these require passing a bill." IV. Why this was the most valuable thing done for the House GOP all cycle 1\. Information asymmetry. House Republicans and their allies have spent hundreds of millions of dollars on television, mail, and digital. No dollar amount can buy the adversary's operational plan. Winters obtained one -- verified, documented, with a public SiX briefing trail from October 22 -- and gave it away. In the economics of campaigns, a copy of the enemy's playbook is worth more than any ad flight, because every ad flight fights a battle the enemy has already chosen. 2\. It was checkable. This was not a rumor or a leak of vibes. The guide exists; SiX publicly linked it in an October 22 briefing by its Shared Tactics & Training director, Anthony Gad. Winters' reporting gave every Republican communications office in the country a quotable, sourceable document. Whether they used it is the subject of this brief. 3\. It predicted the real battlefield. 2020 and 2022 both taught the same lesson: American elections are decided after the polls close -- during counting, ballot curing, litigation, and certification. The playbook's own risk chart places threats across all three phases, with a planning horizon that runs "well past the close of the polls." Winters delivered a map of that terrain five days before the game began. 4\. The timing was maximal. She published on October 28 -- inside the very ten-day window her own reporting identified as the peak information-warfare period. Whatever influence the document could have had on closing messages, surrogate scripts, and Monday-night radio bookings, the window was open. 5\. She had standing the party ignores at its peril. Winters did not merely publish; she co-hosts the most-listened-to program in the movement. The warning did not need a road map to reach the party -- it had a microphone the party controls. That the party still did not act makes the failure inexcusable, not excusable. V. The evidence they did not heed her The party built a lawsuit machine instead of a story machine. The RNC, by its own description, has fielded "the most extensive election integrity apparatus in the party's history": more than 130 election-integrity lawsuits across 30-plus states, deputy state directors in 22 states, and a record observer corps. Necessary work -- and it answers the legal half of the fight. But Winters' document reveals the left's plan is the narrative half: make every escalation politically costly, frame every legal demand as intimidation, mobilize the public, and never -- ever -- fight with facts. Litigation does not rebut a story. Nobody in the GOP apparatus appears to have been assigned to. The doctrine she exposed is already running. On October 30 -- two days after her report -- a federal court barred the Justice Department and DHS from pressuring election officials, threatening prosecutions, or demanding halts to ballot processing. That is exactly the scenario the playbook anticipated, and exactly the moment the intimidation framing was built to exploit. California's attorney general went on cable television to say the administration is "planting post-election loss excuses and sowing distrust." The left's story is deployed and in the field. Where is the Republican counter-story? Not on the air. The trajectory never bent. As of this writing, the Silver Bulletin's average has Democrats up roughly nine on the generic ballot; Kalshi traders put the odds of a Democratic House takeover at 92 percent; the Cook Political Report's late-October projection has Democrats flipping between 12 and 25 House seats against a 219-214 Republican margin. Whatever the warnings changed, it does not show in the numbers. Her reporting reached the converted and stopped there. The playbook expose traveled through War Room, Rumble, Glenn Beck, and the conservative internet -- and no mainstream outlet, no Sunday show, no network evening news treated a "CONFIDENTIAL" plan for post-election constitutional warfare as a national story. That is precisely why a party counter-offensive mattered: without the GOP making the document famous, the information war never left the right's own trench. VI. The counter-argument, answered Protect Democracy will say the guide is civic education: seven bad scenarios, a call to prepare, and -- note it -- a call to accept the results regardless of the winner. Run the symmetry test. If a Trump-aligned group circulated a fourteen-page "CONFIDENTIAL" guide to state legislators on fighting certification with mass mobilization, on educating jurors to "reject improper prosecutions," and on making the seizure of election materials "politically costly," it would be above the fold on every front page in America, and rightly so. The document's own language -- pre-bunking, "mass peaceful mobilizations" if necessary, "none of these require passing a bill" -- is the language of operations, not civics. Winters' reporting made it possible to have that argument in public. The party declined to have it. VII. What heeding her would have looked like -- and still could The window is nearly closed, but not shut, and the lessons outlast Tuesday: 1\. Steal their messenger list. The playbook's own research says trusted voices are clergy, veterans, and business owners. The GOP should have had those exact people on camera all week, in every battleground media market, before the counting starts -- not after. 2\. Pre-bunk, don't rebut. Every lawful observer filing and ballot challenge on Wednesday will be labeled intimidation. That label is in their playbook, word for word. Quote the playbook. The cheapest weapon in politics is an opponent's own sentence. 3\. Stand up a counting-week narrative desk. Their risk chart runs from Election Day through certification. The Republican response -- litigation dockets and observer rosters -- ends where the actual fight begins. Someone must own the story from November 3 until the last gavel. 4\. Adopt the maxim. "When we fight feelings with facts, we lose" is not just their confession; it is the instruction manual. Stop fact-checking feelings. Out-feel them: real voters, real sheriffs, real pastors, real small-business owners, on camera, first. 5\. Institutionalize the Winters function. Every cycle, one desk in the party should do nothing but read the adversary's playbooks full time -- and be answered, not managed. One person with a document and a deadline just demonstrated it can be done. VIII. Conclusion Election Day decides votes. The week after Election Day decides who governs the story -- and the story is what decides who keeps power. Natalie Winters did the only genuinely asymmetric thing done for the House Republican majority this cycle: she read the other side's playbook and rang the bell, in public, in time. The party's answer was 130 lawsuits and zero sermon-writers; poll watchers and no storytellers; a court docket where the enemy planned a doctrine. Whatever happens tomorrow, the record is already written, and it says this plainly: The best help anyone gave House Republicans this year cost them nothing, arrived five days early, and came with the enemy's own words as proof. They left it on the porch. \--- Sources: Natalie G. name: James Carville
subject: Don’t let this one get away from us.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Chris Pappas for Senate
body:
I’ve watched too many Senate races slip away in the final day. Not this one.
Hi. It's James Carville, and I’ll be straight with you: **I’m sweating this race like a glass of iced tea on a July porch.**
The election is tomorrow. TOMORROW. I’ve been in this business long enough to know that the last day is when Senate races are won or when they slip away while good people are still meaning to get around to helping.
**[If you’ve been waiting to chip in to Chris Pappas, I’m asking you to do it right now. Not tomorrow. Right now.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_5.V53tK8&refcode=em20261102-5&t=1&akid=9911%2E582294%2EV2DEl8)**
**[Donate »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_5.V53tK8&amount=25&refcode=em20261102-5&t=2&akid=9911%2E582294%2EV2DEl8)**
Here’s what we’re up against. Republicans are spending **$67 million** to take this seat. Those Sununus have been running New Hampshire politics like a family business for more than forty years. John Sununu’s daddy was governor. His brother was governor. Now John wants his old Senate seat back, even though Granite Staters showed him the door in 2008.
National Republicans know exactly what this race means. New Hampshire is a Democratic-held seat. If they flip it, there’s no path to a Democratic Senate majority. If Democrats hold it, we may just flip the Senate.
Chris Pappas has won the toughest district in New Hampshire **_four damn times_**. He knows how to close. But closing costs money: ads in the final stretch, mail hitting doors, organizers knocking from Nashua to the North Country. Every dollar that comes in this week will be spent before Election Day. A dollar that shows up after November 3rd doesn’t win us a damn thing.
**[So here’s my ask: $10, $25, $50, whatever you can spare, to support Chris Pappas today.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_5.V53tK8&refcode=em20261102-5&t=3&akid=9911%2E582294%2EV2DEl8)**
**[Donate »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_5.V53tK8&amount=5&refcode=em20261102-5&t=4&akid=9911%2E582294%2EV2DEl8)**
I’ve sat in too many rooms on election night watching a race we should’ve won slip away by a few thousand votes. Every time, somebody says, “If we’d just had a little more at the end.” We can’t let that happen in New Hampshire.
**[In a race this close, the dollar you give today might be the difference, and I’m not exaggerating. Chip in $25 now, and help Chris finish this race strong.](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_5.V53tK8&amount=25&refcode=em20261102-5&t=5&akid=9911%2E582294%2EV2DEl8)**
**[Donate $5 »](https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20261102_5.V53tK8&amount=5&refcode=em20261102-5&t=24&akid=9911%2E582294%2EV2DEl8)**
Let’s win this damn thing and flip control of the Senate.
– James Carville

subject: I’m speechless
body:

Peter,
I didn’t expect to write you an email like this again. Not the day before Election Day.
If you’ve been waiting for the right moment to make your first gift to this campaign, this is it.
Here’s why I’m reaching out. A generous supporter has just offered to match grassroots donations up to $200,000 until polls close at 7 p.m. tomorrow, for one purpose: getting every last Texan who hasn’t voted to the polls.
_**That means if we raise $200,000, we’ll have $400,000 for our final get-out-the-vote push.**_ Every dollar you give becomes two.
As of today, more than 7.7 million Texans have already voted early, and the final polls show this race separated by a point or two. We feel good about what we’re seeing. But early votes only take us part of the way. **If we come up short on Election Day, everything we’ve built together over this campaign could be wasted.**
This race is going to come down to who shows up tomorrow. So every dollar of this match goes to the work that gets people there:
→ Gas money for the volunteers and staff driving across the state to reach voters
→ Walk lists, clipboards, and literature for canvassers knocking doors through tomorrow night
→ Phone and text banks reminding voters where their polling place is and what they need to bring to the polls
→ Food and water to keep our volunteers going through long days

subject: What Democrats are doing in the final stretch
body:

Derek, we are just **_hours**_ away from Election Day. **FIRST** : Thanks to our nationwide network of grassroots supporters like you, we _crushed_ our $2 million end-of-month October fundraising goal. Hitting this goal ensured Democrats had the resources to keep their foot on the gas with voter contact throughout the month. **THEN** : DNC fundraising started plummeting at the start of this month, putting us on the brink of lowering our final Election Day goal. And Derek, if we want to see Democratic victories _across the country_ , lowering our goal isn’t an option. We **need** to raise **_$1 million to power Democrats to victory.**_ [](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261102_10213_fr&amount=7&t=6&akid=10213%2E22930333%2E83x1NW) **NOW** : Thousands of donors have already stepped up to help us hit our **last** fundraising goal before Election Day. Every single grassroots donor represents an American ready to stand up, fight back, and prevent another two years of unchecked MAGA policies from the Trump administration. Yesterday’s projections showed us falling 28% short of our target, but we’ve narrowed that gap to 15% as of this morning. **Now we need your help to finish the job.** This **$1 MILLION goal** is NOT arbitrary, Derek — it’s carefully calculated to sustain our crucial door-knocking, phone-banking, and voter outreach operations in key battlegrounds until the very last polls close. **_But we can only reach it with YOUR help.**_ [**So please, Derek: Will you chip in $7 to the DNC to help us keep reaching voters in key battleground races and build grassroots power to help Democrats get elected up and down the ballot TOMORROW?**](https://ak.democrats.org/go/2234?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.gb4rMu&refcode=em_20261102_10213_fr&amount=7&t=7&akid=10213%2E22930333%2E83x1NW) _If you 've stored your info with ActBlue, we'll process your contribution instantly._ | | | **[Donate $7](https://ak.democrats.org/go/89866?c0=em-dnc-november-2026-gfr.9s4leO&amount=7&refcode=em_20261102_10213_fr&t=8&akid=10213%2E22930333%2E83x1NW)**

| | Hello Peter,

I’ll be honest with you: I was hoping we’d raise enough yesterday that I wouldn’t need to reach out again today. You have already given so much to this campaign, through your time, your generosity, and your belief in what we’re building together in Ohio’s 8th District, and I’m deeply grateful for every bit of it.
But we came up just short, and I don’t want to leave a single voter behind.
**We need $967 to send Get-Out-the-Vote texts to 12,099 of our voter targets.**
These are neighbors who care about the issues we’ve been fighting for. Many of them just need a friendly reminder of where to vote, when the polls are open, and why their voice matters.
That works out to **about 8 cents per voter.** For less than a dime, we can help one more person get to the polls.Every gift counts:
* **$10** reaches about 125 voters
* **$25** reaches more than 300 voters
* **$50** reaches more than 600 voters
* **$100** reaches more than 1,200 voters

**Here’s the good news: if just 10 people give $100, we can easily reach our goal.** Would you be one of those 10 today?

Elections like this one are won in the final hours, by the campaigns that do the work of making sure every supporter actually casts a ballot. With your help today, we can make sure 12,099 voters hear from us before they decide whether to go.
Thank you for standing with me, for standing with our community, and for believing that we deserve leadership that shows up for us. I couldn’t do this without you.With gratitude and hope,
**Dr. Vanessa Enoch**

But we came up just short, and I don’t want to leave a single voter behind. We need $967 to send Get-Out-the-Vote texts to 12,099 of our voter targets. These are neighbors who care about the issues we’ve been fighting for. Many of them just need a friendly reminder of where to vote, when the polls are open, and why their voice matters. That works out to about 8 cents per voter. For less than a dime, we can help one more person get to the polls.Every gift counts: $10 reaches about 125 voters $25 reaches more than 300 voters $50 reaches more than 600 voters $100 reaches more than 1,200 voters Here’s the good news: if just 10 people give $100, we can easily reach our goal. Would you be one of those 10 today? | [YES, I’LL GIVE $100 →]() | [I’ll chip in another amount →]() | | Elections like this one are won in the final hours, by the campaigns that do the work of making sure every supporter actually casts a ballot. With your help today, we can make sure 12,099 voters hear from us before they decide whether to go. Thank you for standing with me, for standing with our community, and for believing that we deserve leadership that shows up for us. I couldn’t do this without you.With gratitude and hope, Dr. Vanessa Enoch Democratic Candidate for Congress, Ohio’s 8th District P.S. If you’ve already given, thank you. Forwarding this email to one friend who might chip in $10 would make a real difference too. | | | Tomorrow is Election Day. If your ballot is still on the kitchen counter, don't put it in the mail. Take it to an official drop box by 8 PM tomorrow. Any drop box in Oregon will do. Then sign up at OregonVotes.gov/Track. You'll get a text or email when your ballot is accepted, and a heads-up if there's a signature problem you need to fix. **Oregonians are showing up. More than a million ballots were already in by last Thursday. But I'm not going to pretend this is a normal election.** The Trump Justice Department is sending federal "election monitors" into Multnomah County tomorrow. Days before the election, it sent me a letter warning of fines and prison time. They've attacked vote-by-mail, demanded voter data, and fought Oregon in court for months. They want you to doubt your ballot. They want election workers scared. And they're setting things up to challenge any results they don't like. **So here's what I'll tell you: Oregon has voted safely by mail for decades. We follow the law, and we'll count every legal ballot, no matter how long it takes or who's watching.** That fight doesn't end at 8 PM tomorrow. It may get harder. Results take time, and if you're counting every ballot, that's how it should be. The pressure to cut corners, cast doubt, and challenge the results will come after polls close. **[That’s why we need to be ready for anything and why I’m leaving nothing to chance and using all my tools, including my campaign team, to communicate with Oregonians.
