> Democrats are likely to win big on Tuesday, but the more important question is which Democratic Party wins. Here are the races that will decide whether the party heading into not just the next Congress, but 2028, is one that tweaks the status quo or one that takes on corporate and billionaire power and is willing to make transformational change to our economic system.
The races around the country that are getting the most attention - and rightfully so - are the ones that will determine who controls the next Congress and how badly the Republican coalition has been fractured. But it's become pretty clear that Democrats are very likely to win a healthy majority in the House and might even win a majority in the Senate - something that was unthinkable a year ago. So I wanted to talk about something different in this post. I wanted to talk about the races that will determine what _kind_ of Democratic Party will be taking power next Congress, how that will shape the kind of Democratic Party that may be in charge two years from now, and why that is so important.
The Republicans are in ruins right now because they are being led by a historically unpopular buffoon who decided to put America into another endless war, jack up the price on everything, and take part in corruption at a level we've never seen. Because of that, Democrats have a chance to win a landslide election at a scale we haven't seen since after Watergate. But Democrats shouldn't assume a big win in November is the same as people loving Democrats. In fact, right now, Democrats are only slightly more popular than Trump:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5c3b26a5-7b50-4c50-9902-7b3fd4189543?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
People are going to vote for Democrats because they're the other option. But, importantly, what Democrats do next year and in 2028 WILL give Democrats a chance to rebuild their trust with the American people, and right now there are two very different views on where the Democratic Party should go.
One wing of the Democratic Party is starting to realize that it won't be enough to say we go back to a pre-Trump status quo. So they have started using some of the correct rhetoric, such as espousing universal healthcare or saying inequality is too high or calling for regulations on AI or saying that what Israel is doing in Gaza is wrong. But they are also unwilling to directly challenge corporate power, billionaire power, or the power of our military-industrial complex because they are afraid that doing so will mean the wealthiest donors will flee the Democratic Party (even though they mostly already give to Republicans anyway). They are afraid to invest in our economy at the scale we need to really turn it around and create a country that can build and produce again. In short, they are afraid to fundamentally change a system that has been broken.
The problem is that actually creating universal healthcare, or effective AI regulation, or tackling inequality, or breaking our war-driven foreign policy, or building an America that can build at speed and scale will not be possible unless we break the stranglehold corporations and billionaires have on our government and politics. It will not be possible if the only policy solutions out there are about tweaking a regulation here or there rather than making investments at a scale we haven't seen since the New Deal and World War II mobilization. This wing of the party is led by people like Hakeem Jeffries, Chuck Schumer, and Gavin Newsom.
I'm afraid that if this ends up being the dominant force in the Democratic Party, we will end up with Democrats gaining power in this election and in 2028 by saying the right things on the campaign trail, but then failing to deliver on those promises once in power. And if that happens, the backlash from voters will end up electing someone even worse than Trump in 2028 or 2032.
Then there is another wing of the Democratic Party that believes the fight is not left vs. right, but top vs. bottom. This is the Democratic Party that traces its roots to the New Deal and the Great Society. This wing is defined by candidates who are taking no corporate money, who are often going up against AIPAC, and who are willing to call out BS in our own party's leadership. They understand our country needs transformational change, not just a few policy tweaks. They are the fighters who realize we can't fight fascism while taking orders from the same oligarchs who are funding it.
A lot of the fight over these two visions of the Democratic Party played out in the primaries earlier this year. But there are still plenty of races in November that will determine where we are headed and give us a clue as to which Democratic Party emerges as the dominant force over the next six years.
Notice that I said six years there, not two. That's because the larger effect of this midterm election is going to be determining how the 2028 Democratic presidential primaries go and then, if a Democrat wins and has a majority in the House and Senate, how the Democrats will govern with that power. Even if progressives across the country win their elections but aren't a majority of the Democratic caucus in the next Congress, they will have a megaphone and outsized influence as an ascendant force inside the party.
In 2018, when I was working with AOC and helped elect the Squad to Congress, we were in a similar spot. The entire media ecosystem wanted to cover what they'd do, and we capitalized on it to push ideas. During her first week of freshman orientation, AOC joined the Sunrise Movement for a sit-in in Nancy Pelosi's office, and the press, which loves conflict, ate it up. But critically, AOC used the sit-in not just to criticize Pelosi, but to push something new: the Green New Deal. We then launched the full Green New Deal right as the 2020 Democratic presidential primaries were starting, with the explicit goal of pushing Democratic presidential candidates to adopt ideas like industrial policy and set real goals for building a clean economy by investing at a scale not seen since World War II. The result was that everyone running for president responded with their own ambitious plans to tackle climate change - and importantly, their plans were not just some regulatory reforms, but actual plans for investing in and building the alternatives to our current dirty, expensive energy system. Even Joe Biden responded with Build Back Better, which eventually became, in pared-down form, the Inflation Reduction Act and passed. It wasn't everything we wanted, but it was the largest investment in tackling climate change in history and the biggest investment in union jobs since the New Deal.
The moment we are in now completely dwarfs what we had in 2018. The Squad was four people - the new progressives entering Congress next year will number way more than that. In 2020, there was still an appetite in the Democratic Party for going back to the halcyon days of Obama. Today, nobody running for president will be able to pitch a return to a pre-Trump status quo. Everyone running for president in 2028 will have to pitch new ideas and a real vision, and this is exactly where the new bloc of progressives getting elected will have outsized influence. And of course, the policies these progressives are running on are popular - not just in the Democratic Party but in the country at large. Ideas like [Medicare for All](https://substack.com/redirect/a7dfa205-ad46-4406-8eea-067f0f355079?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [taxing billionaires](https://substack.com/redirect/4e57fbe6-c8a3-4084-92b8-7e5c6ea3d686?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [reducing funding for endless wars](https://substack.com/redirect/3449b98d-5b63-4795-be7b-05875dbb5a20?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and [ending our funding of Israel's genocide](https://substack.com/redirect/b3a82305-891c-4e2b-87b7-31e3cdd12326?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) all have majority support in recent polling, and some have supermajority support. The question now is simply: will we have leaders in DC with the guts to push the will of the American people in the halls of power? That's what is really at stake tomorrow, and these are the races that will shape it.
* * *
# The Senate Races
Not every race I'm paying attention to is under the radar. Most of the Senate races are definitely getting the attention they deserve because they'll determine if Democrats retake the Senate.
### Minnesota - Peggy Flanagan
Michigan and Minnesota are both open seats that are must-holds for Democrats to regain control, and in both, we have unapologetic progressives likely to win. Peggy Flanagan is the Bernie-backed progressive who crushed her corporate-backed opponent in the primary by about twenty points. If elected, she'd be the first Native American woman to ever serve in the Senate.
### Michigan - Abdul El-Sayed
Michigan is arguably a more consequential seat for a progressive to win. Any Democrat running for president needs to win Michigan. Obama won it twice, Trump flipped it in 2016, Biden won it back in 2020, and Trump took it again in 2024. More than any other state, Michigan represents the rise and fall of American industry. A politics of rebuilding Michigan is a politics of rebuilding the country.
The race in Michigan has also put every argument against progressives to the test. Abdul El-Sayed hasn't backed away from his progressive agenda since winning the primary. His main message is still "money out of politics, money in your pocket, and Medicare for All." Republicans, meanwhile, are running on straight-up bigotry: their main line of attack is that he's [Muslim and therefore dangerous](https://substack.com/redirect/d86e2d64-a2aa-4089-9c63-6edce481d404?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They've spent about $70 million on ads against him.
That's why, if Abdul wins, he'll become one of the most powerful voices in Congress. He'll show that a politics of hatred, no matter how well funded, can't beat a bold candidate who doesn't back down. He'll become a de facto national leader of the progressive movement, and his campaign will be the blueprint for the 2028 Democratic presidential primary.
### Florida - Angie Nixon
The harder races on Tuesday will be Florida and Nebraska. In Florida, Angie Nixon is a democratic socialist who beat Alex Vindman in the primary despite being outraised about 16-to-1. She hasn't backed away from who she is or what she stands for, and unlike Michigan, Florida is no longer a purple state. It has become reliably Republican. A democratic socialist becoming the first Democrat to win a Senate race in Florida since 2012 would shatter conventional wisdom about electability in red and purple states, and her campaign would become a blueprint for populists running in red states across the country. Polls have Moody ahead, but [early-vote data](https://substack.com/redirect/ef15c82b-f078-41e4-819b-db8d8e7f2f64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) shows a surge for Democrats, so Nixon still has a real chance.
### Nebraska - Dan Osborn
Nebraska is even redder than Florida, and Dan Osborn, a union leader and mechanic, is running there as an independent against billionaire Pete Ricketts. Two years ago, he came within about seven points of winning, running well ahead of Kamala Harris in Nebraska. This year, the polling averages have him down but close. If Osborn wins, it will show that a working-class populist campaign can win even in states Democrats gave up on long ago.
* * *
# The House Races
### CA-07 - Mai Vang
In California, we have a jungle primary system where the top two in the primary, regardless of party, make it to the general. As a result, we still have a number of Dem-on-Dem races in our general election tomorrow where the winner will determine what kind of Democrat takes the seat.
In CA-07, Mai Vang is going against 82-year-old incumbent Doris Matsui. Matsui takes AIPAC money and is heavily funded by corporate PACs. Mai Vang, on the other hand, is not just a progressive on the issues - she's been clear that [she won't support Hakeem Jeffries for Speaker of the House](https://substack.com/redirect/5fb49f7b-ab3c-4e22-8f2d-7f1dfa9d46de?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), so she's willing to take real risks to change things. And we need more people like Mai in Congress so we CAN change Democratic Party leadership - it's something [even Democrats in Florida want to see](https://substack.com/redirect/a777e002-411e-4077-9125-6b70a5b52671?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)! [Vang is up in the latest polls, but just barely.](https://substack.com/redirect/bf40ba8b-868b-43c0-aafa-38117857caff?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### CA-34 - Angela Gonzales-Torres
Gonzales-Torres is challenging Jimmy Gomez. On the surface, Gomez doesn't seem like the worst incumbent. He's a member of the Congressional Progressive Caucus and supports Medicare for all, which has meant no sitting progressive in Congress has come in to support Angela (other than Ro Khanna, who actually has some courage when it comes to challenging his own party). But in reality, Gomez is a textbook case of a progressive who says the right things and votes the wrong way.
Gomez has taken millions from AIPAC. He is, in fact, [one of the top 10 Democratic AIPAC recipients](https://substack.com/redirect/a329dae1-0462-4639-906a-38c02ecb31dc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). He also voted to deregulate the crypto industry by voting for the GENIUS and CLARITY Acts - votes that he's been handsomely rewarded for with crypto money backing his campaign. And worst of all, he's been credibly accused by a former staffer of sexual assault. It's well known on Capitol Hill that Gomez and Swalwell, who recently had to resign because of his own sexual assault claims, were close drinking buddies who partied together. Los Angeles deserves better than representatives who say the right things on Medicare for All while actually doing the bidding of AIPAC and the crypto lobby.
### CA-11 - Connie Chan
Connie Chan is running against Scott Wiener in CA-11 - Nancy Pelosi's old seat based in San Francisco. This is home for me and I ran a primary against both Connie and Scott. So suffice it to say - I have my disagreements with both of them. However, most of my disagreements with Connie are on local issues like transit or housing that Congress has little to do with other than funding both (which she heavily supports).
In Congress, the big fights are 1) taxing the wealth of the billionaires, 2) taking on our military-industrial complex and our funding of endless wars and genocides, 3) doing real regulation of the AI industry, not weak bills, and 4) removing corporate money from our politics. In those fights, Connie is on the right side, and Scott simply isn't. Connie supports a wealth tax on billionaires and supports California's billionaire wealth tax - Prop 40 - while Scott doesn't. Connie supports a full arms embargo on Israel to stop the genocide there, while Scott doesn't. Connie is willing to call for a data center moratorium until we get real regulations - [something even tech billionaire Chris Larsen now backs](https://substack.com/redirect/e75be7cb-2038-44ec-b7d8-020211a1d7a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) - while Scott doesn't. And Connie takes no corporate money and never has, while [Scott is one of the most heavily corporate-backed candidates in California](https://substack.com/redirect/440d49b1-e16b-48fb-8a84-392186452af7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Scott Wiener likes to talk about how he led on AI regulation, but if you look at the law he actually passed, it has been watered down to the point of meaninglessness. Reportedly, [he met with industry lobbyists](https://substack.com/redirect/3c4f847b-e4af-47c4-879d-7eb3467d254a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) before passing it and his explanation was that he had to make tradeoffs to pass the bill. But the tradeoffs he made - like reducing fines on AI companies to only $1 million per violation, or reducing whistleblower protections - sound a lot more like industry giveaways than good-faith tradeoffs on the question of safety vs. innovation. And as an example of just how ineffective the law is - it wouldn't have even covered the Hugging Face hacking attack from earlier this year.
In Congress, I worry Scott will be seen as a progressive from San Francisco and use that position to provide cover for the corporate wing of the Democratic Party.
### CA-14 - Aisha Wahab
Aisha Wahab is already in Congress. In August, she won the special election to finish Eric Swalwell's term after he resigned amid sexual assault allegations, and she became the[ first Afghan American ever elected to Congress](https://substack.com/redirect/9ae3eb68-3ce2-45d2-b114-9cdc2b1913a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). On Tuesday she has to win the seat again, for a full term, against the same opponent.
That opponent is Melissa Hernandez, a moderate who serves as BART board president and was previously mayor of Dublin. She's backed by police unions, and AIPAC has gone all in for her. AIPAC's super PAC, the United Democracy Project, spent close to $2.5 million attacking Wahab, and Bold America, a group funded by UDP, added roughly another $1.8 million ([JTA](https://substack.com/redirect/54dfd1cd-2e15-489c-8d10-42c1a091fd4a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). By most estimates, the total is around [$5 million](https://substack.com/redirect/6efbfad8-75fe-4839-9b04-9330223494ec?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The ads mostly don't mention Israel. They try to paint Wahab as soft on crime, because AIPAC knows that attacking her on Gaza wouldn't work with Democratic voters.
The difference between the two candidates is clear. In a debate, Wahab was asked whether Israel's war in Gaza is a genocide, and she said yes. Hernandez wouldn't answer yes or no. Wahab is a daughter of Afghan refugees who is running on housing, healthcare, childcare and "No More Wars," and she's endorsed by labor unions, the California Democratic Party, and Our Revolution.
Wahab crushed Hernandez in the June special primary, 43% to 17%. Then the AIPAC money arrived, and the August runoff ended 53-47 ([Danville San Ramon](https://substack.com/redirect/9ae3eb68-3ce2-45d2-b114-9cdc2b1913a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). That was a win, but a much closer one, with turnout of just 23%. Hernandez called the November rematch "game on." Higher turnout on Tuesday should help Wahab, but this is the clearest test in the country of whether AIPAC can beat a progressive with enough money.
### CA-04 - Eric Jones
Mike Thompson has represented much of the North Bay since 1999, nearly 28 years. He's a perfectly pleasant, establishment Democrat, and that's the problem. In this cycle alone, Thompson has taken[ $745,000 from 251 PACs](https://substack.com/redirect/170335af-8003-49c8-b16f-c6b518a5581d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including PricewaterhouseCoopers, Constellation Brands, and insurance giants like AFLAC, Travelers, and Prudential. Asked about it, he said he's[ "not embarrassed for taking those."](https://substack.com/redirect/df969b9a-58cc-4090-aa19-4e82c5e8031d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) He's also taken money from PG&E's PAC, in a district that has been devastated by PG&E-caused wildfires.
Eric Jones takes no corporate PAC, lobbyist, or special-interest money. He's running on a platform built for working people:
* Medicare for All, with expanded coverage for dental, vision, hearing, and in-home care
* Universal childcare
* A $10,000 tax refund for working-class families, paid for by closing the corporate tax loopholes and offshore tax havens that people like Thompson's donors use
* Banning members of Congress from trading stocks
* Term limits

Jones came in second in the June primary, behind Thompson and just ahead of the top Republican. It's an uphill race, and to win he'll have to bring in independents and even Republicans. He hasn't strayed from his message in the general election, so if he manages to do that while keeping his populist messaging, it will show how populism can win across party lines in any district.
### CA-22 - Randy Villegas
Unlike the other California races on this list, this one's against a Republican. The Central Valley's 22nd District is majority-Latino and working class, and Republican David Valadao has held it for years by convincing voters he's a moderate. Then he[ voted for Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill](https://substack.com/redirect/7a27d058-84eb-40a1-ae15-d36b201f698a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), including an estimated $911 billion in Medicaid cuts, in one of the districts that depends most on Medicaid in the country. Randy Villegas is a 31-year-old community college instructor and Visalia school board trustee who isn't running as a Republican-lite Democrat. He's for universal healthcare, opposes the wars in Iran and Gaza, opposes military aid to Israel, and has stood up against ICE sweeps in a district full of farmworker families. Republicans thought he'd be easy to beat: their super PAC[ boosted him in the primary](https://substack.com/redirect/7a27d058-84eb-40a1-ae15-d36b201f698a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Now the race is a toss-up, and a Villegas win would bury the idea that progressives can't win swing seats in the Central Valley.
### MI-07 - Will Lawrence
Michigan's 7th District, around Lansing, is one of the swingiest seats in the country, exactly the kind of place the consultant class says needs a cautious, centrist Democrat. Will Lawrence is proving them wrong. He won a competitive primary with Bernie Sanders's backing, and since then he's[ leaned harder into Medicare for All](https://substack.com/redirect/393d871a-ab87-445c-a3d4-15ed863ca1af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), not away from it. He's also taken on the data center buildout that's driving up utility bills and draining water across Michigan, an issue[ The New Republic has highlighted](https://substack.com/redirect/2cd08cf5-2d4c-4519-af98-cc76457669a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and one more Democrats should be running on. I've actually known Will for nearly a decade now. I first met him in 2018, during AOC's sit-in in Nancy Pelosi's office, when he was working for the Sunrise Movement. If he can beat Republican Tom Barrett, it will show that running on bold economic populism in a swing district is a winning strategy.
### TN-09 - Justin Pearson
Justin Pearson first made national news in 2023, when Tennessee Republicans expelled him from the state legislature for protesting gun violence. Voters sent him right back. This year, Republicans came after him again. After the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act in _Louisiana v. Callais_ , they held a special session to[ carve up Memphis](https://substack.com/redirect/2794dbc7-d49b-49b8-8c7d-fc6ddc4e90f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). They turned a district Democrats had held for over 40 years into an L-shaped seat that stretches from wealthy suburbs through rural Tennessee and leans Republican by 9 points. Pearson ran anyway, won the primary, and now faces Trump-endorsed state Senator Brent Taylor. This is the hardest race on my list, and arguably the one that matters the most. If Pearson wins a seat drawn specifically to keep someone like him out of Congress, it will be one of the biggest statements of the night. And given [Taylor's recent scandal](https://substack.com/redirect/d6565786-7bf7-4c9c-88af-d7b65342f147?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Pearson really may do it.
I'm also excited about this race because of who Pearson is. I had the opportunity to hear him speak recently at an event, and he is a uniquely talented orator and politician. However this race turns out, I know this won't be the last we've seen of Pearson.
* * *
# Ballot Propositions
Some of the most direct fights over corporate and billionaire power on Tuesday aren't between candidates at all.
### California Prop 40
Prop 40 is a one-time 5% tax on the wealth of California's billionaires, with[ 90% of the money going to Medi-Cal](https://substack.com/redirect/514da202-10da-44a9-8c75-d01244f45710?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to backfill Trump's healthcare cuts. It's the clearest test in the country of whether Democrats will actually tax concentrated wealth or just talk about it, and it's become a clear wedge between the two visions of the party I talked about at the top. The California Democratic Party and Ro Khanna have endorsed it. Gavin Newsom not only opposes it, he[ endorsed Prop 42](https://substack.com/redirect/514da202-10da-44a9-8c75-d01244f45710?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a measure bankrolled by Google co-founder Sergey Brin that would cancel Prop 40 and ban future wealth taxes. If you're in California, vote Yes on 40 and No on 41 and 42. Voting yes on 40 alone isn't enough. And if you aren't fully convinced, [read my longer post taking on all the arguments against Prop 40](https://substack.com/redirect/743b031e-972b-4afd-a7ba-85978ba29569?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
### Washington I-645
Earlier this year, Washington finally passed a 9.9% tax on household income over $1 million, in a state with one of the most regressive tax systems in the country. Now a repeal initiative, I-645, would scrap it and ban any future state or local income tax. That would[ strip funding from K-12 schools](https://substack.com/redirect/f06669b1-ad1b-413e-bd41-3c88def951c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to protect a tiny number of the state's richest households. Governor Ferguson and organized labor are leading the No campaign. Like Prop 40, this is one of the clearest tests of whether we can take on the wealth of the richest in our country.
### Montana I-194
This might be the most creative attack on corporate money in politics in a generation. Instead of waiting for the Supreme Court to overturn _Citizens United_ , Montana's I-194 goes after the powers states grant corporations in the first place. It would bar corporations doing business in Montana, along with dark-money groups, from spending in elections. It has support across the spectrum, from Jon Tester to former Republican Governor Marc Racicot. The Montana Chamber of Commerce sued to keep it off the ballot and lost. It will almost certainly end up in court if it passes, but a win in a state Trump carried would show that taking money out of politics isn't a left-wing idea, but an American one. And if it holds up in court, this gives us a blueprint for getting rid of corporate money in politics once and for all, even without the Supreme Court.
* * *
There's a lot to be worried about in the world today, but I've never felt as optimistic about the future as I do right now. Part of that is the incredible leaders already headed to Congress, and the ones who will, hopefully, join them tomorrow. But the bigger part is what I'm seeing among people. People are fed up with the status quo and demanding change at a level I've never seen in my lifetime. We're at a moment where anything really is possible. The biggest ideas no longer seem radical; they seem like common sense. We have a real chance to fundamentally reshape this country so it works for everyone, and to break the stranglehold corporations and the ultra-rich have had on our politics for so long.
It won't be easy, but it's happening. So wherever you are, vote.
_Join me on the journey as we explore both the politics and the policies to turn this country around so it works for everyone and not just a handful of people at the top._

clean_body: Democrats are likely to win big on Tuesday, but the more important question is which Democratic Party wins. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more | | | Nov 2 | | | | | | | | | | | | Democrats are likely to win big on Tuesday, but the more important question is which Democratic Party wins. Here are the races that will decide whether the party heading into not just the next Congress, but 2028, is one that tweaks the status quo or one that takes on corporate and billionaire power and is willing to make transformational change to our economic system. The races around the country that are getting the most attention - and rightfully so - are the ones that will determine who controls the next Congress and how badly the Republican coalition has been fractured. But it's become pretty clear that Democrats are very likely to win a healthy majority in the House and might even win a majority in the Senate - something that was unthinkable a year ago. So I wanted to talk about something different in this post. I wanted to talk about the races that will determine what kind of Democratic Party will be taking power next Congress, how that will shape the kind of Democratic Party that may be in charge two years from now, and why that is so important. The Republicans are in ruins right now because they are being led by a historically unpopular buffoon who decided to put America into another endless war, jack up the price on everything, and take part in corruption at a level we've never seen. Because of that, Democrats have a chance to win a landslide election at a scale we haven't seen since after Watergate. But Democrats shouldn't assume a big win in November is the same as people loving Democrats. In fact, right now, Democrats are only slightly more popular than Trump: | | ---|---|--- People are going to vote for Democrats because they're the other option. But, importantly, what Democrats do next year and in 2028 WILL give Democrats a chance to rebuild their trust with the American people, and right now there are two very different views on where the Democratic Party should go. One wing of the Democratic Party is starting to realize that it won't be enough to say we go back to a pre-Trump status quo. So they have started using some of the correct rhetoric, such as espousing universal healthcare or saying inequality is too high or calling for regulations on AI or saying that what Israel is doing in Gaza is wrong. But they are also unwilling to directly challenge corporate power, billionaire power, or the power of our military-industrial complex because they are afraid that doing so will mean the wealthiest donors will flee the Democratic Party (even though they mostly already give to Republicans anyway). They are afraid to invest in our economy at the scale we need to really turn it around and create a country that can build and produce again. In short, they are afraid to fundamentally change a system that has been broken. The problem is that actually creating universal healthcare, or effective AI regulation, or tackling inequality, or breaking our war-driven foreign policy, or building an America that can build at speed and scale will not be possible unless we break the stranglehold corporations and billionaires have on our government and politics. It will not be possible if the only policy solutions out there are about tweaking a regulation here or there rather than making investments at a scale we haven't seen since the New Deal and World War II mobilization. This wing of the party is led by people like Hakeem Jeffries, Chuck Schumer, and Gavin Newsom. I'm afraid that if this ends up being the dominant force in the Democratic Party, we will end up with Democrats gaining power in this election and in 2028 by saying the right things on the campaign trail, but then failing to deliver on those promises once in power. And if that happens, the backlash from voters will end up electing someone even worse than Trump in 2028 or 2032. Then there is another wing of the Democratic Party that believes the fight is not left vs. right, but top vs. bottom. This is the Democratic Party that traces its roots to the New Deal and the Great Society. This wing is defined by candidates who are taking no corporate money, who are often going up against AIPAC, and who are willing to call out BS in our own party's leadership. They understand our country needs transformational change, not just a few policy tweaks. They are the fighters who realize we can't fight fascism while taking orders from the same oligarchs who are funding it. A lot of the fight over these two visions of the Democratic Party played out in the primaries earlier this year. But there are still plenty of races in November that will determine where we are headed and give us a clue as to which Democratic Party emerges as the dominant force over the next six years. Notice that I said six years there, not two. That's because the larger effect of this midterm election is going to be determining how the 2028 Democratic presidential primaries go and then, if a Democrat wins and has a majority in the House and Senate, how the Democrats will govern with that power. Even if progressives across the country win their elections but aren't a majority of the Democratic caucus in the next Congress, they will have a megaphone and outsized influence as an ascendant force inside the party. In 2018, when I was working with AOC and helped elect the Squad to Congress, we were in a similar spot. The entire media ecosystem wanted to cover what they'd do, and we capitalized on it to push ideas. During her first week of freshman orientation, AOC joined the Sunrise Movement for a sit-in in Nancy Pelosi's office, and the press, which loves conflict, ate it up. But critically, AOC used the sit-in not just to criticize Pelosi, but to push something new: the Green New Deal. We then launched the full Green New Deal right as the 2020 Democratic presidential primaries were starting, with the explicit goal of pushing Democratic presidential candidates to adopt ideas like industrial policy and set real goals for building a clean economy by investing at a scale not seen since World War II. The result was that everyone running for president responded with their own ambitious plans to tackle climate change - and importantly, their plans were not just some regulatory reforms, but actual plans for investing in and building the alternatives to our current dirty, expensive energy system. Even Joe Biden responded with Build Back Better, which eventually became, in pared-down form, the Inflation Reduction Act and passed. It wasn't everything we wanted, but it was the largest investment in tackling climate change in history and the biggest investment in union jobs since the New Deal. The moment we are in now completely dwarfs what we had in 2018. The Squad was four people - the new progressives entering Congress next year will number way more than that. In 2020, there was still an appetite in the Democratic Party for going back to the halcyon days of Obama. Today, nobody running for president will be able to pitch a return to a pre-Trump status quo. Everyone running for president in 2028 will have to pitch new ideas and a real vision, and this is exactly where the new bloc of progressives getting elected will have outsized influence. And of course, the policies these progressives are running on are popular - not just in the Democratic Party but in the country at large. Ideas like , , , and all have majority support in recent polling, and some have supermajority support. The question now is simply: will we have leaders in DC with the guts to push the will of the American people in the halls of power? That's what is really at stake tomorrow, and these are the races that will shape it. The Senate Races Not every race I'm paying attention to is under the radar. Most of the Senate races are definitely getting the attention they deserve because they'll determine if Democrats retake the Senate. Minnesota - Peggy Flanagan Michigan and Minnesota are both open seats that are must-holds for Democrats to regain control, and in both, we have unapologetic progressives likely to win. Peggy Flanagan is the Bernie-backed progressive who crushed her corporate-backed opponent in the primary by about twenty points. If elected, she'd be the first Native American woman to ever serve in the Senate. Michigan - Abdul El-Sayed Michigan is arguably a more consequential seat for a progressive to win. Any Democrat running for president needs to win Michigan. Obama won it twice, Trump flipped it in 2016, Biden won it back in 2020, and Trump took it again in 2024. More than any other state, Michigan represents the rise and fall of American industry. A politics of rebuilding Michigan is a politics of rebuilding the country. The race in Michigan has also put every argument against progressives to the test. Abdul El-Sayed hasn't backed away from his progressive agenda since winning the primary. His main message is still "money out of politics, money in your pocket, and Medicare for All." Republicans, meanwhile, are running on straight-up bigotry: their main line of attack is that he's . They've spent about $70 million on ads against him. That's why, if Abdul wins, he'll become one of the most powerful voices in Congress. He'll show that a politics of hatred, no matter how well funded, can't beat a bold candidate who doesn't back down. He'll become a de facto national leader of the progressive movement, and his campaign will be the blueprint for the 2028 Democratic presidential primary. Florida - Angie Nixon The harder races on Tuesday will be Florida and Nebraska. In Florida, Angie Nixon is a democratic socialist who beat Alex Vindman in the primary despite being outraised about 16-to-1. She hasn't backed away from who she is or what she stands for, and unlike Michigan, Florida is no longer a purple state. It has become reliably Republican. A democratic socialist becoming the first Democrat to win a Senate race in Florida since 2012 would shatter conventional wisdom about electability in red and purple states, and her campaign would become a blueprint for populists running in red states across the country. Polls have Moody ahead, but shows a surge for Democrats, so Nixon still has a real chance. Nebraska - Dan Osborn Nebraska is even redder than Florida, and Dan Osborn, a union leader and mechanic, is running there as an independent against billionaire Pete Ricketts. And as an example of just how ineffective the law is - it wouldn't have even covered the Hugging Face hacking attack from earlier this year. Instead of waiting for the Supreme Court to overturn Citizens United , Montana's I-194 goes after the powers states grant corporations in the first place. It would bar corporations doing business in Montana, along with dark-money groups, from spending in elections. It has support across the spectrum, from Jon Tester to former Republican Governor Marc Racicot. The Montana Chamber of Commerce sued to keep it off the ballot and lost. It will almost certainly end up in court if it passes, but a win in a state Trump carried would show that taking money out of politics isn't a left-wing idea, but an American one. And if it holds up in court, this gives us a blueprint for getting rid of corporate money in politics once and for all, even without the Supreme Court. * There's a lot to be worried about in the world today, but I've never felt as optimistic about the future as I do right now. Part of that is the incredible leaders already headed to Congress, and the ones who will, hopefully, join them tomorrow. But the bigger part is what I'm seeing among people. People are fed up with the status quo and demanding change at a level I've never seen in my lifetime. We're at a moment where anything really is possible. The biggest ideas no longer seem radical; they seem like common sense. We have a real chance to fundamentally reshape this country so it works for everyone, and to break the stranglehold corporations and the ultra-rich have had on our politics for so long. It won't be easy, but it's happening. So wherever you are, vote. Join me on the journey as we explore both the politics and the policies to turn this country around so it works for everyone and not just a handful of people at the top. ? | | | | | | | (C) 2026 Saikat for Congress 1388 Haight St #1124, 94117 ? ?

Blue Dog Reps. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez, D-Wash., and Mike Thompson, D-Calif., leave the U.S. Capitol on November 9, 2023. Photo by Tom Williams/CQ-Roll Call, Inc via Getty Images.
The last time that a blue wave powered Democrats to a House majority in 2018, 11 so-called Blue Dogs ousted Republicans, leaving the party in charge with a slim majority. House Speaker Nancy Pelosi would affectionately refer to the Blue Dogs as "majority makers," explaining that their conservative politics may be out of step with the party's base, but without them, the party would be nowhere.
The same was true in 2006 and 2008, when Blue Dogs made the difference for Democrats, exactly as they had promised to do when they organized themselves in 1995 in response to the 1994 Republican wave.
This cycle, instead of taking on Republican incumbents and working to maximize a potential Democratic majority, the Blue Dogs have been spending their scarce resources against other Democrats. A review of financial disclosures, coupled with interviews of campaign operatives, reveal that the coalition's largest expenditure since the primaries has boosted Mike Thompson, [treasurer of the Blue Dog PAC](https://substack.com/redirect/bc6aefb4-6c5e-4431-8982-e7ab39d10dcb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), against another Democrat.
This decision is all the more confusing considering that the Blue Dogs backed a candidate in Florida during the primary who is facing an uphill battle against Republican Ryan Elijah. Blue Dog Action spent $700,000 during the primary to get Bale Dalton over the top in Florida's 7th district, beating out two Democrats to his left. Cook Political Report shifted the race from Likely R to Lean R in the days before the election.
Instead of putting more money behind Dalton, the super PAC has dumped $1.73 million into a general election in California that pits Thompson against another Democrat, Eric Jones, a venture capitalist who has spent $15 million self-funding his anti-corporate, populist campaign focused on getting corporate money out of politics. In other words, rather than spend money helping Democrats retake the majority, Blue Dog Action is spending to maintain their dwindling position.
Blue Dog Action Fund is also dedicating the closing days of the election to complaining about another Democrat running, Matt Dunlap. Last year, Dunlap launched a primary challenge to Rep. Jared Golden, a former co-chair of the Blue Dog Coalition. Golden responded by retiring, and the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee got behind State Sen. Joe Baldacci in the primary, arguing that Dunlap was too progressive to win the general election. Dunlap won the primary narrowly, the party rallied behind him, and now he faces Republican Paul LePage.
But the Blue Dogs haven't forgiven Dunlap. The co-founder of the Blue Dog's super PAC recently went on the record criticizing the House Majority PAC's decision to invest in Maine instead of Florida's 7th district. "I'm not sure what HMP was thinking here," said Phil Gardner, referring to House Majority PAC's decision to cut ad reservations in FL-07 from $3.9 million to $1.95 million, calling it "bonkers they're dumping so much money" behind Dunlap in favor of Dalton--who he called "one of the party's best recruits."
Gardner, who was speaking to [Axios](https://substack.com/redirect/3ba5391b-bb82-45f5-a0cc-daa806295ad6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), is a senior advisor to Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-Wash.).
Republicans, meanwhile, have spent more than $11 million to date supporting former Governor Paul LePage there, signaling that the GOP believes the race is extremely competitive.
HMP recommitted an additional $1.7 million investment in Florida roughly one week after Gardner's critiques were published. Defending this decision, Gardner told Drop Site that, "Spending for Red to Blue candidates in tied races is the entire reason HMP exists. I can't believe any 'Democratic campaign operative' thinks it's the job of a group besides HMP to do HMP's core mission."
With their spending decisions this cycle, critical Democratic colleagues say, the Blue Dogs are forfeiting the argument that while they may be out of step politically with the base of the party on issues like Medicare for All, at least they are important to win a majority.
"Money has to be moved to the races that are in most need, regardless of what flavor of Democrat they are," a Democratic member of Congress granted anonymity to weigh in, said. "Any group that is advocating for a certain type of Democrat should use their money where it matters first and not dictate to those trying to get a majority as a priority."
A national Democratic operative concurred. "Instead of spending the final days of the midterms working to grow their caucus and help take back the House--they're attacking red-to-blue candidates and wasting close to $2 million on a Safe D race," the operative said. "It's one of the most idiotic things I've ever seen."
Gardner dismissed criticisms of Blue Dog Action's spending choices, saying, "Given that I've discussed both of those investments in advance with HMP's leadership, I can't imagine HMP is anything but grateful for BDA PAC's support of Adam Gray, a Frontline incumbent, and Mike Thompson, an ally of Leader Jeffries, given HMP's priorities elsewhere on the electoral map."
The Blue Dogs are also spending $425,000 to protect incumbent Rep. Adam Gray. In this race, there's a Republican on the other side, though [Cook Political Report lists the California district as "likely Dem."](https://substack.com/redirect/bfac7091-c2d5-4479-9938-060f293de7d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Blue Dog PAC, a distinct entity from Blue Dog Action, has contributed directly to Democrats running for seats currently held by Republicans at other times this cycle, [including](https://substack.com/redirect/76a05e47-4e78-46f4-8dd0-9376325a31d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $5,000 to Dalton. Other recipients [received](https://substack.com/redirect/a94d8913-863f-4262-84ed-0d3b6748059e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $10,000, including Rebecca Cooke, taking on Rep. Derrick Van Orden in WI-03, Jamie Ager, running for the NC-11 seat currently held by Rep. Chuck Edwards, and Bobby Pulido, challenging Rep. Monica De La Cruz in TX-15. And Johnny Garcia, running in TX-35 after Texas Republicans redrew it, has [taken home](https://substack.com/redirect/74d98841-c4fb-4cec-bca8-d474f8cca1f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the biggest slice of the pie among Blue Dog challengers at $12,500 in his contest against Carlos De La Cruz, the brother of the aforementioned congresswoman.
Blue Dog PAC raised a total of $2,196,255 this cycle, and has spent roughly $20,000 more than that. Blue Dog Action, on the other hand, has raised $7,267,677 and spent $6,852,972. As it stands, the Blue Dog Coalition only has 10 members remaining in Congress--Gluesenkamp Perez, Golden, Thompson and Gray, as well as Reps. Vicente Gonzalez, Luis Correa, Sanford Bishop, Jim Costa, Henry Cuellar, and Josh Gottheimer. Three of the ten are in competitive races, and Golden, of course, is leaving Congress.
"BDA PAC sent $225,000 to HMP within the last two weeks for HMP to support their general election activities, and I have encouraged BDA PAC's donors to give to HMP for general election spending on Blue Dog candidates. So I'm confident on the whole this cycle Blue Dog Action has more than done its part to support House Democrats in their work to win the majority," Gardner said.

And Johnny Garcia, running in TX-35 after Texas Republicans redrew it, has the biggest slice of the pie among Blue Dog challengers at $12,500 in his contest against Carlos De La Cruz, the brother of the aforementioned congresswoman. Blue Dog PAC raised a total of $2,196,255 this cycle, and has spent roughly $20,000 more than that. Blue Dog Action, on the other hand, has raised $7,267,677 and spent $6,852,972. As it stands, the Blue Dog Coalition only has 10 members remaining in Congress--Gluesenkamp Perez, Golden, Thompson and Gray, as well as Reps. Vicente Gonzalez, Luis Correa, Sanford Bishop, Jim Costa, Henry Cuellar, and Josh Gottheimer. Three of the ten are in competitive races, and Golden, of course, is leaving Congress. "BDA PAC sent $225,000 to HMP within the last two weeks for HMP to support their general election activities, and I have encouraged BDA PAC's donors to give to HMP for general election spending on Blue Dog candidates. So I'm confident on the whole this cycle Blue Dog Action has more than done its part to support House Democrats in their work to win the majority," Gardner said. As you lie in bed tonight, the house quiet and the day finally still, think about this: **_tomorrow you might wake up in a country that no longer has the majority that protects the things you care about most._** All of it can slip away _not because_ the other side suddenly became more popular, _but because_ **enough good people like you decided, just this once, that voting wasn’t quite important enough.**

The executive orders that secured the border, that cut the red tape, that put America first—those become nothing more than paper.
A single hostile committee, a single activist judge, a single speaker who hates everything we stand for, **and the progress stops.** The investigations start.
**The country you voted for in 2024 begins to unravel, not in some dramatic collapse, but in a thousand quiet votes you never cast.**
This is not just another midterm. This is the election that decides whether the America we reclaimed stays reclaimed or gets handed back, piece by piece, to the people who spent years trying to tear it down.
If we lose the majority, it will not be because patriots suddenly became Democrats. It will be because too many of us looked at the calendar, looked at the lines, looked at our own busy lives, and decided someone else would carry the load.

**There is no someone else.**
**There is only you.** ****

Hey, it's Troy.
I just opened a political fundraising email and was immediately hit with the line "DONATE NOW, TRUMP IS BEGGING YOU NOT TO".
So, let me take a moment to be honest with you: **that stuff is a load of sh*t**. Political fundraising emails are important for campaigns like ours to stay in touch with supporters like you and give you a **real** reason to donate to our cause.
### **So, let me tell you what 's real -- and happening right now in our battleground Senate race in Maine.**
* This race is neck and neck; in a recent poll, **I 'm trailing Susan Collins by just half a point.**
* Susan Collins and GOP mega-donors have spent nearly **$114 MILLION** to flood the airwaves with TV ads attacking me and boosting Collins.
* **In a race this close, Susan 's cash advantage alone could win it for her, securing Trump's Senate Majority.**

**Here 's my team's plan to beat Susan Collins:** We need to reach our $200,000 goal before midnight to supercharge our voter turnout operations. With Susan and her allies spending so much on the airwaves, we need a strong ground game to fight back and move undecided voters in our direction.
**[Election Day is tomorrow. So I 'm asking you right now: Can I count on you to chip in whatever you can before midnight so we can fully fund our voter turnout operations? I wouldn't ask if it weren't important, but without your support, we could lose to Susan and lose the Senate. ->](https://substack.com/redirect/de1801b1-447c-4189-a92f-5a3f6a44130c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

In solidarity,
Troy

MYTH #2: “It’s too late to chip in, so my donation won’t make a difference.” I’ll be working every single hour up until Election Day to reach every last undecided voter with my vision for Michigan, rally every last supporter to the polls, and defend myself against every last attack my opponent launches. That work won’t end until the polls close — and neither will the value of your donation. MYTH #3: “I can only chip in $1, and that won’t do anything for Jocelyn’s campaign.” We’re facing some of the biggest far-right spenders in the game, like Elon Musk and the DeVos family. Peter, there's a
lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted.

Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about
politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes.

I will not be distracted. Every minute spent talking about politicians is
a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working
Michiganders.

— This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good
at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.

— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to
“trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of
reach.

— And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide
control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a
check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate,
wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been
fleecing Michigan for decades.

Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.

Election Day is tomorrow. Several polls show us statistically tied with
Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes.

I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front
of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.

Friend,
As we near the end of this campaign, there's one thing I want you to hear from me today: _Thank you._
Supporters like you are the reason we have a chance to flip this U.S. Senate seat for the first time in nearly 100 years. Right now, the momentum is on our side - with experts like Nate Silver saying Kansas is the closest Senate race in the country. We're so close to doing what many thought was impossible, and I'm so full of hope. We can win this!
Here's the problem: Roger Marshall and his GOP super PAC allies have massively increased their ad buys against me. With more and more voters casting their ballots, we have to fight back before it's too late -- and right now, that means raising as much money as we can before tomorrow.
**Whether you 've been with us from the start or it's your first time donating, I'm asking if you can chip in one last donation to help me win in Kansas and flip this seat. Can I count on you?**
**Here 's the best link to give: [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/hamilton-substack-donate](https://substack.com/redirect/7f6be4c5-294b-41da-81bc-4c740ef8ccdb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

* **Leader response:** Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei ordered armed forces to meet any threat with an immediate, unrestricted response.
* **Market lift:** Lower oil helped stock futures rebound as investors returned to risk assets following last week's tech selloff.

# [North Korea steals $6.4B from Binance in 20 minutes then $3.6B flees](https://substack.com/redirect/34b7fb45-350e-441f-9458-020b1ce34958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Binance logged **[$3.64 billion in net outflows,](https://substack.com/redirect/d93a745c-a901-499b-85fa-63624a8418fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d93a745c-a901-499b-85fa-63624a8418fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)about 2.1% of its $171 billion in assets, after reopening withdrawals following its record $6.3 billion hack that the[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/34496bd6-55b1-4e05-a2b3-7d1a38024000?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[FBI blamed on North Korea.](https://substack.com/redirect/34496bd6-55b1-4e05-a2b3-7d1a38024000?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34b7fb45-350e-441f-9458-020b1ce34958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Hack scale:** The theft, attributed by the FBI to North K**[orean hackers under the TraderTraitor operation,](https://substack.com/redirect/ea079627-d0f8-4273-9717-82acb6a8fdbc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** ranks as the largest crypto heist on record.
* **Coverage status:** Binance said it has replenished roughly 95% of the stolen amount using company funds and will absorb the remaining impact rather than pass losses to users.
* **Withdrawal pace:** Most of the net outflows occurred in the first hours after phased resumption began Sunday; volumes later stabilized.
* **Market reaction:** Bitcoin held near $78,000 as the exchange restored access across networks, with some less liquid tokens still limited.

# [Marvell drops $115B bomb on Lumentum to own AI's optical future](https://substack.com/redirect/34b7fb45-350e-441f-9458-020b1ce34958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Marvell **[agreed to buy optical-parts maker Lumentum](https://substack.com/redirect/cb54d60d-04b8-4661-9ef6-20181c5be4fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** in an all-stock deal with an implied $115 billion enterprise value, positioning the combined company as[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/609d1c46-d183-46a7-b9f4-ce9f62c41acd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[a leader in AI data-center connectivity.](https://substack.com/redirect/609d1c46-d183-46a7-b9f4-ce9f62c41acd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/34b7fb45-350e-441f-9458-020b1ce34958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Deal terms:** Lumentum shareholders receive 4.5 Marvell shares for each of theirs, with the transaction expected to close in the first half of 2028.
* **CEO framing:** Matt Murphy called the move a once-in-a-generation opportunity as AI infrastructure shifts toward optical connectivity.
* **Share reaction:** Both stocks fell in premarket trading, with Marvell down about 3% and Lumentum about 4% below the implied deal value.
* **Strategic context:** The acquisition expands Marvell's optical reach for chips used to train and run large language models amid ongoing AI infrastructure spending.

# [Speculators dump $19.5B in gold as it smashes through $4,000](https://substack.com/redirect/34b7fb45-350e-441f-9458-020b1ce34958?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Gold broke below $4,000 support as Goldman data showed **[speculators sold $19.5 billion of futures](https://substack.com/redirect/ba5d7783-a3f6-421a-88c5-166885383836?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** over five straight weeks, marking the metal's worst October since 2008.

---|---|---
* **Liquidation scale:** Speculators net sold $8 billion in the latest week alone, the fifth consecutive week of selling since late September.
* **Positioning note:** Falling real yields failed to support prices, and "Other" accounts still hold gross longs above their two-year median.
* **Technical test:** The metal hit its 100-week moving average; further support sits near $3,800 and the long-term trendline.
* **Hedge performance:** Gold has **[declined even as equity volatility rose,](https://substack.com/redirect/bd35521d-8134-4e94-8a7a-3b1e7c80b2d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/bd35521d-8134-4e94-8a7a-3b1e7c80b2d0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)underscoring its limited reliability as a stress hedge in the current tape.

* **Abu Dhabi activity:** Altman met the crown prince and signed four agreements that include AI tools for government and energy operations.
* **PR move:** The company is reportedly considering[ ](https://open.substack.com/pub/thecapitalistmag/p/capitalist-insider-gen-z-fragrance?r=8bxo8n&utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web&showWelcomeOnShare=true)**[rebranding data centers as"AI compute campuses"](https://open.substack.com/pub/thecapitalistmag/p/capitalist-insider-gen-z-fragrance?r=8bxo8n&utm_campaign=post&utm_medium=web&showWelcomeOnShare=true)** to soften public resistance.
* **Usage limits:** OpenAI also tightened ChatGPT and Codex limits as infrastructure costs remain elevated.

subject: Your plan tomorrow
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Clark for Wisconsin Clark for Wisconsin
body:
Polls open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. Here’s everything you need.| | |
---
---
Friend,

Tomorrow, the people of Wisconsin’s 7th District decide who represents us in Congress.

I've spent these last 13 months on the road, listening to people across this district and making the case for a New Northwoods: a place where our kids can build a future close to home. Now it comes down to one day, and to whether we show up.

So let’s make a plan right now. It takes two minutes:

**When:** Tuesday, November 3, 7 a.m. to 8 p.m. If you’re in line by 8:00, you get to vote. Stay in line.

**Where:** Look up your polling place at [myvote.wi.gov](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142765684/657959680/-573865443?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjEwMzAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjgzNTI0ZDUtZWVkNi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=A9uu_CFyrhO7JkiJv8pwN_2wDMxVcRDC7zXkeoEKY0c=&emci=90d3423e-d5d6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=283524d5-eed6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=28718937). On Election Day, you have to vote at your assigned polling place, so check it even if you think you know.

**What to bring:** A photo ID, such as a Wisconsin driver license or state ID, a U.S. passport, a military ID, or a tribal ID.

**Moved, or not registered yet?** You can register at your polling place on Election Day. Bring proof of residence that shows your current name and address. An electronic copy on your phone works.

**Still have an absentee ballot at home?** It’s too late to mail it. It has to be received by 8 p.m. Tuesday. Go to [myvote.wi.gov](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142765685/657959682/-573865443?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjEwMzAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMjgzNTI0ZDUtZWVkNi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=A9uu_CFyrhO7JkiJv8pwN_2wDMxVcRDC7zXkeoEKY0c=&emci=90d3423e-d5d6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=283524d5-eed6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=28718937) or call your municipal clerk to find out how to return it where you live.

Then do one more thing: pick a time, and tell someone you’re going. People who make a plan are much more likely to follow through.

This race is close, and it will be decided by the people who show up. Let’s make sure that’s us.

See you on the other side,
Fred Clark

subject: Hey
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Pramila for Congress
body:
Peter, there's a
lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted.

Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about
politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes.

I will not be distracted. Every minute spent talking about politicians is
a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working
Michiganders.

— This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good
at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.

— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to
“trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of
reach.

— And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide
control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a
check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate,
wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been
fleecing Michigan for decades.

Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.

Election Day is Tuesday. Several polls show us statistically tied with
Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes.

I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front
of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.

With love and gratitude,
Laura Ciscomani

clean_body: | | | | Thank you | Ciscomani for Congress | Dear Friends, As we head into Election Day on Tuesday, I wanted to take a moment to reach out personally and say THANK YOU. From the very beginning of this journey, so many of you have stood by Juan and our family. Not just during this election cycle, but for years. Through every campaign, every challenge, and every victory, your friendship, encouragement, and unwavering support have meant more to us than you will ever know. Most importantly,thank you for the prayers you have lifted up for Juan, our children, and our family. We have felt them, and they have carried us through some of the busiest and most challenging moments. We are truly blessed to have such an incredible community surrounding us. Now, with Election Day just two days away, we have one final push! I have three simple asks: 🇺🇸 1\. VOTE ON TUESDAY! If you haven't already voted, please make your voice heard on November 3rd. And reach out to THREE friends or family members to remind them to vote, too! Every single vote matters. 🇺🇸 2\. HELP US ON ELECTION DAY! If you have a little time on Tuesday, we would love your help greeting voters at the polls. Even an hour or two makes a difference! [[SIGN UP TO BE A POLL GREETER]]() 🇺🇸 3\. CELEBRATE WITH US TUESDAY NIGHT! Please join our family and Team Ciscomani for our Election Night Watch Party. We would love nothing more than to spend the evening surrounded by the people who have made this journey so special. [[WATCH PARTY DETAILS / RSVP]]() I know how much time, energy, and heart so many of you have poured into this effort. body:
It all comes down to this.| | | |
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142767040/657963746/-642992695?refcode=261102em_sjj_ee-gotv&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3N2JmMzBiMy1lZmQ2LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cZXgLO0DPhU8p4ZqU2rKf3XjqhvUdEcdT1rIVPlKBlU=)
---
Hi friends — before the big day that we’ve all been waiting for arrives, I want to take a minute to share with you some of what I’ve heard out on the campaign trail over the past year. I’ve spent hours upon hours around San Diego and in battleground districts across the country talking to volunteers and voters about this election — and even though I’ve talked to so many different people, what I’ve heard has been very similar: _I’m fired up to flip the House._ _I’m pissed off and ready to hold this administration accountable._ _I’m so worried about our future._ _I’m concerned about our democracy._ _I just want groceries to cost less._ _I’m doing this for my daughter._ _I’m doing this for my neighbor. _ From town to town and state to state, it is clear that people are full of righteous anger, fed up with Donald Trump and the Republican Party, and energized to make a difference on Tuesday. I feel all these same feelings, and I’m honored that people take the time to share them with me. And as we head into the most important Election Day of our lifetimes, I have one request for you: channel those feelings into _one last bit of action_ before polls close tomorrow. Call a friend. Text a neighbor. Message a high school friend on social media. Join a virtual phone bank. Whatever it is, _do something_ that helps get us across the finish line.
* Today I’m joining my friends at SD Dems for a GOTV canvass at 3pm to get out the vote for me and Henry Foster, who’s up for re-election to the City Council in District 4. [Join me by signing up online!](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142767041/657963747/-379830340?refcode=261102em_sjj_ee-gotv&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3N2JmMzBiMy1lZmQ2LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cZXgLO0DPhU8p4ZqU2rKf3XjqhvUdEcdT1rIVPlKBlU=&emci=8816b3d5-ead6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=77bf30b3-efd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14239920)

* You can also check out the [DCCC Mobilize page](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142767042/657963748/134262480?refcode=261102em_sjj_ee-gotv&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3N2JmMzBiMy1lZmQ2LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cZXgLO0DPhU8p4ZqU2rKf3XjqhvUdEcdT1rIVPlKBlU=&emci=8816b3d5-ead6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=77bf30b3-efd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14239920) for lots of virtual events to join from anywhere.

* And if you just don’t have time to volunteer, [consider chipping in](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142767043/657963749/-642992695?refcode=261102em_sjj_ee-gotv&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjEvMS84OTMxMyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3N2JmMzBiMy1lZmQ2LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cZXgLO0DPhU8p4ZqU2rKf3XjqhvUdEcdT1rIVPlKBlU=) to fund the final push of GOTV work on the ground.

You’ll never regret taking one more action in this critical moment, but you may always regret _not_ doing it. Thank you for reading and for everything you do. I’m so grateful to be doing this important work together. -Sara

clean_body: It all comes down to this.| | | | = Hi friends — before the big day that we’ve all been waiting for arrives, I want to take a minute to share with you some of what I’ve heard out on the campaign trail over the past year. I’ve spent hours upon hours around San Diego and in battleground districts across the country talking to volunteers and voters about this election — and even though I’ve talked to so many different people, what I’ve heard has been very similar: I’m fired up to flip the House. I’m pissed off and ready to hold this administration accountable. I’m so worried about our future. I’m concerned about our democracy. I just want groceries to cost less. I’m doing this for my daughter. I’m doing this for my neighbor. From town to town and state to state, it is clear that people are full of righteous anger, fed up with Donald Trump and the Republican Party, and energized to make a difference on Tuesday. I feel all these same feelings, and I’m honored that people take the time to share them with me. And as we head into the most important Election Day of our lifetimes, I have one request for you: channel those feelings into one last bit of action before polls close tomorrow. Call a friend. Text a neighbor. Message a high school friend on social media. Join a virtual phone bank. Whatever it is, do something that helps get us across the finish line. Today I’m joining my friends at SD Dems for a GOTV canvass at 3pm to get out the vote for me and Henry Foster, who’s up for re-election to the City Council in District 4. You can also check out the for lots of virtual events to join from anywhere. * And if you just don’t have time to volunteer, = to fund the final push of GOTV work on the ground. You’ll never regret taking one more action in this critical moment, but you may always regret not doing it. Thank you for reading and for everything you do. Hillsdale College's popular online course, **" The Genesis Story: Reading Biblical Narratives,"** is now FREE on DVD.

In this six-lecture course, you'll explore some of the major themes of Genesis, including the complex relationship between God and man, and what it reveals about divine and human nature.

"The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text.

The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education.

Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation.

You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph.

This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs.

clean_body: I hope you're having a good day. I'm writing with some exciting news. | | | | | Monday, November 2, 2026 This sponsored message from The Flyover is on behalf of Hillsdale College | | | | | | Dear Fellow American, I hope you're having a good day. I'm writing with some exciting news. Hillsdale College's popular online course, " The Genesis Story: Reading Biblical Narratives," is now FREE on DVD. In this six-lecture course, you'll explore some of the major themes of Genesis, including the complex relationship between God and man, and what it reveals about divine and human nature. "The Genesis Story" is taught by Hillsdale College professor of English Justin Jackson, who has taught the subject to undergraduate students here at the College for 15 years. This course aims to deepen a student's theological understanding of the Old Testament by revealing the literary beauty and complexity of the text. The course begins with a lecture and introduction by the president of Hillsdale College, Larry P. Arnn, in which he explains why we teach the Book of Genesis at Hillsdale College and why it's important to both faith and higher education. Then, Dr. Jackson explains the four relationships that dominate the Book of Genesis: God and creation, God and man, man and man, and man and creation. You'll explore these relationships in the narratives of Adam and Eve, Abraham and Sarah, Abraham and Isaac, Jacob and Esau, and finally, Joseph. This course on DVD is perfect for viewing in your home with your family or for use in small groups such as Bible studies and book clubs. To receive your FREE Genesis DVD box set, please use the secure link here: Warm regards, Bill Gray, '01 Vice President Institutional Advancement Hillsdale College | The Flyover, LLC 1910 Thomes Ave. Cheyenne, WY 82001-3527 | ---|---

name: Dan Rayfield
subject: The most consequential midterm of our lives
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Dan Rayfield PAC ID #14046
body:
Democrats need our help | |

| | [ ](https://us.list-manage.com/16zdj_nEX3P?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)
---
| | Peter,

This week's election could be the most consequential midterm of our lives.

Up and down the ballot, candidates who are aligned with Donald Trump are running on implementing a version of his far-right agenda here in Oregon.

And I'll be blunt: _**their campaigns are doing better than they ought to be. **_

While other states will likely see a large shift in momentum for Democrats, as it stands, Oregon could see something different.

Peter, elections are how we hold our government and politicians accountable, and we can't miss this opportunity to elect leaders who will fight Trump's extremism and stand up for Oregonians.

[**With so many voters waiting for Election Day to cast their ballot, our team can still make a difference for Democrats in competitive races across our state. Can you chip in what you can today to help?**](https://us.list-manage.com/Yf8WlSQK6DL?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)
---
| [CHIP IN](https://us.list-manage.com/10E1uPyiYlc?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260 "CHIP IN")
---
| In service,
Dan Rayfield
---
| | | | Since taking office as Oregon’s Attorney General in 2025, Dan Rayfield has focused on protecting Oregon’s working families and homegrown small businesses by taking on pharmaceutical companies, polluters, and large corporations driving up costs for groceries and other everyday needs. He’s been fighting hard to block the Trump Administration from taking away the rights of Oregonians, suing Trump–and winning–dozens of times.

[ ](https://us.list-manage.com/14479MMnky4?e=1768325bd4&c2id=0fcd3a526fabf816bd24466788989260)

Dan grew up in Oregon and is a product of the Oregon public school system. Following his graduation from Tigard High School, Dan attended Western Oregon University and then earned his law degree from Willamette University College of Law. In 2005, prior to his law school graduation, he clerked for the Benton County District Attorney’s office. During his time at the District Attorney’s office, he gained his first trial experience prosecuting DUIs and other misdemeanor charges. Dan has also served as a coach attorney for the OSU Mock Trial Team, a former Linn County Peer Court Judge, and Past President of the Linn-Benton Bar Association.

Since 2015, Dan served as the State Representative for Oregon House District 16, which encompasses the cities of Corvallis and Philomath, and Oregon State University. In 2022, he was elected by his colleagues to serve as Speaker of the House. Over that time, he helped lead the way on issues including a high quality education for our children, access to affordable and reliable healthcare, making sure families are able to earn a living wage while simultaneously nurturing innovation and supporting Oregon’s small businesses, and making our public safety system more effective and accountable. Dan lives in Corvallis with his wife Amanda and their son Adam.

**Prefer to donate via mail? Address a check to:**

Friends of Dan Rayfield
PO Box 42307
Portland, OR 97242
