Republican Senate candidate Mike Rogers, a Republican who is running for the U.S. Senate in Michigan, speaks to reporters on November 1. Photo by Dominic Gwinn/SOPA Images/LightRocket via Getty Images.
_Story by Tom Perkins_
Mike Rogers, the Republican candidate for U.S. Senate in Michigan, earned over $420,000 during his tenure as a board member for a consultancy that is now helping Pete Hegseth plan the next phase of the disastrous Iran war, according to tax filings.
The MITRE Corporation is coordinating the controversial [Project Meridian: "The Future of Warfare,"](https://substack.com/redirect/08294504-5718-4ece-9c3d-d3cbf7bf71b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) which is bringing together weapons manufacturers and tech leaders like Elon Musk to map out the future of U.S. warfare in Iran and beyond. Some have [raised questions](https://substack.com/redirect/e5dfdda0-1dbe-4fd3-a2a4-5d151bed6ded?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over [conflicts of interest](https://substack.com/redirect/956be041-b509-4982-993b-a07609f26524?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) among those leading the project.
Rogers, an establishment war hawk and former member of Congress, served on MITRE's board of trustees, including a stint as its chair, for six years through 2023. He left as he launched his first campaign for U.S. Senate during the 2024 election. The company's CEO said Rogers was brought on for his "vast national security expertise," and [IRS records detail](https://substack.com/redirect/de1c2485-1f6d-401a-abdf-4687d8f9a8ca?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his annual earnings.
Rogers' support for the operation in Iran has been a liability throughout the race against his opponent, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.KEbZfzhQmi3PAzjrhXf-1bCxfVIyXW9num1Fw4c0YGM?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=223212774)
"People say, well, 'What date is it going to end?' It shouldn't be a date. It should be conditional," Rogers [told a right wing podcast host](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc6e332-ea7b-465e-8c7f-1d793329cced?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in March. "This is why Americans need to stop for a minute, come together and say, 'let's get this done, get it done right.'"
The war is among the drivers of stubborn, ongoing inflation and high gas prices, and [polls show](https://substack.com/redirect/da710dc0-5f32-46f8-b89a-3e2f32c61d30?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) as many as 67% of Michigan voters disapprove of it. El-Sayed has hammered Rogers over his support for endless wars, and Rogers in recent weeks [waffled](https://substack.com/redirect/fc646eef-36ff-408c-9cae-7e8c620a5571?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on the operation in Iran, telling Fox News that "we need to start wrapping it down."
The El-Sayed and Rogers campaigns did not respond to requests for comment.
Secretary of War Pete Hegseth on Sept. 30[ announced](https://substack.com/redirect/08294504-5718-4ece-9c3d-d3cbf7bf71b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the MITRE-led Project Meridian as "an effort led by America's best minds to study the future of warfare." Hegseth named Musk, former Republican Speaker of the House Newt Gingrich, and Palmer Luckey, founder of defense technology company Anduril Industries, as top officials.
Former defense officials [noted to NPR](https://substack.com/redirect/956be041-b509-4982-993b-a07609f26524?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that the project's leaders could guide the U.S. to build more space assets or rely more on drones that Musk's and Luckey's companies produce, while making fewer tanks or other military equipment that they do not make. Musk is [among Rogers' largest supporters](https://substack.com/redirect/d51dc4a4-fe06-4f84-b55a-4a31fdb902f6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), backing him via the America PAC that Musk finances.
"There are a lot of issues impacting this race, but everyone understands that the Iran war is a primary reason for the high cost of gasoline and diesel," said Bernie Porn, a Michigan pollster who found El-Sayed [with a small lead over Rogers](https://substack.com/redirect/b63677de-8e59-40b6-8372-68c9429d12fd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in late August. "And that is why you see states like Iowa and Kansas in play, so this is one more thing to tie Rogers to support for the Iran war."
_Tom Perkins is a freelance reporter in Detroit who covers the antiwar movement locally and nationally._

Hi there, it's Michele Tafoya!

If I were to take a guess, there's a 50/50 chance you may recognize me from a stadium's big screen.
If that's not the case, I get it... Let me at least tell you briefly about who I am and what I'm about anyway!

I should clarify first, no, I didn't make my career running for touchdowns or kicking game-winning field goals.

I worked as a sideline reporter in professional football for nearly three decades. Working in the sport for that long was a dream come true, and I wouldn't have wanted it any other way.
[Believe me, I know plenty of people who called me crazy for walking away from a career I loved. But life is short, and I was not willing to sit on the sidelines while everything I care about was on the line.](http://links.justandfreegop.com/u/click?_t=8ca5ef3d31cc43bcb1fbe6968d953911&_m=d44325311cf546e9a00ea5e01461d7d7&_e=A-zKp-HIr-OU8CN4Euk3PGX4sUHOhanl7fWTQIDasL7Sk2EpzaYfQyw6Ra78ssyteYG5y7WToFsIiyI4r9ZrUYU1oVcGKKQrg5k_DtQHwPEmP5P6wLEKxAcG5PlfNz6Ed58uI1IWJn5_TcEzgXBK4ZgKh0t7r9qqkz79XC5efPLn59byACBcbSddHmDPF7TCmq7vdusjXzHWXrI1eiLPDKTBl3KCSj4med2wUl0C8tBmZS9xxP6DgmnmJwYOkWfal8ieF1sgvikucBkGoHn06D7DrZVX5wRajCZYsPRUU5LuNObEPjPXgX2857vpPTI3nGF6J1wpwcPuKXNgEQ-b7Sm_1H6khS8SoNeRpv-LydrWTLCNqmQnpdLBLUXWaP7GfUgbuQZcVIXuuFhN_pCqXBWe-Am3iWyx9KjXw8Sk_bhW3Ov7Isn9N8wFO3c4cRcYYtqDc9e3TG91DO9hfnC19B0jUsk2yJ-SczJSszzhjAi06qa-uEFSRstwmmt7FRmDytZhdsSvJNsB65H5woisupv8c0WiXmpOf_JrPd5SrnVX3RqclyHBBLDEKBjk-vipbCD0YQd97Nszjkby8I53rHE_sS_k3xP4RcRviGwADQiQ8dmDbGZ7QUBvd-tX-MMQT7IzB9hwXtmnjuZn5zHPzcCQinwmoDo4Iqkgd7wBw_nK23_FMROvOe7-j1OzJQhNI2_xdF7WCGwuITbPjp2dFsISD2uQy-XZkScDkO7Fv3fMdk774GhZzeTX1mVJ8ytJaL9vYstrDOvSgOAcyvcyVuSy_nwsAaUMuNLr4OMUuLgIjVWzFRhtk7m4cXQkQ7_6rFsKKWqFMCXijhPL1yOUMVkHMH5zjbvY6I9Io35YjrDFXzsSdPTUnyYyk6g2bcPqrkLfjgSgZ_y9tu2dcUw4GExhChXCxW7HQNQ89Zp_LNF1q5v6Y6fcyi9F_VIwLgunpksSJrNiuerkTzyEeFfQgk9t2cxMEg6ql26WKFCq286ckQLKta88VasfTfI-RT9S)
I told myself before I officially launched my race for U.S. Senate that we had to be all in or not do it at all.

I burned the boats, Patriot, and there's absolutely no looking back.
I will not be canceled. I will not apologize for values that are wholesome and good. And if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, that is exactly why I did it.

I want my daughter and every young American to know one thing:
You earn your place. You think for yourself. And you never let anyone put you in a box. That's the Minnesota I'm fighting for.
Parents who speak up are called transphobes.Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet.And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
This is not complicated.
Girls' sports are for girls, and boys' sports are for boys.

The radical Left has done everything in its power to infiltrate some of the most vulnerable minds in our society. I launched this run because just like you, I'm sick of the indoctrination and want to bring back sanity to our country.

| | | There's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted.Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes. **I will not be distracted.** Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders. — This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it. — This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach. — And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades. Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.Election Day is tomorrow. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. We can’t be distracted.Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes. I will not be distracted. Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders. — This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it. — This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach. — And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades. Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.Election Day is tomorrow. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes. I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now. = = Let them have the drama. Let us earn the votes. If conservatives turn out in November, we'll win every critical battleground and lay the groundwork for victory in 2028 and beyond.

That's why Turning Point Action is focusing all our efforts on three key states: Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire.

**We call these states the new RED WALL.**

_Let us explain why they matter so much... _

After 2024, Charlie looked at the numbers, looked at the maps, and told our team something simple. If we lock down Arizona, Nevada, and New Hampshire, the Left's entire strategy falls apart. Their map collapses. Their path back to power disappears.

Whoever wins in 2028 controls the 2030 Census. The Census drives redistricting. Redistricting sets the congressional map for the next ten years.

This midterm decides which way that goes.

Now, Republican strategists are even admitting it too. One strategist aligned with Trump recently told Politico : “Ohio is going to be your bellwether of what kind of night it is ... I think – I do truly think – as Ohio goes, the Senate goes right now.” This race will set the stage, and we have two options before us: We can join together, flip Ohio’s must-win seat, and take back the Senate. Or, we can take our foot off the gas in this final sprint, let Husted win, and cede control of the Senate to the GOP until 2029 at least. I know what I choose, but I can’t win this fight alone. = I’m so grateful to have your support, Peter. Thank you. body:
Here's what we've been up to over the past week:
| | |
---
| | Monday, November 2

## THE RUSSO REPORT

From the Desk of Allison Russo
---
| |
---
| | [](https://zhwrg7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001yBGQUs51aeiAVHoK8Yi-tJ7DFNWYjZ96V78BFEx-NYYZptSHSKZ1U1mEhpbhgBuTA9ZrfD1GSRsDX6lYQTPWZ8dgLrOOQr6FUNHsnQQ0e5d7ImSOE_txkJToJjFemVSQUAhY5xUBoo8U4GSZigQLfQ==&c=brn7fM5PdJqSBqepRsswMmQJsbejtKHKc8zjIbmjRBoDF8_Mg8mfCQ==&ch=hZ3puKGBP-1roG98K9kVcj34vnWMiwDZbxdHOLIF-xbakMW8WVO3Tg==)
---
| A Note from Allison
Friends,
As we wrap up Election Day Eve, I wanted to step back from the campaign noise for a moment and write to you simply as your neighbor and friend.
Running for statewide office and serving in the legislature is an intense journey, but what keeps me grounded every single day are the real, human interactions we share across our communities.
It's the conversations in driveways, the coffee shop chats, the parents sharing their honest worries about their kids' schools, and the neighbors stopping me at the grocery store to share a quick word of encouragement.
---
| Those moments aren't just bullet points on a campaign platform to me--they are the heart of why I do this.
We talk a lot in politics about big bills, policy platforms, and votes, but at the end of the day, this work is about people. It's about ensuring our kids have strong support systems, our families don't have to choose between financial stability and healthcare, and every person in our community feels heard and valued in our democracy.
This Tuesday, the decision belongs entirely to you.
If you haven't cast your vote yet, please make your plan today. Talk to your family, check in with a neighbor who might need a ride to the polls, and make sure your voice is part of shaping what comes next.
No matter what the headlines say over the next few days, I want to say a heartfelt thank you. Thank you for opening your doors to me, for sharing your stories, and for caring so deeply about the place we all call home. It is a profound privilege to walk alongside you. Let's finish this together.
Warmly,
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Week in Review
---
| On Monday, Allison was able to stop in Mansfield for a "Labor Night at the Movies" event, where she joined Mid-Ohio Area Labor Council President Norm Shoemaker. As you know, Allison's commitment to labor runs deep, and so it was a real pleasure to speak with these union members about the stakes in this election and making sure they have a plan to vote!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Wednesday was up to Northeast Ohio. Allison was in Twinsburg and Hudson supporting the re-election of Congresswoman Emilia Sykes and a chance to break the Ohio House supermajority with Samantha Salamon!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Thursday it was over to Sidney in Shelby County for a press conference with John Kulewicz as the Republican's "Bus Tour" was passing through. Don't worry, our speakers were loud enough that they heard us loud and clear!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Friday we were thrilled to join our ticketmates Justice Jennifer Brunner, Mayor Annette Blackwell, and Councilman John Kulewicz for a series of campaign stops. First up was Lima with a stop at the Democratic Party headquarters. No trip to Lima is complete without grabbing a burger at Kewpee! Next up was a meet and greet in Marion along with a quick stop to record a radio show with Scott Spears. Finally, everyone ended together in Mansfield with a packed house on a Friday night at the local IBEW. People are fired up and ready to FINALLY make change in this state!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
Saturday morning Allison kicked off a canvass in Dayton with Kristina Knickerbocker and the Dayton-Miami Valley AFL-CIO. Then it was back up to Columbus for a GOTV rally with Congresswoman Joyce Beatty, Amy Acton, and Sherrod Brown! Allison closed out the day by visiting the Franklin County Board of Elections to meet people as they were heading in to vote.
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| To round out the week, Allison joined her colleague, Senator Hearcel Craig for church service at First Church of God in Columbus. Bishop Timothy J. Clarke delivered an inspiring and joyful sermon, and it was an honor to be welcomed for it. After service it was up to Canton for a candidate rally with candidates up and down the ticket. Finally, Allison made her way up to Cleveland for the Sherrod Brown and Amy Acton rally!
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| |
---
| On Election Day Eve, tonight ends right back where it started: in Columbus for the final rally with our statewide ticket! We're ready to win this, Ohio!

| |

Hi, there's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted.

Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes.

**I will not be distracted.** Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders.

— This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.

— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach.

— And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades.

Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.

Election Day is tomorrow. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes.

**I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.**

body:

Hi Peter, it’s Julia Louis-Dreyfus.
You might know me as Selina Meyer on Veep, a politician who would say or do absolutely anything to hold on to power. _It made for great television._
But, Peter, what’s happening in Wisconsin right now isn’t a comedy.
I’m not willing to sit back and watch MAGA billionaires buy a governor’s mansion, and I don’t think you are either. **[Will you stand with Wisconsin Democrats and Tammy Baldwin right now and chip in $10 to help elect David Crowley?](https://act.tammybaldwin.com/go/6072?c0=em-ms-tb-20261102-surrogate.rtA3im&refcode=em20261102-5801&t=2&akid=5801%2E35263%2EwRheYW)**

**First:** Tom Tiffany, a 2020 election denier, is running for governor of Wisconsin.
**Then:** The Uihlein family and Diane Hendricks have given his campaign more than $34 million, and Elon Musk is spending big here too.

David Crowley and Wisconsin Democrats have real grassroots power, _and it’s the one thing Tom Tiffany’s donors can’t buy._

body:
What you can still do...

View this email in your browser (https://mailchi.mp/andyfornevada/friday-weekly-5860253?e=6736d7bc47)
https://secure.anedot.com/andyfornevada/email-launch

Dear
Peter,
This past week, I had the pleasure of joining guest host Sam Peters on The Wayne Allyn Root show to discuss my campaign for Assembly District 37.

We covered a lot of ground during the interview, including the coming fight over tax increases, the Democrats’ dangerous attacks on our brave men and women in law enforcement and how they’re undermining our public safety, and the importance of rebuilding Nevada’s economy in a way that promotes economic liberty and prosperity.

Above all, we talked about what’s at stake this November — the competing visions between myself and my left-wing opponent, and why winning this race is so important to breaking the Democrats’ stranglehold on our state legislature.

I hope you’ll click below to take a listen ... and as always, I’d love any feedback or comments you’d like to provide!
https://andyfornevada.com/andy-matthews_sam-peters_8-28-20/
***

By the way, I was also honored this week to receive the endorsement of the National Rifle Association. I’ve long been a proud champion of the Second Amendment, and it’s an absolute thrill to have the support of our nation’s preeminent defender of the right to bear arms.

Especially today, with Nevada’s Democrats waging a relentless assault on our Second Amendment rights (for her part, my opponent received an “F” grade from the NRA), it’s more important than ever that we elect those who will unapologetically defend our Constitution. And you can count on me to do exactly that in Carson City.

For Nevada’s future,

Andy

Prices rose half a percent in September alone. Whoever wins tomorrow,
that number stays.

[https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e16124167/UaHR0cHM6Ly93cm8ubnVjbGV1c2VtYWlsLmNvbS9hbXBsaWZ5L3YvTkM0SlBYWEtmTg/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDI/LbmNsckdCQ2xNWQ/qP2hpZHM9bmNQRVhJRHh5aEt3elJsc10/gaujw2A/s3mb46ffb8a

YOUR IRA & 401(K) ISN'T ON THE BALLOT

Tomorrow you help pick who goes to (or stays in) Washington. One thing
isn't on your ballot: what your money buys.

Government figures out Thursday show prices rose half a percent in
September alone, and 3.6% over the past year.

When prices climb, the dollars in your savings buy a little less food,
a little less at the pharmacy, a little less of everything you live
on.

[Two grocery bags with prescription bottles on a kitchen table. A
label reading $100 in 2016 points to the left bag, full of bread,
apples, bananas and greens, with three pill bottles in front. A red
label reading Same $100 today: about $72 worth points to the right
bag, which holds much less, with two pill bottles. Caption: Your $100
from 2016 now buys about $72 worth.] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e16124167/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDI/LbmNsckdCQ2xNWQ/gaujw2A/s1n6ce067e6

Even Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said last week that when Americans look
around,

_"...THEY SEE THE PRICES ARE UP."_
Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh

If you're retired, no boss hands you a raise to catch up. Your savings
just have to stretch further.

You can't vote on prices. But you can decide how your savings are
spread out [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e16124167/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXS4/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDI/LbmNsckdCQ2xNWQ/gaujw2A/sdkfff342da

That's why savers near or in retirement can diversify part of their
savings into physical gold and silver.

From 1973 to 1979, when prices rose about 9% a year, gold rose about
35% a year. Silver soared too.

[Bar chart of average yearly rise from 1973 to 1979: prices rose
8.8% a year, gold rose 35% a year. Past performance is not a promise
of future results.] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e16124167/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDI/LbmNsckdCQ2xNWQ/gaujw2A/s1n6ce067e6

That's history, not a promise. Gold and silver have rough stretches
too, be very wary of anyone who says otherwise.

But through that long stretch of rising prices, gold and silver held
what money buys.

The free 2026 Ultimate Guide to Gold & Silver shows how you can add
gold & silver to your retirement savings (tax & penalty free) in three
simple steps.

It comes from Goldco, which has helped Americans protect their
retirement savings with gold and silver for over 14 years, earning
more than 8,000 - 5 star reviews, and an A+ rating from the Better
Business Bureau.

The guide is 100% free, available right now, and you can get it by
clicking here [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e16124167/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXTo/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDI/LbmNsckdCQ2xNWQ/gaujw2A/s9i54524311

[The 2026 Ultimate Guide to Gold & Silver from Goldco, shown as a

Goldco folder] [https://link.email.america1stwarroom.com/click/e16124167/UaHR0cHM6Ly9saW5rLmdvbGRjby5jb20vNTVwXQ/SZW1haWxfYW1lcmljYU9ORXN0d2Fycm9vbV9jb20yNjExMDI/LbmNsckdCQ2xNWQ/gaujw2A/s1n6ce067e6

Get The FREE 2026 Ultimate Guide to Gold & Silver Now →

Tomorrow, polls open across the country for Election Day. Here in Pennsylvania, voting will be underway between the hours of 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. | ⚠️ If you are in line to vote between those hours, stay in line! So long as you have been waiting since before 8 p.m., you will be allowed to cast your ballot.
---
We want to make sure you have all the information you need to cast your ballot tomorrow, so read on for our Pennsylvania voter guide, or forward this email to share it with a friend!
**VOTER REGISTRATION:** If you want to cast your ballot tomorrow, you need to be registered to vote. Check your voter registration by clicking **[here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142771404/657979017/88266837?source=JS_EM_FR_110226_B1_Plan&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3MTMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiM2U2YWEwNzctZmJkNi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=bbyEn7HpUDmssRLT_Q3TDYPkywZlGJBriY_lBtNjca8=&emci=a487ee70-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=3e6aa077-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14629434)**.
**WHERE TO VOTE:** To find your designated polling place, you can click **[here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142771405/657979018/364851138?source=JS_EM_FR_110226_B1_Plan&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3MTMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiM2U2YWEwNzctZmJkNi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=bbyEn7HpUDmssRLT_Q3TDYPkywZlGJBriY_lBtNjca8=&emci=a487ee70-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=3e6aa077-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14629434)** and enter your address.
⚠️ If this is your first time voting, make sure you bring a valid form of ID. You can see a list of accepted forms **[here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142771406/657979019/1766602680?source=JS_EM_FR_110226_B1_Plan&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3MTMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiM2U2YWEwNzctZmJkNi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=bbyEn7HpUDmssRLT_Q3TDYPkywZlGJBriY_lBtNjca8=&emci=a487ee70-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=3e6aa077-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14629434)**.
---
**ACCESSIBILITY:** If you need assistance voting due to a disability, you have several options. Every polling place in Pennsylvania has at least one accessible voting system and if you need help voting at the polling place, you are allowed to bring a person of your choice with you to assist you. Click **[here](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142771407/657979020/354469551?source=JS_EM_FR_110226_B1_Plan&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNTkvMS8xMDg3MTMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiM2U2YWEwNzctZmJkNi1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=bbyEn7HpUDmssRLT_Q3TDYPkywZlGJBriY_lBtNjca8=&emci=a487ee70-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=3e6aa077-fbd6-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=14629434)** for a full list of accessible voting choices.

If you would like to unsubscribe, | | Tomorrow, polls open across the country for Election Day. So long as you have been waiting since before 8 p.m., you will be allowed to cast your ballot. We want to make sure you have all the information you need to cast your ballot tomorrow, so read on for our Pennsylvania voter guide, or forward this email to share it with a friend! VOTER REGISTRATION: If you want to cast your ballot tomorrow, you need to be registered to vote. Check your voter registration by clicking . WHERE TO VOTE: To find your designated polling place, you can click and enter your address. ⚠️ If this is your first time voting, make sure you bring a valid form of ID. You can see a list of accepted forms . ACCESSIBILITY: If you need assistance voting due to a disability, you have several options. Every polling place in Pennsylvania has at least one accessible voting system and if you need help voting at the polling place, you are allowed to bring a person of your choice with you to assist you. Tomorrow Is the Day. New Hampshire's Future Is on the Ballot

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/nhgop/rice-warmington-65524?e=f3aa6419cd)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/ijOxQDDCRzC?e=f3aa6419cd&c2id=cbe815d8d4829b0196839495b093775b&m=8ALczic4Sk9nexg8pEvIRS30YIKei1uSGgFsk5pfRKCWIK9I25qJEGHSNA==)
| | | | | |

**Friend,**
Tomorrow is the day.We have worked hard every single day to get to this moment, and it all comes down to tomorrow. The future of our state is at stake. If we fail to show up, we risk handing New Hampshire over to the radical policies and threat of socialism pushed by Democrats.I urge you to take time out of your day tomorrow to vote. Vote up and down the entire ballot, and vote YES on Question 2 to cap your property taxes.I know you have been flooded with countless emails, texts, phone calls, and mailers. I know you have heard it time and time again, but I cannot stress enough how important this election is. We have too much at stake to sit this one out.We must keep Governor Kelly Ayotte in the corner office. She has delivered for the Granite State in countless ways, from education and public safety to childcare. We have an incredible Governor who is fighting for New Hampshire. As she said best on WMUR, we cannot put an Opioid Lobbyist in the corner office.We must elect John E. Sununu to the U.S. Senate. He has an independent record of putting Granite Staters ahead of party politics, and he will do the same when he returns to Washington. Make no mistake, if Chris Pappas is elected, he will not just be there for two years. He will be in Washington for another SIX YEARS. After eight years in Congress with ZERO accomplishments to show for it, why would we give him a promotion to do the same in the Senate?For those of you in CD-1, we must elect Anthony DiLorenzo to Congress. He is the epitome of the American Dream. He understands Granite Staters and has practical solutions to the challenges facing our state. His business experience will be an incredible asset in Washington. He is not a political insider like his opponent, Stefany Shaheen, who cannot seem to answer simple questions, including whether men belong in women's sports. She wants to dismantle ICE and supports government-run healthcare. We cannot afford to send someone with those priorities to Congress.For those of you in CD-2, Lily Tang Williams is the candidate we need. She is a fighter who listens to Granite Staters and understands the importance of standing up for our freedoms. Her story is inspiring, and she will never back down from a challenge. Her opponent, Maggie Goodlander, seems to only come around New Hampshire during election season. After her time in Congress, she has little to show for it beyond the infamous video calling for the military to defy orders.We must also hold our majorities in the State Senate and State House and maintain our majority on the Executive Council. Our New Hampshire Advantage is on the line. Tomorrow, we have a choice. We can move New Hampshire forward, or we can let Democrats take us backward.Please make a plan to vote. Bring a friend, bring a family member, and encourage your neighbors to do the same. Vote the entire ballot. Vote YES on Question 2.
Best, Scott Maltzie NHGOP Chairman ###

We have too much at stake to sit this one out.We must keep Governor Kelly Ayotte in the corner office. She has delivered for the Granite State in countless ways, from education and public safety to childcare. We have an incredible Governor who is fighting for New Hampshire. As she said best on WMUR, we cannot put an Opioid Lobbyist in the corner office.We must elect John E. Sununu to the U.S. Senate. He has an independent record of putting Granite Staters ahead of party politics, and he will do the same when he returns to Washington. Make no mistake, if Chris Pappas is elected, he will not just be there for two years. He will be in Washington for another SIX YEARS. After eight years in Congress with ZERO accomplishments to show for it, why would we give him a promotion to do the same in the Senate?For those of you in CD-1, we must elect Anthony DiLorenzo to Congress. He is the epitome of the American Dream. He understands Granite Staters and has practical solutions to the challenges facing our state. His business experience will be an incredible asset in Washington. He is not a political insider like his opponent, Stefany Shaheen, who cannot seem to answer simple questions, including whether men belong in women's sports. She wants to dismantle ICE and supports government-run healthcare. We cannot afford to send someone with those priorities to Congress.For those of you in CD-2, Lily Tang Williams is the candidate we need. She is a fighter who listens to Granite Staters and understands the importance of standing up for our freedoms. Her story is inspiring, and she will never back down from a challenge. Her opponent, Maggie Goodlander, seems to only come around New Hampshire during election season. After her time in Congress, she has little to show for it beyond the infamous video calling for the military to defy orders.We must also hold our majorities in the State Senate and State House and maintain our majority on the Executive Council. Our New Hampshire Advantage is on the line. Tomorrow, we have a choice. We can move New Hampshire forward, or we can let Democrats take us backward.Please make a plan to vote. Bring a friend, bring a family member, and encourage your neighbors to do the same. Vote the entire ballot. Vote YES on Question 2. Best, Scott Maltzie NHGOP Chairman ### | | | | | | https:// https:// https:// | | | | | | | | | | Copyright (C) 2026 New Hampshire Republican Party. All rights reserved.

While history might not repeat, it certainly rhymes. The refrain emanating from Michigan today offers a painful--and revealing--reminder of what happens when Democrats forget lessons from the recent past.
### **We 've seen this movie before**
When Bernie Sanders emerged from a crowded field of presidential candidates in 2016, and again in 2020, the Democratic Party machine organized attacks ranging from [opportunistic accusations of sexism](https://substack.com/redirect/8c2deb72-87b8-4bde-bb79-707a628093f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to anticompetitive [consolidation among moderate candidates](https://substack.com/redirect/e9bb7040-f5c9-455e-a7b0-a7525edd22ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) behind Joe Biden--who had been [forced out](https://substack.com/redirect/1e511bb7-a266-4220-adc4-f4c15a029e4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of multiple previous presidential primaries due to public lies & plagiarism--in 2020.
We observed in the wake of that saga, and the eventual results of the 2024 election, that the Democratic Party is [primarily committed](https://substack.com/redirect/3e6b7dda-5d42-4b56-ab5f-344bf432cd53?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) not to its own electoral victories, nor to principles, nor to any particular policies, but rather to the interests of elites who often find themselves winning, even when the party & the public lose.
_Chronicles of a Dying Empire is a publication made possible by readers, rather than advertisers. To receive new posts,**sign up for a free subscription!** To support my work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber._
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.._ttDMfGORzTMWNn3VzHjXKXniz9yy8MjtXa8qwCzNWU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=223225021)
In 2020, Democrats betrayed their own base, and electoral prospects, by arraying itself behind a quintessential Wall Street presidential candidate--one who was welcomed into the Obama administration in 2008 precisely in order to [placate fears](https://substack.com/redirect/922cffd9-9b56-4448-81d0-9dafd25985f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from Wall Street, guaranteeing the primacy of [capital over labor](https://substack.com/redirect/85d694e9-954a-45d0-a984-0021d174c96f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) under the first administration led by a Black American, and [foretelling](https://substack.com/redirect/ffc99447-d65b-4db9-9cb0-c1d65ce6450e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the result of the 2024 election that Biden & Harris lost to Trump.
In both 2016 and 2020, Bernie Sanders performed [far better against Trump](https://substack.com/redirect/8ebf09d9-56a0-4913-8f6c-05958b3b6fb0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in head-to-head polls than machine Democrats like Biden, and for good reason. Much of Trump's support came from voters attracted to his supposed [iconoclasm](https://substack.com/redirect/5e1b7676-7e66-400c-8663-877de61de47e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and promises to make a sharp turn away from the corporate corruption and forever wars that had long [united](https://substack.com/redirect/064625c9-3501-4270-b2cd-cff65f3901c2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Republicans and Democrats in Washington. Of course, Trump's supporters ultimately leapt from a frying pan into a fire, inviting any number of [constitutional horrors](https://substack.com/redirect/f80e5dda-aab2-46fe-8e60-843567b73e08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [economic calamities](https://substack.com/redirect/6ad7c2d6-56cf-49aa-b1b7-a6986248f4b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) during each of his terms.
As many observers seem to have forgotten, Bernie captured much of that same sentiment, defanging Trump while also mobilizing millions of new voters and volunteers poised to usher in a new era of politics in the U.S.
Instead of embracing that transpartisan populist movement--as people who describe themselves as supporters of democracy would reasonably be expected to do--Democrats closed ranks around Wall Street. By abandoning working Americans in the midst of the mounting polycrisis, those Democrats created the political space for the ascendant right wing to adhere its poisonous ideology to working class grievances.
I was a visible part of the movement that could have charted a different history. My challenge to Pelosi in 2020 was inspired by the 2016 presidential campaign of Bernie Sanders (and a colleague who immediately said, "I'd vote for you!" when I unfortunately joked in a 2018 meeting about wanting to quit my job and run against her after witnessing yet another [betrayal](https://substack.com/redirect/f611fed5-c854-4f46-84ba-21f644364ab1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of her grassroots base).
As a congressional candidate in the 2020 general election, I was proud to support many of Bernie's policies, while adding [a few](https://substack.com/redirect/86839f74-4836-4812-8852-5fa485cf8c43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of [my own](https://substack.com/redirect/0bf29190-0d16-4970-85e7-f0f1c53646a9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the political discussion informed by my exploration of constitutional law both at Stanford and in Washington, DC.
Bernie was kneecapped by the Democratic establishment on the eve of a presidential election that would have changed the course of human history, and offered a fighting chance to overcome the polycrisis that increasingly threatens (whatever most people think of as) civilization. [My](https://substack.com/redirect/5da22597-91f8-46b8-8e37-75c771df1ca7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[](https://substack.com/redirect/5da22597-91f8-46b8-8e37-75c771df1ca7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[own character assassination](https://substack.com/redirect/5da22597-91f8-46b8-8e37-75c771df1ca7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at the hands of AIPAC Democrats effectively silenced me--weeks before an election in which I was the first progressive candidate to appear in nearly half a century, and in which even a mere debate would have offered accountability for one of the [most powerful, and corrupt, agents](https://substack.com/redirect/e47a6233-044c-44a2-bf0f-0e5ab80b7363?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of Wall Street in Congress.
### **The sequel sucks**
This year, Abdul El-Syed won the Democratic nomination for the U.S. Senate seat representing Michigan in tomorrow's general election. He beat a career Democrat, Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI), to get there.
Stevens has been a paid operative in the Democratic Party for two decades, before winning a seat in Congress in 2018. El-Syed is an epidemiologist & public health administrator who was inspired to seek elected office by the crisis in our country's healthcare system.
Their primary was bitter. While many issues divided El-Syed and Stevens, the race turned to a bizarre extent on Israel, due essentially to the embedded white supremacy that pervades U.S. politics. Forced repeatedly to [demonstrate his allegiance](https://substack.com/redirect/cad347ed-bb8e-466d-ae38-e873cc546aac?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--to a country whose elected leaders have openly [betrayed & looted it for decades](https://substack.com/redirect/82c76096-a6e6-470f-a39f-9984bdaad8a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--El-Syed emerged from the contested primary with the Party's nomination despite his unbowed support for public healthcare and climate justice, alongside limits on executive power and militarism.

[ Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1018597&post_id=223225021&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjIzMjI1MDIxLCJpYXQiOjE3OTM2NTE5MDEsImV4cCI6MTc5NjI0MzkwMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTEwMTg1OTciLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.a_S90CjT5X9HNM5XCMFd12BftI8GuobEwVIQ0zLQqyc)
There have been few feats of political judo over the past generation more profound than El-Syed drawing [public support](https://substack.com/redirect/82c76096-a6e6-470f-a39f-9984bdaad8a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) from former president Barack Obama. On the one hand, they seem cut from similar cloth: young candidates of color running for the U.S. Senate from midwestern states with roots outside the Party's political machine.
But while El-Syed has been an outspoken opponent of militarism, Obama was among its most [crucial enablers](https://substack.com/redirect/99477ebd-3aed-4caf-a5c9-ab31e8b7bbbb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--running to repudiate the Bush-Obama legacy before then [reinforcing](https://substack.com/redirect/1fdc1f74-d3a4-4219-a1ae-980072b6ac77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it with an unprecedented war on whistleblowers, a free pass for CIA torture, and a perverse expansion of the mass surveillance regime despite its exposure by Edward Snowden, who effectively fled into exile rather than become a political prisoner.
To be fair, Obama ran for the presidency (and the Senate before that) as an [antiwar candidate](https://substack.com/redirect/2119319e-9ab2-4196-a400-506c22696203?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). So, depending on which era of Obama we consider, the alignment with El-Syed can seem either on brand, or instead ironic. I have been meaning for over a year now to write an article about the political instability of "change" promised through the executive branch, citing Obama's arc as a public figure as one compelling demonstration among others, but I digress.
The point is that El-Syed getting Obama to campaign for him is a political coup. And it might frankly be a fluke, driven by the razor-thin majority in the Senate that Democrats are poised to flip. Would Obama campaign for El-Syed were his seat less crucial to Democrats taking the Senate, and with it, the power to block Trump's judicial nominees and restrain public funding for his initiatives?
### **Worst ending ever**
Obama's support for El-Syed makes [this weekend's betrayal by Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/redirect/6d9b702e-ccb7-4627-a7c5-3a7eb490e317?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) all the more bizarre, a self-inflicted wound by a party whose allegiances have long strayed from its public commitments. Despite how crucial Michigan's seat in the Senate has become to the possibility of constitutional accountability, Stevens--who has had a seat in Congress since 2019--placed a greater priority on fidelity to Israel.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/32749b8a-c086-436e-ad90-f67d8c81645f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Democrats have spent the last decade braying about supposed threats to democracy embodied by the Republican Party and the various organizations--from FOX News to the Heritage Institute and Federalist Society--that support and enable it. Now, on the eve of a crucial midterm election, a prominent centrist Democrat in a crucial swing state has endorsed a Republican rather than support the progressive who beat her in the primary election.
It is a revealing stance, one that should make clear for all to see what machine Democrats have tried to hide--with astounding success--for years: the party is co-opted not only by a domestic [military-industrial complex](https://substack.com/redirect/348987bd-2130-499c-a76e-0802bd789f02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), but also what amounts to an [international criminal syndicate](https://substack.com/@sarahkendzior/note/c-375836993?utm_source=notes-share-action&r=97w99) supporting zionism and human rights abuses.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.._ttDMfGORzTMWNn3VzHjXKXniz9yy8MjtXa8qwCzNWU?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=223225021)
### **A bit of irony**
Most outlandish of all, Stevens' critics include none other than Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY), the Senate Minority Leader and a--maybe _the_ --leading agent of AIPAC in the Democratic Party. If even Schumer sees fit to support El-Syed, who is Stevens to get in the way, other than a disgruntled career politician displaced by popular accountability?
Like Obama's conflicting ideological and institutional allegiances as a president, Schumer might seem torn between conflicting poles. On the one hand, he has often described his support for Israel as "existential." That commitment would suggest supporting Stevens in her defection to the Republican Party as the only bastion of Zionism in that race.
But Schumer also has at stake his own institutional power and authority as a potential Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress. That interest suggests getting El-Syed, the party's nominee, in the seat--even at the cost of his own ideological preferences.
Schumer was willing to set aside his fidelity to Israel for the sake of the party's (and his own) interests, as well as the possibility of constitutional accountability (that I, for one, have no faith he is poised to oversee). He chose to place his institutional interest in a Senate majority over his existential support for Israel.
But Stevens made a different choice. Voters around the country, and in her congressional district, are juggling one crisis after another, yet rather than support a candidate in her own party who supports a chance for every American to get healthcare as a right, Stevens chose to carry water for Israel, instead.
That choice reveals her primary fidelity to zionism before even her own party and its grassroots supporters. While Stevens has been [called out](https://substack.com/redirect/60e0b237-df82-4a57-82ca-79ad9cdc5cf4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by any number of party apparatchiks since her betrayal, many Democrats have made the same choice before, and too many will likely repeat it.
As outrageous as it is, there's a perspective from which that might ultimately not be such a bad thing:
[| | | Brittany Carter 1dIt's a great sign for progressive politics that El-Sayed's campaign has forced centrist Dems to close ranks around him and actively pushed conservative Democrats like Hayley Stevens to move to the GOP. That kind of cleaning house is long overdue.

### **Just to be clear**
I focus my fire on Democrats for the same reasons that Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. reserved his [most fervent critique](https://substack.com/redirect/068eec80-c37a-4295-8b3b-3b0df785aacd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for "the White Moderate." I have no love for Republicans and expect nothing useful from them, particularly under their present alignment as a cult of personality serving an autocrat.
At the same time, I have no illusions that a Democratically controlled Senate would be progressive in any way. But one might hope that a new Senate Majority, emboldened by the excesses of this administration and the grassroots demands for checks & balances, might demonstrate a stronger backbone under new leadership.
Whether they'll have the chance to do so is the most important issue at stake in tomorrow's election.

We warned in 2016 that Democrats would rather support fascists than progressives. The pattern we predicted then bore itself out--and is repeating in Michigan on the eve of the midterm elections. | | | Nov 2 | | | | | | | | | | | | While history might not repeat, it certainly rhymes. The refrain emanating from Michigan today offers a painful--and revealing--reminder of what happens when Democrats forget lessons from the recent past. We 've seen this movie before When Bernie Sanders emerged from a crowded field of presidential candidates in 2016, and again in 2020, the Democratic Party machine organized attacks ranging from to anticompetitive behind Joe Biden--who had been of multiple previous presidential primaries due to public lies & plagiarism--in 2020. We observed in the wake of that saga, and the eventual results of the 2024 election, that the Democratic Party is not to its own electoral victories, nor to principles, nor to any particular policies, but rather to the interests of elites who often find themselves winning, even when the party & the public lose. Chronicles of a Dying Empire is a publication made possible by readers, rather than advertisers. To receive new posts,sign up for a free subscription! To support my work, please consider becoming a paid subscriber. In 2020, Democrats betrayed their own base, and electoral prospects, by arraying itself behind a quintessential Wall Street presidential candidate--one who was welcomed into the Obama administration in 2008 precisely in order to from Wall Street, guaranteeing the primacy of under the first administration led by a Black American, and the result of the 2024 election that Biden & Harris lost to Trump. In both 2016 and 2020, Bernie Sanders performed in head-to-head polls than machine Democrats like Biden, and for good reason. Much of Trump's support came from voters attracted to his supposed , and promises to make a sharp turn away from the corporate corruption and forever wars that had long Republicans and Democrats in Washington. Of course, Trump's supporters ultimately leapt from a frying pan into a fire, inviting any number of and during each of his terms. As many observers seem to have forgotten, Bernie captured much of that same sentiment, defanging Trump while also mobilizing millions of new voters and volunteers poised to usher in a new era of politics in the U.S. Instead of embracing that transpartisan populist movement--as people who describe themselves as supporters of democracy would reasonably be expected to do--Democrats closed ranks around Wall Street. By abandoning working Americans in the midst of the mounting polycrisis, those Democrats created the political space for the ascendant right wing to adhere its poisonous ideology to working class grievances. I was a visible part of the movement that could have charted a different history. My challenge to Pelosi in 2020 was inspired by the 2016 presidential campaign of Bernie Sanders (and a colleague who immediately said, "I'd vote for you!" when I unfortunately joked in a 2018 meeting about wanting to quit my job and run against her after witnessing yet another of her grassroots base). As a congressional candidate in the 2020 general election, I was proud to support many of Bernie's policies, while adding of to the political discussion informed by my exploration of constitutional law both at Stanford and in Washington, DC. Bernie was kneecapped by the Democratic establishment on the eve of a presidential election that would have changed the course of human history, and offered a fighting chance to overcome the polycrisis that increasingly threatens (whatever most people think of as) civilization. at the hands of AIPAC Democrats effectively silenced me--weeks before an election in which I was the first progressive candidate to appear in nearly half a century, and in which even a mere debate would have offered accountability for one of the of Wall Street in Congress. The sequel sucks This year, Abdul El-Syed won the Democratic nomination for the U.S. Senate seat representing Michigan in tomorrow's general election. He beat a career Democrat, Rep. Haley Stevens (D-MI), to get there. Stevens has been a paid operative in the Democratic Party for two decades, before winning a seat in Congress in 2018. El-Syed is an epidemiologist & public health administrator who was inspired to seek elected office by the crisis in our country's healthcare system. Their primary was bitter. While many issues divided El-Syed and Stevens, the race turned to a bizarre extent on Israel, due essentially to the embedded white supremacy that pervades U.S. politics. Forced repeatedly to a country whose elected leaders have openly emerged from the contested primary with the Party's nomination despite his unbowed support for public healthcare and climate justice, alongside limits on executive power and militarism. Thanks for reading Chronicles of a Dying Empire! This post is freely accessible. Feel free to share it with your friends. There have been few feats of political judo over the past generation more profound than El-Syed drawing from former president Barack Obama. On the one hand, they seem cut from similar cloth: young candidates of color running for the U.S. Senate from midwestern states with roots outside the Party's political machine. But while El-Syed has been an outspoken opponent of militarism, Obama was among its most to repudiate the Bush-Obama legacy before then it with an unprecedented war on whistleblowers, a free pass for CIA torture, and a perverse expansion of the mass surveillance regime despite its exposure by Edward Snowden, who effectively fled into exile rather than become a political prisoner. To be fair, Obama ran for the presidency (and the Senate before that) as an . So, depending on which era of Obama we consider, the alignment with El-Syed can seem either on brand, or instead ironic. I have been meaning for over a year now to write an article about the political instability of "change" promised through the executive branch, citing Obama's arc as a public figure as one compelling demonstration among others, but I digress. The point is that El-Syed getting Obama to campaign for him is a political coup. And it might frankly be a fluke, driven by the razor-thin majority in the Senate that Democrats are poised to flip. Would Obama campaign for El-Syed were his seat less crucial to Democrats taking the Senate, and with it, the power to block Trump's judicial nominees and restrain public funding for his initiatives? Worst ending ever Obama's support for El-Syed makes all the more bizarre, a self-inflicted wound by a party whose allegiances have long strayed from its public commitments. Despite how crucial Michigan's seat in the Senate has become to the possibility of constitutional accountability, Stevens--who has had a seat in Congress since 2019--placed a greater priority on fidelity to Israel. | | ---|---|--- Democrats have spent the last decade braying about supposed threats to democracy embodied by the Republican Party and the various organizations--from FOX News to the Heritage Institute and Federalist Society--that support and enable it. Now, on the eve of a crucial midterm election, a prominent centrist Democrat in a crucial swing state has endorsed a Republican rather than support the progressive who beat her in the primary election. It is a revealing stance, one that should make clear for all to see what machine Democrats have tried to hide--with astounding success--for years: the party is co-opted not only by a domestic , but also what amounts to an supporting zionism and human rights abuses. A bit of irony Most outlandish of all, Stevens' critics include none other than Sen. Chuck Schumer (D-NY), the Senate Minority Leader and a--maybe the --leading agent of AIPAC in the Democratic Party. If even Schumer sees fit to support El-Syed, who is Stevens to get in the way, other than a disgruntled career politician displaced by popular accountability? Like Obama's conflicting ideological and institutional allegiances as a president, Schumer might seem torn between conflicting poles. On the one hand, he has often described his support for Israel as "existential." That commitment would suggest supporting Stevens in her defection to the Republican Party as the only bastion of Zionism in that race. But Schumer also has at stake his own institutional power and authority as a potential Senate Majority Leader in the next Congress. That interest suggests getting El-Syed, the party's nominee, in the seat--even at the cost of his own ideological preferences. Schumer was willing to set aside his fidelity to Israel for the sake of the party's (and his own) interests, as well as the possibility of constitutional accountability (that I, for one, have no faith he is poised to oversee). He chose to place his institutional interest in a Senate majority over his existential support for Israel. But Stevens made a different choice. Voters around the country, and in her congressional district, are juggling one crisis after another, yet rather than support a candidate in her own party who supports a chance for every American to get healthcare as a right, Stevens chose to carry water for Israel, instead. That choice reveals her primary fidelity to zionism before even her own party and its grassroots supporters. While Stevens has been by any number of party apparatchiks since her betrayal, many Democrats have made the same choice before, and too many will likely repeat it. As outrageous as it is, there's a perspective from which that might ultimately not be such a bad thing: Just to be clear I focus my fire on Democrats for the same reasons that Dr. Martin Luther King, Jr. reserved his for "the White Moderate." I have no love for Republicans and expect nothing useful from them, particularly under their present alignment as a cult of personality serving an autocrat. At the same time, I have no illusions that a Democratically controlled Senate would be progressive in any way. But one might hope that a new Senate Majority, emboldened by the excesses of this administration and the grassroots demands for checks & balances, might demonstrate a stronger backbone under new leadership. When we launched this campaign nearly a year ago, folks called us a long shot. Some people wrote us off entirely. After all, Trump won this district by 12 points in 2024, and McGuire won it by 15. _After Gov. Spanberger fell short in the 5th during her romp across Virginia, the pundits solidified their belief that this district was too ruby red to be won by any Democrat._ Where the political operatives saw statistics, I saw people – people enraged by what they saw happening in DC and ready to vote for change. But only if we showed up, listened, and offered a serious alternative. And then showed up again, and again, and again. **Giving up on this region is simply not an option for me, because I grew up here, in the shadow of Virginia’s Blue Ridge Mountains.** From my Eagle Scout service project with local area food banks to fights for a living wage and against dangerous gas pipelines, I love serving this community. These are the people and the communities that first gave me the chance to serve in Congress. These are the folks who have been abandoned by elites in both parties far too many times to trust just anyone to represent them. I knew it would take something different and more patient, building on foundations laid over many years, with sweat equity from hundreds and eventually _thousands_ of volunteers determined to reclaim our voice in Congress – and our sense of right and wrong. We have one day and a wake up left to see this project through to its next phase of governing. Criss-crossing the district this weekend, we had crowds rallying in our reddest counties, an outpouring of support at the Boydton Day parade, and a lot more treats than tricks being offered at the massive community Halloween events. We held a presser with former GOP Rep. Denver Riggleman and other former and current Republicans at a beloved local bar in Lynchburg. And, perhaps most importantly, my mother and her Campaign Cookie Crew (The Triple C), baked and dispatched their 25,000th chocolate chip cookie of the campaign. That is not a typo. The twenty-five-thousandth home-baked cookie went out on Saturday, and Mom and co are not done yet! _We are on the brink of blending together all that grassroots energy, generous support, and righteous resistance rage into a delicious victory on Tuesday night. _ But we have not won anything yet, and there is no prize for second place. **The fate of the House majority may rest on this race, along with my ability to fight to prevent a generational destruction of rural healthcare, and to end this war. We are a toss-up race that is going to come down to Election Day turnout._And even though we feel the contagious hope and shaky optimism emanating from the fired-up people in every corner of the district and the record number of early votes cast – we know that this race is winnable, but it is not yet won. _** We cannot leave a single stone unturned, a single voter unreached, a single precinct overlooked – and there are over 300 of them! The budget is tight, and every single dollar makes a difference in what we can do in these final hours. [**If you haven’t made a donation yet, I am telling you that now is the time. clean_body: We could be the difference.| | | | | | | = When we launched this campaign nearly a year ago, folks called us a long shot. Some people wrote us off entirely. After all, Trump won this district by 12 points in 2024, and McGuire won it by 15. After Gov. Spanberger fell short in the 5th during her romp across Virginia, the pundits solidified their belief that this district was too ruby red to be won by any Democrat. Where the political operatives saw statistics, I saw people – people enraged by what they saw happening in DC and ready to vote for change. But only if we showed up, listened, and offered a serious alternative. And then showed up again, and again, and again. Giving up on this region is simply not an option for me, because I grew up here, in the shadow of Virginia’s Blue Ridge Mountains. From my Eagle Scout service project with local area food banks to fights for a living wage and against dangerous gas pipelines, I love serving this community. These are the people and the communities that first gave me the chance to serve in Congress. These are the folks who have been abandoned by elites in both parties far too many times to trust just anyone to represent them. I knew it would take something different and more patient, building on foundations laid over many years, with sweat equity from hundreds and eventually thousands of volunteers determined to reclaim our voice in Congress – and our sense of right and wrong. We have one day and a wake up left to see this project through to its next phase of governing. Criss-crossing the district this weekend, we had crowds rallying in our reddest counties, an outpouring of support at the Boydton Day parade, and a lot more treats than tricks being offered at the massive community Halloween events. We held a presser with former GOP Rep. Denver Riggleman and other former and current Republicans at a beloved local bar in Lynchburg. And, perhaps most importantly, my mother and her Campaign Cookie Crew (The Triple C), baked and dispatched their 25,000th chocolate chip cookie of the campaign. That is not a typo. The twenty-five-thousandth home-baked cookie went out on Saturday, and Mom and co are not done yet! We are on the brink of blending together all that grassroots energy, generous support, and righteous resistance rage into a delicious victory on Tuesday night. But we have not won anything yet, and there is no prize for second place. The fate of the House majority may rest on this race, along with my ability to fight to prevent a generational destruction of rural healthcare, and to end this war. We are a toss-up race that is going to come down to Election Day turnout.And even though we feel the contagious hope and shaky optimism emanating from the fired-up people in every corner of the district and the record number of early votes cast – we know that this race is winnable, but it is not yet won. We cannot leave a single stone unturned, a single voter unreached, a single precinct overlooked – and there are over 300 of them! The budget is tight, and every single dollar makes a difference in what we can do in these final hours. = = I got into this race because I know I can make a difference. I’m the only Democrat in a century to flip a seat west of Richmond – and tomorrow, with your help, we are going to do it again. This isn't new to me. I've been called names. I've been threatened and attacked for refusing to stay quiet. Ron DeSantis even had me arrested for standing up against illegal, discriminatory voting maps. But what's happening now is different. Messages like the ones I've been receiving lately, racist attacks and direct threats against my family, are showing up regularly. Not occasionally. Regularly. I want to be completely honest with you about why I'm sharing this. I will not be intimidated. I will not stop fighting for the people of this state. That has never been in question, and it never will be. But I also have a responsibility to take these threats seriously, for my own safety and for the safety of my family. We urgently need to increase security for me, for them, and for this campaign as we head into the general election. This isn't a cost I expected to be writing to you about. It's not glamorous, and it's not what any campaign wants to spend resources on. But it's necessary, and I refuse to let anyone's threats slow this campaign down or push us out of this fight. I am so excited to keep spreading the word about our people-powered movement. I wish I could tell you the story ends there, with a celebration and nothing else. But since our victory, the racist threats and harassment I've faced have only gotten worse. | == This isn't new to me. I've been called names. I've been threatened and attacked for refusing to stay quiet. Ron DeSantis even had me arrested for standing up against illegal, discriminatory voting maps. But what's happening now is different. Messages like the ones I've been receiving lately, racist attacks and direct threats against my family, are showing up regularly. Not occasionally. Regularly. I want to be completely honest with you about why I'm sharing this. I will not be intimidated. I will not stop fighting for the people of this state. That has never been in question, and it never will be. But I also have a responsibility to take these threats seriously, for my own safety and for the safety of my family. We urgently need to increase security for me, for them, and for this campaign as we head into the general election. This isn't a cost I expected to be writing to you about. It's not glamorous, and it's not what any campaign wants to spend resources on. But it's necessary, and I refuse to let anyone's threats slow this campaign down or push us out of this fight. == | == I got into this race to fight for working Florida families, not to back down from anyone trying to scare me out of it. When I was growing up in Bethel, salmon fishing with my father in the summers and dog mushing in the winters, Alaska was a place of abundance.

Now, all across Alaska, we have scarcity.

Multi-national companies are trawling our waters and decimating our fish stocks. The moose, caribou, and migratory birds that used to fill our freezers are harder to find.

So we buy more groceries, where the prices are just crushing Alaska families.

And I've got to tell you, DC people do not care that we are paying nearly 20 bucks for a gallon of fuel. They don’t even believe us.

They're focused on their own wallets – not ours.

And when they actually work together on something, it’s usually to help themselves. The rigged system in DC is shutting down Alaska and hurting all of us while politicians and their millionaire and billionaire donors feather their own nest.

It’s why our prices keep rising, all while the healthcare and services Alaskans rely on get gutted.

I'm done with politicians getting richer while things get tougher here at home.

My agenda for Alaska will always be: fish, family, freedom. These values have been the core values of my campaigns since the very beginning. But if we’re going to secure Alaska’s future, we need another priority: fighting corruption.

I'm running for Alaska's Senate seat because it is the fight for our future. This is going to be the closest and most consequential Senate race this year, and I cannot do this alone. There is only one way we’ll be able to flip this seat... and that is together.

So I am asking:

**[Please split a contribution between Equal Opportunity Now and my campaign for the U.S. Senate today before our upcoming deadline. We are looking for a huge surge in support to put us in a position to win. No donation is too small. They will all add up fast to give us the resources we need to WIN in November. ](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142773436/657986548/916216164?refcode=261024_peltola_decision&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICIwZGJmNmRjYS0wMGQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=Pupc_7HQv9TLklmrhzv906dd-CGKYSHvNmh4uJTXFmc=)**

First, early voting results showed _record breaking_ Black turnout surpassing Obama ‘08 and a narrow 16,000 vote Democratic lead. In response, Trump announced an emergency rally here. Then the _2nd poll_ showing Democrat Jamie Davis _tied_ came out. Now, for the first time since the race began**a national party has begun spending in the race:** [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsykqgM-Njm5GO2lzL0vPpXGMOuiZbvWlTL5bGhNoB6xEWecY-XJJR6eLhGr9z9kF_jKNMM9OiwTmF6X_QdRP5rXG9SDbdKtsAy7PIRuhzax6E06GnsdRya2Ck2W7L0ZVRllJKBCyfIyz_cIZGoWD6X8cMJ58HEEbihzRxM7hwuwru2StobjCIf19d6-bL7QC_RXT-42FCNrFKnWe7wESvJOPy849lUqbdT6Ft5n0-8BpndniXOcqDTaNUIo11ejaexjo6Xi8OWSIIESlkvwjqLSdKl5cpUyqwIi-2KSyz9oOKqMGo_mUh4AmC5tI2I8e0maWJHDZneZyZF5Zhco91ySUpVAzT0CvyQD678dZJTwexEoxyd5Owx4wMbI2U0ZqU/4ve/F_6eO7hiRIaHy4L0QkQbjA/h1/h001.NCQ5K3CaK4z0JbY8FWpcVBqLyPpfIcpOpawahG0H_ik)

**Exhibit B — the hot spots.** In early October, California led the country at about $6.40 a gallon, followed by Hawaii, Washington and Nevada. Diesel averaged $6.29 in September, the highest monthly figure on record.

**Exhibit C — the supply.** The Strait of Hormuz has been effectively closed for months, and Brent crude settled near $114 on October 27. In California, Phillips 66 closed its Los Angeles refinery late last year, and Valero moved to shut its Benicia plant in 2026.

Some relief is possible. The EIA expects prices to ease next year, and a deal with Iran could quickly lower crude.

When prices spike, someone in the chain profits. Knowing who that is turns a painful bill into a potential opportunity.

name: Cooper, Roy
subject: I’m ready to finish the job tomorrow. Are you with me?
body:
I believe our best days are ahead of us. I really do.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1753&source=&t=1&akid=5181%2E124072%2E6HDAZX) | | | |
---
Peter, I’m feeling grateful tonight.
Tomorrow, voters in North Carolina and across the country will cast their ballots in one of the most important elections in our lifetimes. This moment feels big – and it is – but right now, I’m just so thankful for **supporters like you.**
Look, my decision to run for U.S. Senate wasn’t made lightly.
Serving as Governor was one of the greatest experiences of my life, but after my second term, I was ready to hang up my suit and tie. From adding hundreds of thousands of good-paying jobs, to giving schoolteachers much-needed raises, to expanding access to Medicaid, my #1 priority was to improve the lives of everyday people – and we did that.
That’s why it’s been so upsetting to see how Washington DC insiders like Michael Whatley have turned their backs on hardworking people. He’s built his career promoting the interests of Big Oil, utility companies and wealthy donors at the _expense_ of working families.
So while I didn’t plan to go to Washington DC, I couldn’t stand by and watch the GOP continue bringing us down this dark path. I got back in the fight, and I’m glad I did.
**I’m ready to finish the job tomorrow, but just as in elections past, I can’t do it alone.**
[**_If you can, chip in $5 to help fuel our final voter outreach efforts, flip NC and take back the Senate for the people. If you can’t, that’s OK – I’m just grateful for your support throughout this campaign._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1753&amount=5&t=8&akid=5181%2E124072%2E6HDAZX)
I believe our best days are ahead of us. I really do. Thank you for everything.
Roy Cooper
| |
* * *
[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1753&t=2&akid=5181%2E124072%2E6HDAZX)

Alright, Derek – let’s walk through this together:
Growing up, my family faced challenges that many Wisconsinites know all too well, including addiction, mental health challenges, and unstable housing. I never knew if I would come home to find our belongings on the curb from another eviction, food in the refrigerator, or a safe place to land. My parents worked hard, but it was tough.
**Luckily, I had people in my community who believed in me and gave me opportunities that changed my life.**
They helped me graduate from high school, supported my passion for public service, and helped me run for elected office. They also helped me return to college to finish my undergraduate degree while serving as Milwaukee County executive.
I’ve had an unconventional path, Derek, but my community has had my back every step of the way. **I believe every person, every family deserves that same support.**
That belief shaped my priorities as Milwaukee County executive, and it’s why I’m running for governor now. I’ve seen first-hand what happens when we put working families first:
→ When we expanded access to affordable housing, **our per capita unhoused population dropped to _the lowest in the nation_**. Now, fewer families suffer the upheaval of eviction that my family faced.
→ When we expanded healthcare access – including opening a 24/7 walk-in mental health emergency center – **our community felt the relief of _safe, comprehensive care close to home_**. That’s a resource I wish my parents would've had.
→ When we invested in public transit and local parks, **our communities thrived with new opportunities to stay connected and active.** Now, folks from backgrounds like mine have greater access to the kinds of opportunities that helped me thrive.
**But, Derek, this is just the beginning.**
I’m serious about fighting to make life better for working families across Wisconsin. I’m serious about lowering costs, funding our public schools, expanding access to healthcare and public services. I’m serious about building a Wisconsin where working people can build a life they love without leaving the state they love.
**So, Derek, my cards are on the table. You’ve seen my track record, and you’ve heard my vision for the future of Wisconsin. clean_body: I’m laying all my cards on the table so you can see my track record for yourself. | | | | Today, I want to lay all my cards on the table so you can see my track record for yourself. This is a longer email than I usually send, and I really hope you’ll stick around to hear my story. | | Alright, Derek – let’s walk through this together: Growing up, my family faced challenges that many Wisconsinites know all too well, including addiction, mental health challenges, and unstable housing. I never knew if I would come home to find our belongings on the curb from another eviction, food in the refrigerator, or a safe place to land. My parents worked hard, but it was tough. Luckily, I had people in my community who believed in me and gave me opportunities that changed my life. They helped me graduate from high school, supported my passion for public service, and helped me run for elected office. They also helped me return to college to finish my undergraduate degree while serving as Milwaukee County executive. I’ve had an unconventional path, Derek, but my community has had my back every step of the way. I believe every person, every family deserves that same support. That belief shaped my priorities as Milwaukee County executive, and it’s why I’m running for governor now. I’ve seen first-hand what happens when we put working families first: → When we expanded access to affordable housing, our per capita unhoused population dropped to the lowest in the nation. Now, fewer families suffer the upheaval of eviction that my family faced. → When we expanded healthcare access – including opening a 24/7 walk-in mental health emergency center – our community felt the relief of safe, comprehensive care close to home. That’s a resource I wish my parents would've had. → When we invested in public transit and local parks, our communities thrived with new opportunities to stay connected and active. Now, folks from backgrounds like mine have greater access to the kinds of opportunities that helped me thrive. But, Derek, this is just the beginning. I’m serious about fighting to make life better for working families across Wisconsin. I’m serious about lowering costs, funding our public schools, expanding access to healthcare and public services. I’m serious about building a Wisconsin where working people can build a life they love without leaving the state they love. So, Derek, my cards are on the table. You’ve seen my track record, and you’ve heard my vision for the future of Wisconsin. Now, I’m asking you to stand with me to make it a reality.
