# [](https://act.fordfornevada.com/go/12?t=1&akid=1255%2E127862%2Ef4PiGa)
_“Wait, there’s an election tomorrow?”_
If you’re reading this email, that’s probably not a question you’d ask.
**But all across Nevada, thousands of potential voters who don’t keep up with the news and haven’t been tuned in to this election until *this very moment* are asking exactly that.**
It’s these last-minute voters who will ultimately determine whether we win or lose this toss-up race for governor.
That is why we _must_ keep campaigning and organizing until the very last minute.
Whether these sporadic, late-breaking voters show up to vote for Aaron at the polls will be determined by our ability to reach them in these final 24 hours. So we are asking for your urgent support so we can contact them ASAP.
[_**Can you pitch in $5 or any amount to help Aaron before it’s too late? ❤️ Everyone is welcome!

IT WILL BE MONUMENTAL!! 🌟❤️🎉

| | **_Meet Russell:_** Born and raised in Surfside Beach, SC, Congressman Russell Fry is the proud and homegrown Representative for South Carolina’s 7th Congressional District. Growing up in a cinder block home with no heating or air conditioning, Russell learned at an early age that hard work and perseverance pave the only true path to the American Dream. He watched his parents work day in and day out to make ends meet. And the values they instilled in him during his upbringing led Russell to self-fund both his undergraduate education at the University of South Carolina, and later his law studies at the Charleston School of Law. At Charleston, Russell served as the President of the Student Bar Association and even helped the school achieve its American Bar Association accreditation. He went on to practice law in the Grand Strand area for over a decade before entering the political arena to serve in the South Carolina House of Representatives for State House District 106 (Horry County). During his seven-year tenure in the SC House, Russell fought to safeguard Constitutional liberties, lower taxes, and put the best interests of South Carolina families above all else. He climbed the ranks to become Chief Majority Whip, and also chaired the House Opioid Prevention Study Committee. Under Russell’s leadership, 18 policy initiatives to combat the opioid crisis were signed into law. Since the first day he stepped foot in Washington, Russell has strived to shake up the corrupt status quo and deliver real change for the American people. He believes adamantly that so long as the American people stand united, we can keep the American Dream alive for every citizen of our great nation. Russell is a dedicated husband to his wife, Bronwen, and a loving father to his son, James. The family lives in Murrells Inlet with their chocolate lab, Jasper.

body:
If you are having trouble viewing this message or would like to share it on a social network, you can [view the message online](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1).

#
# **Election Day is TOMORROW, November 3rd**
**Here 's Everything You Need to Know About Election Day**
* Election Day is TOMORROW, Tuesday, November 3, 2026
* Polls will be open from 7:00AM to 8:00PM. If you are in line by 8:00PM, you can cast your vote.
* Find your [polling place HERE](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18720)
* Completed mail-in and absentee ballots must be received by your county board of elections by 8:00PM TOMORROW. If you still have your mail-in ballot, plan to return it to a drop box by TOMORROW. It's too late now to put it in the mail.
* You can find a drop box near you [HERE](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18721)

**Voter ID Requirements** **Returning Voters** **do not** need to present identification if you have previously voted at your current polling place district. **First-Time Voters** who are voting in a district for the first time, must bring a valid form of identification.
* **Approved Photo IDs** : PA Driver's License or PennDOT ID, U.S. Passport, U.S. Military ID, Student ID, or Employee ID.
* **Approved Non-Photo IDs (showing your name and address)** : Voter Registration Card, Utility Bill, Bank Statement, Paycheck, or Government Check.

**If You Have Questions** If you run into issues or have questions on election day, call the Pennsylvania Department of State at **1-877-868-3772** or the [nonpartisan Election Protection Hotline at 1-866-OUR-VOTE](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18722)(1-866-687-8683). The [Pennsylvania Department of State](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18723) also has lots of information available on their website. And the [Committee of Seventy](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18724), a nonpartisan voting organization, has [information about what's on the ballot](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18725) and everything you need to know to be an informed voter.
* * *
**Stay in Touch on Social Media** If you haven't visited Senator Hughes' [**Facebook page**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18726), join the conversation by 'liking' the page and following our office on [**Instagram**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18728), [**TikTok**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18711), [**X**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18712), and [**Bluesky**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18714). We have lots of information available on these pages about community events and issues affecting our district. If you have questions or concerns, send us an email at [**hughes@pasenate.com**](http://enews.senatorhughes.com/mail/util.cfm?mailaction=clickthru&gpiv=2100172656.172922.227&gen=1&mailing_linkid=18715).

On video, she told voters she's backing Mike Rogers for U.S. Senate. | | ---|--- That's the moment we're in, Friend. That's all. | | ---|---

name: Abdul El-Sayed
subject: Let them have the drama
body:
Peter, there's a
lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted.

Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about
politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes.

I will not be distracted. Every minute spent talking about politicians is
a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working
Michiganders.

— This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good
at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.

— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to
“trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of
reach.

— And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide
control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a
check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate,
wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been
fleecing Michigan for decades.

Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.

Election Day is Tuesday. Several polls show us statistically tied with
Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes.

I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front
of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.

Abdul

name: Doug Ollivant for Congress
subject: Tomorrow.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY OLLIVANT FOR CONGRESS
body:
Vindman unmasked himself with his friend AOC.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1BBefKZ3J_h?e=14c77a6723&c2id=09489c9156c428bed3a67a2822595ae0)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Friends and neighbors,
_**Election Day is tomorrow.**_
Yevgeny “Eugene” Vindman has spent two years posing as a moderate, a familiar tactic. Then he closed his campaign by standing on stage in Dumfries with Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, the leading face of the Democratic Socialists of America, and called her a friend and colleague.
_**Vindman welcomed AOC into the district as his closer, days before the vote.**_
Vindman’s family escaped the Soviet Union. He knows what that system produced. Instead of rejecting the ideology, he imported its loudest American spokesman for a celebrity GOTV show and thanked her for her “leadership.”
That is not moderation. That is the mask coming off. Yevgeny’s rally sums up his character. When it mattered most, he showed exactly whose agenda he is willing to amplify.
Virginia’s 7th has had enough of Yevgeny’s same party-line votes that drive up costs, threaten parental rights, undermine energy abundance, and erode the American way of life.
I am a combat veteran, a husband, father of seven, and grandfather. I will fight for parental choice in education, reliable and affordable energy, lower costs for working families, integrity against fraud, and the Second Amendment. The choice is straightforward.
_**Tomorrow, vote. Bring a friend. Bring a neighbor. Flip VA-07.**_
One team. One fight.
****

**Republican Nominee for U.S. Congress****Virginia’s 7th Congressional District**

Troy here -- take a walk down memory lane with me for a second.
This is me as a kid. I don't remember the exact moment the photo was taken, but I probably caught that fish with my dad. We didn't spend a whole lot of time together when I was growing up because he worked such long hours out in the woods, but I really loved the time we did get.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f0dc1729-7174-4c4a-bf98-6860e865ea87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Fast forward a little more than a decade, and this is me again, this time with two sons of my own. I hate that I didn't spend a whole lot of time with them growing up either, because just like my dad, I was out in the woods working the same long hours to try to make ends meet.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f0dc1729-7174-4c4a-bf98-6860e865ea87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### **I 've been trying to put this into words for a long time.**
When we're living in a system that's rigged to benefit the super-rich -- a system that forces us to work 80-hour weeks to put food on the table, or take two or three jobs at a time to afford health insurance -- we're losing a whole lot more than just money.
_We 're losing what little time we have with our families._
### **I 'm still trying to make up for a life lost with my kids.**
When my boys were growing up, times were tough for our family. There was never enough money, and I was spending all my time out on the road, driving hours to chase down logging jobs that I needed if we were gonna be able to get by.
Leaving home before sunrise, never getting back before sunset, spending nights sitting around the kitchen table looking at the bills piling up, and doing it all again the next day.
### **You 're bone-tired, and it takes a toll on your family.**
And it's not just me. I see it everywhere I go: people constantly having to chase down money for the next medical bill, the rent that's always due, the damn groceries that just keep getting more expensive -- it gets so bad there's no time left for living life.
The oligarchy's greatest robbery from the working class is our time.**** The people in power see working-class folks as nothing more than a commodity.
### **This billionaire economy is not just about taking our money. It is about taking pieces of our lives away from us.**
So when I'm out on the road across Maine, and I'm talking to folks about the stakes of this election and what I'm fighting for, I want to be clear:
Yes, I'm fighting for higher wages and lower costs, for affordable healthcare and tax breaks for working families.
**And what all of that really means is I 'm** _**fighting for the things that make your life worth living**_**.**
That's what this is all about.
It's what I've been fighting for my whole life, and it's what I'll fight for in the U.S. Senate, if you can help me get there.
**[Election Day is tomorrow -- so if you're in a position to donate, will you chip in right now to support this fight? We're up against tens of millions of dollars in MAGA dark money trying to protect Susan Collins, not to mention the money pouring in from Elon Musk, and we're being outspent.](https://substack.com/redirect/f0dc1729-7174-4c4a-bf98-6860e865ea87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[CONTRIBUTE ->](https://substack.com/redirect/f0dc1729-7174-4c4a-bf98-6860e865ea87?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you for being a part of this team, however you can.
--Troy

name: Mary Buell
subject: TOMORROW IS ELECTION DAY — Every Vote Actually Matters!
body:
Tomorrow, November 3, is Election Day! Every vote counts, and we need everyone to make their voice heard!

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/jeffwalterforcongress/tomorrow-is-election-day-every-vote-actually-matters?e=fa724b03ca)
---
|
---
| | | | | |

Friends,
**TOMORROW IS ELECTION DAY!**
After months of hard work, conversations with voters, and campaigning across Illinois's 11th Congressional District, the final day has arrived!
This election presents voters with important choices about the future of our economy, our communities, and our country.
**We need EVERY Republican in Illinois's 11th Congressional District who hasn't voted yet to make their voice heard tomorrow!** Every vote matters, and turnout will play a critical role in determining the outcome of this election. If you haven't cast your ballot, tomorrow, November 3, is your opportunity to participate. Make a plan to vote, and remind your family, friends, and neighbors that Election Day is here.
Jeff Walter, a businessman and Navy veteran, has made his priorities clear:
* **Rebuild America's Economy:** Unleash American energy, cut unnecessary red tape, and bring back good-paying jobs.
* **Lower Taxes and the Cost of Living:** Address the rising costs of groceries, gasoline, and everyday essentials.
* **Keep Our Communities Safe:** Support law enforcement and hold criminals accountable.
* **Protect Social Security and Medicare:** Preserve the benefits that seniors have earned.
* **End Wasteful Washington Spending:** Fight government fraud, reduce reckless spending, and protect taxpayers.

**Every vote counts, and every voice deserves to be heard.**
In a congressional election, every ballot contributes to the final result. No one should assume their vote doesn't matter or that the outcome is already decided.
If you haven't voted yet, make your voting plan today. Check your polling location, know when the polls open, and encourage your friends, family, and neighbors to participate.
**Tomorrow, November 3, make your voice heard!**
Thank you for your involvement, dedication, and support throughout this campaign.
Mary Buell
Campaign Manager
Jeff Walter for Congress

I burned the boats, Peter, and there's absolutely no looking back.
I will not be canceled. I will not apologize for values that are wholesome and good. And if my voice gives someone else the courage to use theirs, that is exactly why I did it.

I want my daughter and every young American to know one thing:
You earn your place. You think for yourself. And you never let anyone put you in a box. That's the Minnesota I'm fighting for.
Parents who speak up are called transphobes.Girls who lose opportunities are told to be quiet.And women's groups are nowhere to be found.
This is not complicated.
Girls' sports are for girls, and boys' sports are for boys.

The radical Left has done everything in its power to infiltrate some of the most vulnerable minds in our society. I launched this run because just like you, I'm sick of the indoctrination and want to bring back sanity to our country.

It's going to be FAR from easy. Minnesota hasn't had a Republican Senator in nearly two decades! However, it's ripe for a flip....with the disastrous leadership of Governor Walz and the Democratic Party in the state, people are fed up.

* * *
Hey folks,
We're one day away from a massive election, and I just sat down with [Adam Mockler](https://open.substack.com/users/72893096-adam-mockler?utm_source=mentions) to talk about what could be a defining moment for the Democratic Party and the future of this country.
And look, I'm excited. Really excited. But I'm also thinking about what comes next.
Because beating MAGA isn't enough. We have to build something better. A new generation of leaders. A government that actually works for working people. And a Democratic Party that's finally willing to take on corruption, corporate power, and the broken systems that got us here.
Adam and I get into all of it. And we don't hold back.
Here's what we covered:
* [**00:01:10**] A new generation is stepping up. Why leaders like AOC, Jon Ossoff, James Talarico, and Josh Turek represent something bigger than just younger faces in Washington.
* [**00:04:30**] The stakes go way beyond this election. From AI threatening jobs and privacy to the urgent need to pass the torch, I explain why Democrats can't afford to waste this moment.
* [**00:08:45**] Corruption is the defining issue. I lay out my vision for a Democratic Party built around fighting corruption, fixing the economy, protecting our safety, and defending our fundamental rights.
* [**00:12:50**] What Democrats should actually do with power. Adam and I debate aggressive, single-issue legislation to ban congressional stock trading, end gerrymandering, eliminate junk fees, and make healthcare more affordable.
* [**00:16:45**] Why independent media matters more than ever. We get personal about the people who make this work possible and why building a media ecosystem that isn't controlled by billionaires is essential to winning the fights ahead.

Here's what I keep coming back to: **We cannot just go back to normal.**
Normal wasn't working for millions of Americans. Normal gave us a political system where billionaires have more influence than working families, where healthcare is a constant source of anxiety, and where politicians spend more time protecting their careers than improving people's lives.
We have an opportunity to change that. But it requires courage. It requires new leadership. And it requires a willingness to fight for people even when the political establishment tells us to play it safe.
This conversation with Adam is about what that fight looks like, why I'm hopeful, and why the work is just beginning.
If you believe in a Democratic Party that actually delivers for people, and independent media that's willing to challenge power instead of protecting it, **help me keep these conversations going.**

With urgency,
--Mike

The man who says he’s “nobody’s man” is calling in everybody he can.

---
| | | | 🚨 **JD Vance and President Trump’s son are in upstate New York today, the day before Election Day, to campaign for Anthony Constantino.** 🚨
---

Working people are working harder than ever before, and they're not getting their share of the profit. This campaign is all about changing that – and election analysts say we have a strong shot at winning in November. But I'll need your help to pull it off: My opponent is a Washington insider being propped up by the Republican establishment, and he's got virtually unlimited resources. That's not how our campaign works. We're a grassroots movement, and that means we rely on ordinary people chipping in a couple bucks. = If you'd like to receive exclusive updates from my team, you can text "OHIO" to 64054. body:
The work we’re doing to turn out voters is critically important.
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=4107%2E21716%2EbTtvYC)
**We’ve got one day left until Election Day** , and my team and I worked all through the weekend to get out the vote. And we’re not stopping until the polls are closed!
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261102-1.ZghbnO&refcode=em20261102-4107&t=2&akid=4107%2E21716%2EbTtvYC)
On Friday, we were out on the trail in Kent County with **Ramona Bracy** , candidate for Kent County Recorder of Deeds, **Annie Norman** , candidate for Delaware’s 34th District, and **Josh Pennington** , who’s running in the 33rd District.
[](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1184?c0=mcb-em-20261102-1.ZghbnO&refcode=em20261102-4107&t=3&akid=4107%2E21716%2EbTtvYC)
I also had the chance to join the **Interdenominational Ministers Action Council of Delaware** for Souls to the Polls and a Prayer Service for Peace in Wilmington.

Friend,

A lot of people have already stepped back.

_And I don’t blame them._ This fight has taken countless hours of hard work and dedication towards the future of our district and our nation.

But the fight isn’t over yet.

**This is our FINAL push before the Midterms, and I want to know that I gave this campaign my all.** I’m not asking for a miracle, and I’m not asking for a crowd of hundreds. I’m asking for the people who have continuously stood with me.

subject: How we’re getting ready for tomorrow
body:
[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1006&refcode=20261102_PreEday_T1&akid=301%2E344797%2El5YMIU ]COURIER Newsroom

Peter,

For months, COURIER has been bringing you stories about the people and
issues at the center of the 2026 midterms.

From candidate forums to conversations with everyday voters, from deep
dives on the Epstein scandal to reporting on Trump’s attempts to subvert
free and fair elections, COURIER reporters have been providing
independent, fact-based news and analysis and making sure it gets in front
of people on the platforms they use every day.

Now, with just hours to go until Election Day, we’re getting ready to
cover even more ground.

Starting before polls open tomorrow and going long after they close,
COURIER reporters will be on the ground in states including Texas,
Michigan, Wisconsin, Pennsylvania, Iowa, Nebraska, North Carolina,
Georgia, Alaska, Arizona, Nevada and more to cover breaking developments
in key races.

They’ll be reporting out the facts in the face of any disinformation
campaigns or conspiracy theories that might start spreading.

And well after all the votes are counted and the campaigns leave the
field, COURIER will still be here, making sure factual information reaches
communities on the issues that matter — and that right-wing billionaires
don’t have a monopoly on the public conversation.

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1003&refcode=20261102_PreEday_T1&akid=301%2E344797%2El5YMIU ]This work is what we were built for, Peter — but we can’t do
it without you. If you’re in a position to do so, please make one final
pre-Election Day contribution to power COURIER’s reporting on the ground:

[ https://act.couriernewsroom.com/go/398?t=1004&refcode=20261102_PreEday_T1&akid=301%2E344797%2El5YMIU ]Contribute

Thank you for making our reporting possible,

— The COURIER Team

across our social media channels for special Election Day coverage and
breaking news.

subject: It’s my favorite part, even after all these years
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Friends of Mark Warner
body:
I have one last ask for this grassroots team before Election Day

|
---

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142777467/657999950/-1193941463?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_GOTVFund4_261102_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYjFjYjlmNC0wYmQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VQhvy0vYL-O-kt2M6tGRrom0a4XSMgOkbPu43S_fz6k=) Derek, I’m about to get on stage in Alexandria for my final rally before Election Day.

I’ll admit I’m getting a little nostalgic. I’ve been in public service for a long time. And after all these years, my favorite part is still getting out there and talking to Virginians about the issues that matter most to them. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142777468/657999951/-1193941463?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_GOTVFund4_261102_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYjFjYjlmNC0wYmQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VQhvy0vYL-O-kt2M6tGRrom0a4XSMgOkbPu43S_fz6k=) Over the course of this campaign, I’ve talked to thousands of you who are frustrated with the chaos and corruption coming out of Washington – and you’re ready to elect leaders who will fight for you and your family.

You want to send folks to Washington who will fight to bring down costs, expand access to health care, and make it easier to buy a home and start a family.

_Tomorrow is Election Day, and we have the chance to turn our frustration and hope into action. We’ve got to hold this Senate seat for Democrats – and win Virginia’s battleground House races._

You’ve been an important part of this campaign – stepping up at critical moments repeatedly. And now, with just a few hours left until Election Day, I’m humbly asking you to step up one more time and fuel our campaign’s Get out the Vote operation tomorrow.

[_**Derek, will you chip in to our campaign’s Emergency GOTV Fund before midnight?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142777469/657999952/1233520376?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_GOTVFund4_261102_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYjFjYjlmNC0wYmQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VQhvy0vYL-O-kt2M6tGRrom0a4XSMgOkbPu43S_fz6k=)

Whether you can give tonight or not, please know that I am grateful to have you in this fight with me.

Let’s go win this thing,

Mark Warner **[CONTRIBUTE](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142777470/657999953/1233520376?refcode=MW_ATA_EM_FR_GOTVFund4_261102_T1_2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDAvMS84ODY1NCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJmYjFjYjlmNC0wYmQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=VQhvy0vYL-O-kt2M6tGRrom0a4XSMgOkbPu43S_fz6k=)**

[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261102-61962&t=1001&akid=61962%2E1407376%2Ea5xVha ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20261102-61962&t=1002&akid=61962%2E1407376%2Ea5xVha ]Demand Justice PAC

Tomorrow is
Election Day. Before you head to the polls, you need to see this.

Demand Justice just released a new report exposing Trump’s
election-denying judges. They sit in districts covering 53 of the 60 most
competitive races on the ballot.

Under oath, every one of these loyalist judges was asked a simple
question: Did Joe Biden win the 2020 election? All refused to answer
truthfully.

→ 29 battleground races have one of these judges on the district court.
→ 38 races could face one of these judges on appeal if Trump challenges
the results.

Trump’s DOJ has already sued to block certification of Alaska’s Senate
race if Republican Senator Dan Sullivan loses. Trump is laying the
groundwork to interfere in the midterm results, and he’s counting on the
courts to rubber-stamp his abuse of power.

Every one of these judges got there the same way: a Senate vote.

That’s what’s at stake tomorrow. The senators voters elect will decide who
gets a lifetime seat on the federal bench. Those judges will rule on our
voting rights, our reproductive freedom, our health care, and whether
future election results stand.

Voters deserve to know that their Senate vote is also a vote on the
courts. We have one day left to get that message out.

body:
I would rather be at a county fair shaking hands, but tomorrow Wisconsin votes.
| | | | [](https://link.victory.glenngrothman.)
---
| | Friend,
I’ve always believed you earn someone’s vote by showing up at their door. But Election Day is tomorrow, and I can’t knock on every door myself.
**[Tonight’s my last chance to ask. Will you help my team reach the voters I can’t get to before polls close?](https://link.victory.glenngrothman.)**
As your congressman, I’ve kept it simple. Here’s what I’ve fought for:
✅ **_Putting AMERICAN workers first_**
✅ **_Lower taxes, so you keep more of what you earn_**
✅ **_A border that’s actually enforced_**
✅ _**Cutting waste and fraud in Washington**_
In Wisconsin, we work hard and take care of our own. We don’t wait on Washington to do it for us.
**But the extreme Left wants bigger government, endless spending, and more people living off Washington instead of earning a paycheck. That’s not who we are.**
**[If you’ve already given, thank you. If you can give once more, it’ll keep our team knocking doors and making calls through the end of Election Day.](https://link.victory.glenngrothman.)**

### Forwardists on the Ballot!
Tomorrow is the 5th Election Day since the Pennsylvania Forward Party was formed in 2022 and the stakes couldn't be higher. We provide a base of support for candidates and office holders who don't fit into the two-party election system. We're also advocates for completely reforming that system. The offices that can make those reforms are up for election tomorrow and we'll be watching the results very closely. **State Races** This year we've endorsed 4 candidates for the PA State House. We're again thrilled to be working with sitting Republican Representative Valerie Gaydos. We've endorsed 2 Democrats running for seats in deep red parts of the state, Shannon Jackson and Ron Ruman. We also could not be happier to be working with Forward Independent, Chris Gambino, who has done a great job highlighting the challenges currently facing Independent and 3rd party candidates. **Federal Races** For the first time, we're weighing in on 2 Federal Races. Dennis Mahoney is an Independent in a head to head race for an otherwise uncontested open seat in the Philadelphia area. In a major first, we were also happy to announce last week that sitting Republican congressman Brian Fitzpatrick was endorsed by the Forward Party. Rep Fitzpatrick is one of the strongest advocates in the country for bipartisan coalition building and will be a huge help to the National Forward Party's efforts to have an impact in Washington. **Local Public Service** We also can't forget the 5 Forward Judges and Inspectors of Elections. They do a tremendous service to their communities by filling these roles that too often go unfilled. **For those running for office, supporting a campaign, working the polls, or making time to vote, we hope everyone has a great election day tomorrow!**
---
## 2026 Candidates!
Helping promising candidates get elected is what will turn ideas into action! The best way you can help us right now is to support these candidates. You'll be glad you did.

clean_body: We're counting on you. | | | Forwardists on the Ballot! Tomorrow is the 5th Election Day since the Pennsylvania Forward Party was formed in 2022 and the stakes couldn't be higher. We provide a base of support for candidates and office holders who don't fit into the two-party election system. We're also advocates for completely reforming that system. The offices that can make those reforms are up for election tomorrow and we'll be watching the results very closely. State Races This year we've endorsed 4 candidates for the PA State House. We're again thrilled to be working with sitting Republican Representative Valerie Gaydos. We've endorsed 2 Democrats running for seats in deep red parts of the state, Shannon Jackson and Ron Ruman. We also could not be happier to be working with Forward Independent, Chris Gambino, who has done a great job highlighting the challenges currently facing Independent and 3rd party candidates. Federal Races For the first time, we're weighing in on 2 Federal Races. Dennis Mahoney is an Independent in a head to head race for an otherwise uncontested open seat in the Philadelphia area. In a major first, we were also happy to announce last week that sitting Republican congressman Brian Fitzpatrick was endorsed by the Forward Party. Rep Fitzpatrick is one of the strongest advocates in the country for bipartisan coalition building and will be a huge help to the National Forward Party's efforts to have an impact in Washington. Local Public Service We also can't forget the 5 Forward Judges and Inspectors of Elections. They do a tremendous service to their communities by filling these roles that too often go unfilled. For those running for office, supporting a campaign, working the polls, or making time to vote, we hope everyone has a great election day tomorrow! 2026 Candidates! Helping promising candidates get elected is what will turn ideas into action! The best way you can help us right now is to support these candidates. You'll be glad you did. | | Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick has represented PA's 1st district in Bucks County since 2016. He's been an independent voice for bipartisanship and being accountable to voters over parties. He's the Chair of the Bipartisan Problem Solvers Caucus and Forward congressional candidates from across the country will benefit from his experience. | | Chris Gambino (PhD, MPA) is running to represent State House District 143, in Bucks County, as a Forward Independent. This has been a daunting task – due to the many institutional barriers faced by independent challengers – but Chris has risen tirelessly to face those challenges. The PA Forward Party looks forward to supporting him in the lead up to November. Learn more about Chris and offer your help at gambinoforpa.com | | PA Representative Gaydos has been officially affiliated with the PA Forward Party since 2024 and was familiar to us even earlier. She has been a role model as a Republican in a purple district doing her best to represent her community (NW Allegheny County). Learn more about Valerie at | | Shannon Jackson has worked in Chambersburg since 1993 and been a Software Developer since 2001. He's running for PA State House district 89 which covers the townships of Greene, Guilford, and Hamilton. Shannon is laser-focused on the affordability crisis in his community. | | Dennis Mahoney is an independent running for Congress in PA's 3rd District. He's a political outsider who has spent his career helping communities recover from disasters. As you lie in bed tonight, the house quiet and the day finally still, think about this: **_tomorrow you might wake up in a country that no longer has the majority that protects the things you care about most._** All of it can slip away _not because_ the other side suddenly became more popular, _but because_ **enough good people like you decided, just this once, that voting wasn’t quite important enough.**
I know what you’re telling yourself. Trump’s already President. Why do I still have to show up? You’ve got a lot going on. Voting feels like one more thing. I get it. I hear it every day.
But the truth is simple and it is hard: **if we lose the House and the Senate, everything we have fought for since I walked back into that office can be stopped cold.**
The executive orders that secured the border, that cut the red tape, that put America first—those become nothing more than paper.
A single hostile committee, a single activist judge, a single speaker who hates everything we stand for, **and the progress stops.** The investigations start.
**The country you voted for in 2024 begins to unravel, not in some dramatic collapse, but in a thousand quiet votes you never cast.**
This is not just another midterm. This is the election that decides whether the America we reclaimed stays reclaimed or gets handed back, piece by piece, to the people who spent years trying to tear it down.
If we lose the majority, it will not be because patriots suddenly became Democrats. It will be because too many of us looked at the calendar, looked at the lines, looked at our own busy lives, and decided someone else would carry the load.

**There is no someone else.**
**There is only you.** ****

All of it can slip away not because the other side suddenly became more popular, but because enough good people like you decided, just this once, that voting wasn’t quite important enough. I know what you’re telling yourself. Trump’s already President. Why do I still have to show up? You’ve got a lot going on. Voting feels like one more thing. I get it. I hear it every day. But the truth is simple and it is hard: if we lose the House and the Senate, everything we have fought for since I walked back into that office can be stopped cold. The executive orders that secured the border, that cut the red tape, that put America first—those become nothing more than paper. A single hostile committee, a single activist judge, a single speaker who hates everything we stand for, and the progress stops. The investigations start. The country you voted for in 2024 begins to unravel, not in some dramatic collapse, but in a thousand quiet votes you never cast. This is not just another midterm. This is the election that decides whether the America we reclaimed stays reclaimed or gets handed back, piece by piece, to the people who spent years trying to tear it down. If we lose the majority, it will not be because patriots suddenly became Democrats. It will be because too many of us looked at the calendar, looked at the lines, looked at our own busy lives, and decided someone else would carry the load. There is no someone else. | | |
---
Friend, there's a lot of noise out there right now. We can’t be distracted.
Some people would love for the last days of this race to be about politicians. Who said what. Who's mad at whom. Screenshots and hot takes.
**I will not be distracted.** Every minute spent talking about politicians is a minute taken from the people this election is really about: working Michiganders.
— This election is about the dad I met who told me his kid is really good at baseball but can't play next year because he just can't afford it.
— This election is about everyone who's been told to wait for relief to “trickle down” while groceries, rent, and healthcare slip further out of reach.
— And it's about people far beyond our state. Because Michigan will decide control of the United States Senate. A Democratic Senate is how we put a check on Donald Trump's power. Mike Rogers, Trump's handpicked candidate, wants to be one more vote for the same billionaire agenda that's been fleecing Michigan for decades.

Please don’t get distracted by the political drama. I promise you I won’t.

Election Day is tomorrow. Several polls show us statistically tied with Mike Rogers. In 2024, the Senate race here came down to 20,217 votes.

**I’m told there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front of Michigan voters, but only if we have the cash to run them right now.**

Peter, Bobby Pulido here, and I'm going to be radically transparent with you: We have hours until polls open in South Texas. Our race is rated the #1 most flippable House seat in the entire state. But we don't have the resources we need to win. **[So I'm throwing a Hail Mary and respectfully asking you to donate $10 to my campaign.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142778442/658003259/1592407273?amount=10&refcode=email_110226_actives_hailmary&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMjA2OTAiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiZjI2ZDAzMzAtMGZkNy1mMTExLWJmNWItMDAwZDNhNTQ0NDJlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=jbyEYs3aGu7gfCXwp-OxAOy2Lc6J1CK8tYcgeH1SmFY=)** You may be thinking: what can my $10 even do this close to Election Day? _A lot._ We have organizers ready to knock on doors, ads ready to air, phone bankers ready to start their shift. If you can't afford a contribution today, I totally get that. But if you've been waiting for the right time, the time has officially arrived. Peter, Before the polls open tomorrow morning, I wanted to take a moment to extend my sincere gratitude to all of you for being a part of our campaign. We’ve accomplished so much, and none of it would have been possible without your support. Representing my neighbors in IL-17 has always been personal for me: I was born and raised in this district. I served the residents of our district as a meteorologist for years, helping people prepare for their days. Because my roots here are so deep, I’m intimately familiar with the problems that the residents of Northwest and Central Illinois are facing. And I’ll continue to work every day to address these issues and improve the lives of our constituents. **No matter what happens tomorrow, I am humbled and inspired by the hard work, time, and passion each one of you has brought to this effort to keep a trusted voice representing Illinois’ 17th District in Congress.** Because of you, we feel like we can overcome National Republicans trying to buy this seat, but we still need to finish strong. [**Will you make one final contribution to help us through the home stretch? Al-Abd Abu Beid prepares a meal of lentils from food rations distributed by the World Food Programme, one day after the UN agency announced it would reduce food aid in Gaza by around one-third. October 20, 2026. Screenshot from footage by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
GAZA CITY--Al-Abd Abu Beid set a box of food rations down on a pile of stones he uses as a makeshift table outside his ramshackle tent on the coastline west of Gaza City. The cardboard box displayed the blue logo of the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), along with a stamp showing it had been packed on July 11, 2026. Abu Beid sifted through the contents: a plastic bottle of sunflower oil, a bag of red split lentils, and eight cans of hummus or white beans.
"We have no income at all," Abu Beid told Drop Site News. "We depend heavily on the brown boxes from the World Food Programme."
"We were actually hoping they would improve the contents of these boxes, because they contain rice, lentils, and the same things over and over again," he continued. "Instead, we were shocked to hear that they're going to cut it off."
Abu Beid spoke to Drop Site on October 20--one day after the WFP [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/c8cca01a-fd14-40bb-a01a-fd8b354e75b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it was reducing food aid in Gaza by around one-third, cutting off access to half a million Palestinians from critical food assistance due to funding shortages. The cuts also reduce food rations by half--with families receiving only one food parcel a month instead of two--and a smaller bag of wheat flour. In addition, WFP cut the number of daily hot meals it provides from 250,000 to 150,000. Meanwhile, families living in the most hard-to-reach areas of Gaza, including near the yellow line of Israeli military control, will now receive a hot meal every other day instead of daily. The value of cash assistance provided to 75,000 families would also be reduced, the UN agency said.
"What is a family supposed to do? I have seven people in my family. How am I supposed to feed them? Even if the food was repetitive, just rice and lentils, I have no income, so I relied on it to cook for my children," Abu Beid said. "This is a humanitarian crime. People are being killed and slaughtered every day, and now you're cutting off their food too. This is catastrophic."
The WFP announcement came a little over a year after the "ceasefire" agreement that was supposed to bring an end to Israel's assault on Gaza and restore the delivery of food, fuel, medicine, and other life essentials to what experts say are the minimum required levels.
Instead, the Israeli military has continued its attacks, killing over 1,500 men, women and children while severely restricting the amount of aid allowed into Gaza in violation of the agreement. In October alone, Israel killed 143 Palestinians in direct attacks, according to the Health Ministry, including 23 children, and injured over 670.
The unrelenting Israeli assault prompted a UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry to [conclude](https://substack.com/redirect/e3e2cc14-d1f0-47b1-a5ce-abf95e07ee5b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) earlier this month that Israel is continuing to "commit genocidal acts even after the so-called ceasefire agreement, with the intent to destroy the Palestinian people, in whole or in part."
With the genocide now its fourth year, levels of hunger and malnutrition are once again growing. In the same announcement that it was heavily reducing food assistance to Gaza, the WFP said that an estimated 1.4 million Palestinians, or 67% of Gaza's population, are experiencing acute food insecurity at "crisis levels or worse." Some 200,000 people remain in "emergency conditions," where immediate food assistance is needed to prevent deaths from hunger.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/714f3908-e596-49ae-be81-8f649ff151f0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Video: Families in a tent encampment on the shoreline west of Gaza prepare meager meals with UN food rations and people gather in Al-Shati refugee camp to protest against UN aid cuts. October 20, 2026. Footage by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
"We depend on these parcels for everything: flour, rice, lentils, paste, chickpeas, and beans. Most of what we eat is beans, rice, and lentils. We use the flour to make bread on a metal griddle over a fire," Linda Abu Warda told Drop Site. She sat stirring a blackened pot filled with a rice stew as her husband, Fares, fed small pieces of wood into the fire beneath it--a thin metal box serving as a makeshift stove. "Now they're saying the aid has stopped, or that it's going to stop. We're already barely managing to get by with what little we have. Imagine what will happen if they cut it off completely. I have children, as you can see. They'll die of hunger."
She added, "We've already lived through famine. We've experienced it. We were hoping they'd increase the amount of aid we receive, not reduce it."
In mid-2025, Gaza was plunged into a full-blown famine, with Palestinians collapsing in the streets and men, women, and children dying from hunger and malnutrition on a daily basis. An Israeli starvation campaign that included a full blockade in March 2025 was followed by a privatized "aid distribution" system overseen by the U.S. and Israeli-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) that replaced the UN. With just four distribution sites across the entirety of the enclave, guarded by American mercenaries and located in areas occupied by Israeli soldiers, the GHF sites became death traps for starving Palestinians seeking food. More than 2,600 Palestinians were killed at or near GHF distribution sites or at the few UN convoys allowed inside.
"We hope they'll allow this aid to enter officially and legally, instead of forcing us to go back to Zikim like before, when people had to risk their lives just to bring home a bite of food for their children," Linda's husband, Fares, said, referring to one of the aid distribution sites in 2025 where hundreds of Palestinians were killed. "A man would go out and instead of coming home with a bag of flour, he'd come back in a body bag."
Food prices have soared as a result of food shortages and arbitrary closures of the crossings into Gaza by Israel. In mid-October, Israel suddenly halted all commercial shipments into Gaza. While commercial goods were eventually allowed back in after several days, the brief closure nevertheless sent prices shooting upward.
"The closure of the crossings is what's driving prices up," Linda Abu Warda said. "When we want to cook a meal, we can't even afford a single onion, it's expensive. Onions cost 30 or 40 shekels a kilo [about $9.5 to $12.75], so we've had to do without them...They used to cost four or five shekels [about $1.25 to $1.60]." She added, "People don't have the money to buy anything. They've raised the prices of sugar, food, cooking oil, and vegetables."

[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.Xhbm8MLJDJk__HcQrKioZpse3uHbIgMM5KuRfFLYx30?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=223224965)
Other humanitarian groups have also reduced aid distribution to Gaza. In May, World Central Kitchen (WCK), the biggest provider of hot meals in Gaza [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/61411de0-03ad-4333-81c9-729d20564a2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it was cutting its distribution in half, from around one million meals a day to 500,000. WCK said the decision was "driven entirely by financial pressure," citing rising food prices as a result of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
"The famine has not ended in Gaza," Ahmed Abu Qamar, a writer and economic affairs researcher in Gaza City, told Drop Site. "Perhaps its severity has eased slightly. When we look back at last summer, the famine was extremely severe. Since the ceasefire agreement last October, Israel has been pursuing a policy of engineered starvation. In other words, it may allow people the bare minimum to eat each day, or even less than that, but it does not provide them with what they need to achieve food security and sustain their lives."
## "We're extremely, extremely afraid of winter"
Mohammed Zayed, who lives in the same tent encampment on the sandy shoreline west of Gaza City, used rudimentary tools to try and erect a wall of tarp and blankets around his tent. Wind billowed through the pieces of cloth and tarp hanging from thin metal poles and pieces of wood hammered into the ground and connected by lengths of wire and rope.
"Here on the beach, we suffer terribly in both summer and winter. And now, as winter approaches, we're trying to prepare because living here is extremely difficult," Zayed told Drop Site on October 14. "These tents can't withstand that because they're worn out and falling apart. They're three years old now. "
"We're extremely, extremely afraid of winter," he continued. "We try to stitch up tarps and secure the metal poles properly. We're trying to reduce the impact of the wind, because otherwise it'll blow everything away. It's extremely difficult for me and for everyone here. People's tents are worn out, falling apart, collapsing around them. Nobody has the means to replace a tent or change the tarps to prepare for winter."
"All of this is just an illusion," he said, pointing to the tarps. "All of this will be blown away."
Zayed's tent is part of a vast tent encampment on the northern Gaza coastline. Nearly the entirety of Gaza's population has been forced to displace by Israel's assault, with many families displaced multiple times. The majority of Palestinians in Gaza are now living crammed in tent encampments. Dilapidated tents now occupy every open space, with streets, squares, stadiums, courtyards, and fields filled with tent encampments.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/b5f3ec03-822e-4bfe-865f-a868f40e3f68?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
###### Video: Families in a tent encampment west of Gaza City try to prepare their tents for winter with few supplies. In the Jabaliya refugee camp,Mohammed Al-Shabrawi tries to cover up the broken walls of his badly damaged home. October 14, 2026. Footage by Abdel Qader Sabbah.
The lack of proper shelter has been disastrous and even fatal, particularly in winter with torrential rains, high winds, flooding, and cold temperatures. Over the past three winters, Palestinians--mostly infants--[have died](https://substack.com/redirect/77ebacd5-1b9c-45d0-82a8-b9260994542a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of hypothermia in Gaza as a result of exposure, including [11 children](https://substack.com/redirect/2432fe80-dc62-48e8-984b-ea38e1e5eb9c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last winter alone.
"The humanitarian situation remains catastrophic with the near totality of the population still surviving in deteriorated tents and makeshift shelters, bracing for a fourth winter without adequate protection from the cold, wind, rain and flooding risks," the UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs noted in its latest situation [report](https://substack.com/redirect/aa7121b0-c647-42f2-ba95-997d136889b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week.
Since the ceasefire, Israel has continued to push inward, expanding the yellow line that demarcates its area of control, driving Palestinians further west onto just 30% of the enclave. Israel has also blocked the entry of reconstruction materials, mobile homes, and heavily restricted the number of tents and shelter materials allowed into Gaza in violation of the agreement.
"Those displaced before the announcement of a ceasefire have little to no prospect of return to the areas they fled, most of which are inaccessible because they fall beyond the so-called yellow line. And they continue to be displaced again and again," said Ajith Sunghay, the head of UN Human Rights in the occupied territories, in a [statement](https://substack.com/redirect/c46701d5-357b-4fc1-b695-93c30484360e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) last week. "There must be an end to this suffering. This is the fourth year of displacement for most Palestinians in Gaza, the fourth winter in tents too flimsy to withstand the rain, and they are still under fire through it all."
Before the genocide, Khalda Ghattas lived in an apartment in the Tuffah neighborhood of Gaza City. "I used to live in an apartment building protected by concrete, with warmth, mattresses, furniture sets, and carpets. What a beautiful home it was," she told Drop Site. Now, she lives in a flimsy tent on the sand. "Then we were displaced to the port. The cold is already eating us alive. We can't keep the wind out."
She continued, "You put up a tarp, another one falls down. You put up a blanket, it falls too. And the biggest problem is that I can't afford to buy good, sturdy tarps. And even if I bought one, I'd need metal poles to hold it up. We have nothing." Due to the severe shortages, Ghattas said a tarp can cost between 180 and 200 shekels (around $57 to $64). "Where am I supposed to get that money? I simply can't afford it," she said. "We're still in autumn, but we already can't withstand the wind. And I have children, as you can see. I have so many children, including babies. This little girl has asthma, and I have children with respiratory diseases. I suffer from rheumatism, and my husband has a heart condition."
Nasser Al-Shanbari, who was displaced from Beit Hanoun in northern Gaza, now runs a small street stall in Gaza City selling tarps, mattresses, sheets and other shelter items.
"Tarps have become scarcer this season, prices have gone up, and people have very little money," Al-Shanbari told Drop Site. "Some of the tarps we have aren't even any good. The ones we get these days don't last more than two or three months in the wind and rain before they fall apart. Prices have risen, and deliveries have also decreased recently. We buy them from people and from traders, but the quantities available are very limited."
He continued, "A plank that used to cost 10 shekels now costs 150 shekels. A small measure of nails that used to cost 10 shekels now costs 50. All of this is expensive. To fix up a shelter with wood, nails, and tarps, it would cost at least around 5,000 shekels [about $1,600]."

"We're trying to seal off the openings with tarps and strips of fabric. Even the wall behind me is made of tarp, and everything you see here is covered with tarps. It's extremely difficult for us to buy them because they're so expensive," Al-Shabrawi told Drop Site.
"We're living in a bombed out house... We're struggling to cover the walls and roof. When it rains tomorrow, the entire roof will leak. There isn't a single part of it that doesn't leak and let water pour down on us."

October 20, 2026. Screenshot from footage by Abdel Qader Sabbah. GAZA CITY--Al-Abd Abu Beid set a box of food rations down on a pile of stones he uses as a makeshift table outside his ramshackle tent on the coastline west of Gaza City. The cardboard box displayed the blue logo of the United Nations World Food Programme (WFP), along with a stamp showing it had been packed on July 11, 2026. Abu Beid sifted through the contents: a plastic bottle of sunflower oil, a bag of red split lentils, and eight cans of hummus or white beans. "We have no income at all," Abu Beid told Drop Site News. "We depend heavily on the brown boxes from the World Food Programme." "We were actually hoping they would improve the contents of these boxes, because they contain rice, lentils, and the same things over and over again," he continued. "Instead, we were shocked to hear that they're going to cut it off." Abu Beid spoke to Drop Site on October 20--one day after the WFP it was reducing food aid in Gaza by around one-third, cutting off access to half a million Palestinians from critical food assistance due to funding shortages. The cuts also reduce food rations by half--with families receiving only one food parcel a month instead of two--and a smaller bag of wheat flour. In addition, WFP cut the number of daily hot meals it provides from 250,000 to 150,000. Meanwhile, families living in the most hard-to-reach areas of Gaza, including near the yellow line of Israeli military control, will now receive a hot meal every other day instead of daily. The value of cash assistance provided to 75,000 families would also be reduced, the UN agency said. "What is a family supposed to do? I have seven people in my family. How am I supposed to feed them? Even if the food was repetitive, just rice and lentils, I have no income, so I relied on it to cook for my children," Abu Beid said. "This is a humanitarian crime. People are being killed and slaughtered every day, and now you're cutting off their food too. This is catastrophic." The WFP announcement came a little over a year after the "ceasefire" agreement that was supposed to bring an end to Israel's assault on Gaza and restore the delivery of food, fuel, medicine, and other life essentials to what experts say are the minimum required levels. Instead, the Israeli military has continued its attacks, killing over 1,500 men, women and children while severely restricting the amount of aid allowed into Gaza in violation of the agreement. In October alone, Israel killed 143 Palestinians in direct attacks, according to the Health Ministry, including 23 children, and injured over 670. The unrelenting Israeli assault prompted a UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry to earlier this month that Israel is continuing to "commit genocidal acts even after the so-called ceasefire agreement, with the intent to destroy the Palestinian people, in whole or in part." With the genocide now its fourth year, levels of hunger and malnutrition are once again growing. In the same announcement that it was heavily reducing food assistance to Gaza, the WFP said that an estimated 1.4 million Palestinians, or 67% of Gaza's population, are experiencing acute food insecurity at "crisis levels or worse." An Israeli starvation campaign that included a full blockade in March 2025 was followed by a privatized "aid distribution" system overseen by the U.S. and Israeli-backed Gaza Humanitarian Foundation (GHF) that replaced the UN. With just four distribution sites across the entirety of the enclave, guarded by American mercenaries and located in areas occupied by Israeli soldiers, the GHF sites became death traps for starving Palestinians seeking food. More than 2,600 Palestinians were killed at or near GHF distribution sites or at the few UN convoys allowed inside. "We hope they'll allow this aid to enter officially and legally, instead of forcing us to go back to Zikim like before, when people had to risk their lives just to bring home a bite of food for their children," Linda's husband, Fares, said, referring to one of the aid distribution sites in 2025 where hundreds of Palestinians were killed. "A man would go out and instead of coming home with a bag of flour, he'd come back in a body bag." Food prices have soared as a result of food shortages and arbitrary closures of the crossings into Gaza by Israel. In mid-October, Israel suddenly halted all commercial shipments into Gaza. While commercial goods were eventually allowed back in after several days, the brief closure nevertheless sent prices shooting upward. "The closure of the crossings is what's driving prices up," Linda Abu Warda said. "When we want to cook a meal, we can't even afford a single onion, it's expensive. Onions cost 30 or 40 shekels a kilo [about $9.5 to $12.75], so we've had to do without them...They used to cost four or five shekels [about $1.25 to $1.60]." She added, "People don't have the money to buy anything. They've raised the prices of sugar, food, cooking oil, and vegetables." Drop Site News is reader-supported. In May, World Central Kitchen (WCK), the biggest provider of hot meals in Gaza it was cutting its distribution in half, from around one million meals a day to 500,000. WCK said the decision was "driven entirely by financial pressure," citing rising food prices as a result of the U.S.-Israeli war with Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. "The famine has not ended in Gaza," Ahmed Abu Qamar, a writer and economic affairs researcher in Gaza City, told Drop Site. "Perhaps its severity has eased slightly. When we look back at last summer, the famine was extremely severe. Since the ceasefire agreement last October, Israel has been pursuing a policy of engineered starvation. Dilapidated tents now occupy every open space, with streets, squares, stadiums, courtyards, and fields filled with tent encampments. I wanted you to hear this from me first.| | | | Peter, I wanted you to hear this from me first. **A brand-new poll shows me leading Greg Abbott, 49% to 46%.**
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142779427/658006770/1593610140?amount=25&refcode=261102_gina_yougov&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkNDg0MjVkOS0xMWQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=wm_3sF1iy0Ri15r45H_IHrsq0FROok5aJlJ3nda_iFk=)
---
Here’s why that number matters so much. In early October, we had cut Abbott’s lead to just 1.3 points. Then the polls started moving back his way. His lead in the polling average grew, and a lot of insiders decided this race was slipping away from us. **_This poll was taken in the middle of early voting, and it shows us ahead._** What makes it remarkable is this: Greg Abbott has now spent $181 million in this race, five times what our campaign has spent. In the last month alone, he spent $35 million. **That’s as much as we’ve spent since the day we launched.**
---
_**Spending: TX-GOV**_ 🔴 Abbott, total: $181 million🔴 Abbott, last 30 days: $35 million 🔵 Our entire campaign: $35 million
---
He has outspent us 5 to 1. **But we’re outworking him, and grassroots supporters are the reason why.** I’m not going to pretend one poll settles anything. Three points is within the margin of error, and Abbott isn’t going to stop spending now. The voters who decide this race are about to be buried in his ads. **We have to make sure they hear from us too.** **That’s why my team set a goal to raise $3 million this week, which would bring us to $10 million raised in October.** As of writing this, we’re 87% of the way there. Supporters like you helped get us this far, and I need you with me for the final stretch. clean_body: I wanted you to hear this from me first.| | | | Peter, I wanted you to hear this from me first. A brand-new poll shows me leading Greg Abbott, 49% to 46%. = Here’s why that number matters so much. In early October, we had cut Abbott’s lead to just 1.3 points. Then the polls started moving back his way. His lead in the polling average grew, and a lot of insiders decided this race was slipping away from us. This poll was taken in the middle of early voting, and it shows us ahead. What makes it remarkable is this: Greg Abbott has now spent $181 million in this race, five times what our campaign has spent. In the last month alone, he spent $35 million. That’s as much as we’ve spent since the day we launched. Spending: TX-GOV 🔴 Abbott, total: $181 million🔴 Abbott, last 30 days: $35 million 🔵 Our entire campaign: $35 million He has outspent us 5 to 1. But we’re outworking him, and grassroots supporters are the reason why. I’m not going to pretend one poll settles anything. Three points is within the margin of error, and Abbott isn’t going to stop spending now. The voters who decide this race are about to be buried in his ads. We have to make sure they hear from us too. That’s why my team set a goal to raise $3 million this week, which would bring us to $10 million raised in October. As of writing this, we’re 87% of the way there. Supporters like you helped get us this far, and I need you with me for the final stretch. = = | | | We closed a 7-point gap once already. Derek, the 2026 midterm elections are some of the most consequential in our lifetimes, and Election Day is _tomorrow_ , Tuesday, November 3. If you haven’t voted yet, please make a plan to cast your ballot tomorrow. Here in Virginia, polls will be open from 6 AM — 7 PM. **[No matter where you are, click here to confirm your polling location and find out everything you need to know about voting in your state.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/142779475/658006936/-1612268846?refcode=261102em_tk_electionday-tomorrow&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDQvMS84ODkyNCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlZmJlOGVmMy0xMWQ3LWYxMTEtYmY1Yi0wMDBkM2E1NDQ0MmUiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=IJrtTvMdIw6J4DeOCI5nJasGf2yYWZLwOPICWZ0tyf8=&emci=e4e083bf-0bd7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&emdi=efbe8ef3-11d7-f111-bf5b-000d3a54442e&ceid=1801409)** Your vote is your voice — and it has never been more important for all of us to speak out loudly and clearly. The Trump-Vance agenda has been made clear over the past 21 months: Rip healthcare away from millions of Americans with massive cuts to Medicaid. Cut SNAP benefits that hungry kids rely on. Start a foolish and illegal war in the Middle East that puts American service members in danger and sends oil prices skyrocketing. And who can forget: hand out $4.5 trillion in tax cuts to billionaires and massive corporations, and blow up the deficit — all at the expense of the American people. Americans cannot afford another two years of a GOP Congress, and tomorrow we have a chance to not just send a message, but to make a real change. I encourage you to get out and vote for strong Democrats up and down the ticket who will put people over politics and help get our country back on track. And if you’ve already voted, please forward this email to any friends and family who may need a reminder. Thank you for being a voter! —Tim Kaine P.S. body:
If you’ve ever believed in our mission, I need you with us one more time before tomorrow.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20261102-2&t=1&akid=4227%2E587540%2EDhHruW)
Peter,
Before Election Day is officially here, I want to take a second to be real with you.
When we started Leaders We Deserve, the mission was simple: give people something real to believe in. Not leaders who send strongly worded letters or tweet empty gestures, but leaders who will actually stand up to Trump and deliver for the people.
We set out to build a genuine progressive movement for a generation that’s been told fighting for their future is too hard and too radical.
**Now, in the biggest year in our organization’s history, we’re on the cusp of making it real.** Bold young progressives are on ballots across the country, ready to flip red seats blue, shatter far-right supermajorities, expand our power in Congress, energize our party, and prove that people-powered politics is the way to win.
_None of this was a sure thing when we started._
Someone had to take a leap and believe in this vision first — and you did. Every time you read one of these emails, chipped in a few dollars when you could, or showed up for one of our candidates, you made this all possible.
I’ve spent this last month on the road rallying alongside our candidates, and what I keep seeing everywhere I go is **hope**. I know, I know, it sounds cliché, but I don’t use that word lightly.
People who are fed up with the chaos in this country are showing up because they finally have a reason to believe the future could actually be better. That they could actually afford to buy a home, see a doctor without going broke, earn a liveable wage, and build a meaningful life, not just struggle to survive.
**The young leaders we’re backing are the ones giving them that hope — and that’s what makes them worth believing and investing in.**
_You_ helped build that energy, Peter. _You_ helped ignite that movement. And when polls open tomorrow and young progressives are in the position to flip statehouse chambers and take back the House and Senate, _it will be because of you._
So here’s my final ask before tomorrow: **If you’ve ever believed in what we’re building at Leaders We Deserve, I need you with us one more time.**
Whatever you can give right now will help our candidates finish what they started and elect the next generation of fearless, people-powered, young leaders we deserve. **[Will you pitch in $5?](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20261102_2_closing.AFQZxV&refcode=em20261102-4227&amount=5&t=2&akid=4227%2E587540%2EDhHruW)**

Thank you for your support, Peter.
Let’s finish this strong,
David Hogg

subject: Tomorrow is EVERYTHING. Let's WIN this!
body:
Peter, we could lose because of the people who DON'T vote.

| | | | | | |
#### [DrewForNevada.com](https://us.list-manage.com/2TZ05MdMZxy?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | [](https://us.list-manage.com/tR78FkZ1k9a?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)

---](https://us.list-manage.com/ymsy3CSBAXl?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| | | | | |
Peter -
**Tomorrow is Election Day. And after nearly two years of campaigning, it all comes down to this.**
The races across Nevada are incredibly close. Some could be decided by just a handful of votes.
But here's what worries me most: **This election could be decided by the people who DON'T vote.**
Think about that. We could lose races that were absolutely winnable simply because people didn't take the time to cast their ballots.
**When we don't vote, we only cheat ourselves. We cannot let that happen tomorrow.**
So, I'm asking you for three final things:
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/GuNUmDLqMOe?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| |
**PLEASE, PLEASE VOTE TOMORROW**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

If you've already voted, THANK YOU! But if you haven't, tomorrow is your last chance.
Polls are open from **7 AM to 7 PM on Tuesday, November 3.**[**Click here to find a polling station near you.**](https://us.list-manage.com/u9eQpaIKOZZ?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
**Need a ride to the polls? Need someone to help you return your completed mail ballot? LET US KNOW!**
Our team will make sure nothing stands between you and your vote.
Don't forget to check with your friends, family, neighbors, and coworkers, too. A simple reminder could make all the difference.
---
| [Get Help Voting](mailto:info@drewfornevada.com?subject=Get%20Help%20Voting!&body=)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/12i6QqdJICU?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| |
**HELP US WITH THE FINAL PUSH**
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

Even with Election Day just hours away, my team and I are still hard at work contacting voters, sending text messages, and doing everything we can to get people to the polls.
**And we still need your help funding these final outreach efforts.**
If you can spare $10 or $15 today, it would mean so much. Every dollar will help us continue reaching voters in these final critical hours.
---
| [Help Us Finish Strong!](https://us.list-manage.com/BcUrRZ7Tuqw?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/17VZbto7q5p?e=817ed65ac7&c2id=d5ba536a36ebcb17f684b24f2e31274d)
| |
**KNOW HOW MUCH YOUR SUPPORT HAS MEANT TO US**
---
| |

Tomorrow is the culmination of nearly two years of hard work, thousands of miles traveled across Nevada, countless conversations with voters, and the dedication of so many incredible people.
To every donor who believed in this campaign, every volunteer who wrote postcards, knocked on doors, made calls, or hosted an event, and every supporter who shared our message or encouraged a friend to vote: **THANK YOU.**
I could not be more grateful.
We've given this campaign everything we've got because we believe Nevada deserves a State Treasurer who will fight for taxpayers, demand accountability, and protect your hard-earned money.
Now, after two years, it all comes down to what happens tomorrow.
**Let's make every mile, every conversation, every dollar, and every hour of hard work count.**
**GET OUT AND VOTE.**
**GET YOUR FRIENDS AND FAMILY TO VOTE.**
**LET'S WIN TOMORROW!**

Peter,

Tomorrow is Election Day.

I want to take a moment to tell you what this campaign has meant to me.

I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve built together, and none of this would have been possible without you.

I’m the son of Mexican immigrants who grew up sharing a bunk bed in our living room -- working at the swap meet on weekends and watching my dad keep our family auto shop running here in Bakersfield. I never imagined that one day I’d be on the cusp of flipping a seat in Congress, and you’re the reason we are here.

But this race has always been about much more than me or my opponent.

Tomorrow, the Valley decides whether we send a congressman back to Washington who promised not to cut Medicaid and did it anyway, or someone who grew up relying on it and knows exactly what those cuts mean.

We will decide whether this seat is controlled by corporate PACs, or finally answers to the farmworkers, nurses, teachers, and small business owners who actually live here.

And we will decide whether working families will be forced to keep waiting for their turn, or finally have someone in Congress who will fight to bring down the cost of housing, healthcare, and groceries.

**This is one of the most important toss-up races in the country, and what the Central Valley decides tomorrow will be felt by working families across the country -- which is why I’m asking for your help one last time:**

clean_body: | = Peter, Tomorrow is Election Day. I want to take a moment to tell you what this campaign has meant to me. I’m incredibly proud of what we’ve built together, and none of this would have been possible without you. I’m the son of Mexican immigrants who grew up sharing a bunk bed in our living room -- working at the swap meet on weekends and watching my dad keep our family auto shop running here in Bakersfield. I never imagined that one day I’d be on the cusp of flipping a seat in Congress, and you’re the reason we are here. But this race has always been about much more than me or my opponent. Tomorrow, the Valley decides whether we send a congressman back to Washington who promised not to cut Medicaid and did it anyway, or someone who grew up relying on it and knows exactly what those cuts mean. We will decide whether this seat is controlled by corporate PACs, or finally answers to the farmworkers, nurses, teachers, and small business owners who actually live here. And we will decide whether working families will be forced to keep waiting for their turn, or finally have someone in Congress who will fight to bring down the cost of housing, healthcare, and groceries. This is one of the most important toss-up races in the country, and what the Central Valley decides tomorrow will be felt by working families across the country -- which is why I’m asking for your help one last time: = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | = | | = | = | | = | = Thank you for believing in me, and for believing in the Central Valley. Team,

Tomorrow is Election Day — the last day to cast a ballot in this race. Before it arrives, I want to share a few final thoughts with you.

No matter what happens, I am so proud of the campaign we built together — and more than anything,**I want to say thank you.** I would not be here without you. A daughter of Hmong refugees, raised as the oldest of 16 kids in South Sacramento, running a competitive campaign for Congress. That's not something I could ever have imagined. You made it possible.

But I also want to be clear about what tomorrow is really about, because this was never just a contest between two names on a ballot.

It’s a choice.

Between 21 years of establishment politics that left working families behind -- and a new generation ready to meet this moment with urgency.

Between a Washington that answers to corporate donors and AIPAC-aligned money -- and a representative who answers only to you.

Between playing it safe while the cost of living crushes people -- and actually fighting to make housing and healthcare work for working families again.

This is much bigger than just CA-07. It’s about the kind of future we’re willing to fight for and who we trust to fight for it.

Which is why I have to ask you one last time.

**My team tells me there's still time to put our final get-out-the-vote ads in front of voters tomorrow — but only if we have the resources to run them right now. In a race this close, those ads could be the difference.**
